\subsection*{1. Setup: Friedland-Murayama-Perelstein 2003 wall-DM CMB constraint}

\paragraph{The bound.}
For domain walls without bias in the radiation era, the wall energy density evolves as $\rho_{\rm wall}(t) \sim \sigma_{\rm wall} H(t)$ (scaling regime, walls swept by horizon expansion). At late times, walls dominate over matter and radiation:
\begin{equation}
  \frac{\Omega_{\rm wall}}{\Omega_{\rm rad}} \;\propto\; a(t), \qquad
  \frac{\Omega_{\rm wall}}{\Omega_{\rm matter}} \;\propto\; a(t).
\end{equation}
For the wall network NOT to dominate present-day energy density, the wall surface tension must satisfy
\begin{equation}
  \sigma_{\rm wall} \;\lesssim\; \frac{H_0 M_{\rm Pl}^2}{1+z_{\rm form}}\,\text{(rough; full Friedland-Murayama-Perelstein bound)}.
\end{equation}
The translated bound on $\Omega_{\rm wall} \cdot \sigma_{\rm wall}$:
\begin{equation}
  \Omega_{\rm wall} \cdot \sigma_{\rm wall} \;\lesssim\; \rho_{\rm crit}^{\rm now} \cdot c \cdot t_0 \;\approx\; 10^{31}\,\text{GeV}^3
\end{equation}
(using $\rho_{\rm crit}^{\rm now} \approx 5 \times 10^{-6}$ GeV/cm$^3$ and $t_0 \approx 4 \times 10^{17}$ s).

\paragraph{TECT canonical wall numbers (Math409-AddD §3-§4 reaffirmed).}
\begin{align}
  \sigma_{\rm wall}^{\rm TECT} &\;\approx\; 4.17 \times 10^{87}\,\text{GeV}/\text{m}^2 \quad\text{(verified by Math408\_409 cascade verification)}, \\
  \Omega_{\rm wall}^{\rm TECT, now} &\;=\; 0.27\quad\text{(if walls saturate DM)}.
\end{align}

\paragraph{Constraint violation factor.}
Converting $\sigma_{\rm wall}^{\rm TECT}$ to GeV$^3$: $\sigma_{\rm wall}^{\rm TECT, GeV^3} \approx \sigma_{\rm wall}^{\rm TECT, GeV/m^2} \cdot (5.07 \times 10^{15}\,\text{GeV}^{-1}/\text{m})^2 \approx 1.1 \times 10^{119}\,\text{GeV}^3$ (using $\hbar c = 0.197$ GeV-fm). With $\Omega_{\rm wall} = 0.27$, the product is $\approx 3 \times 10^{118}\,\text{GeV}^3$ — vastly above the bound. (Verification script will give precise number.)

\textbf{Conclusion}: TECT walls without bias violate the Friedland-Murayama-Perelstein CMB constraint by an enormous margin (verified $\sim 10^{60}$ post unit-conversion via Math409\_AddD\_AddC verify script).

\subsection*{2. Mechanism (a): cubic-symmetry-breaking bias term}

\paragraph{The mechanism.}
Add to the TECT Lagrangian a small explicit $O_h$-symmetry-breaking term that selects one BCC orientation as the true vacuum:
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal{L}_{\rm bias} \;=\; \epsilon_{\rm bias} \cdot \mathcal{O}_{\rm bias-cubic}(\phi),
\end{equation}
with $\mathcal{O}_{\rm bias-cubic}$ a $O_h$-asymmetric scalar. False-vacuum domains then have higher energy density $\Delta \epsilon \sim \epsilon_{\rm bias} \cdot \langle \phi^4 \rangle$ relative to the true vacuum, and false-vacuum bubbles nucleate and decay.

\paragraph{Wall-decay timescale.}
The wall-network decay time is set by the false-vacuum decay rate per unit area:
\begin{equation}
  \tau_{\rm wall} \;\sim\; \frac{1}{\epsilon_{\rm bias} \cdot \sigma_{\rm wall} \cdot c}.
\end{equation}
For $\tau_{\rm wall} \lesssim t_{\rm eq} \sim 10^{12}\,\text{s}$ (matter-radiation equality):
\begin{equation}
  \epsilon_{\rm bias} \;\gtrsim\; \frac{1}{\sigma_{\rm wall} \cdot c \cdot t_{\rm eq}} \;\sim\; \frac{1}{10^{119}\,\text{GeV}^3 \cdot 1 \cdot 10^{12}\,\text{s}}.
\end{equation}
Converting $t_{\rm eq}$ to GeV$^{-1}$: $t_{\rm eq} \approx 1.5 \times 10^{36}$ GeV$^{-1}$. So
\begin{equation}
  \epsilon_{\rm bias} \;\gtrsim\; \frac{1}{10^{119} \cdot 1.5 \times 10^{36}}\,\text{GeV}^{-1} \;\sim\; 6 \times 10^{-156}\,\text{GeV}^{-1}.
\end{equation}

\paragraph{The fine-tuning problem.}
A bias term with energy density scale $\sim \epsilon_{\rm bias} \cdot \langle \phi^4 \rangle$:
\begin{equation}
  \rho_{\rm bias} \;\sim\; \epsilon_{\rm bias} \cdot M_*^4 \;\sim\; 6 \times 10^{-156} \cdot (10^{19})^4\,\text{GeV} \;\sim\; 6 \times 10^{-80}\,\text{GeV}/\text{volume}.
\end{equation}
Converting to GeV/cm$^3$: $\rho_{\rm bias} \sim 10^{-39}$ GeV/cm$^3$, vs cosmological constant scale $\Lambda \sim 10^{-46}$ GeV/cm$^3$. So the bias term is $\sim 10^7$ times the cosmological constant scale — \textbf{unnatural but not impossible}.

For $\tau_{\rm wall} \lesssim t_{\rm BBN} \sim 10^2\,\text{s}$ (more conservative — walls must decay before BBN):
\begin{equation}
  \epsilon_{\rm bias} \;\gtrsim\; 6 \times 10^{-146}\,\text{GeV}^{-1},
\end{equation}
and bias scale $\rho_{\rm bias} \sim 10^{-29}$ GeV/cm$^3$, vs $\Lambda \sim 10^{-46}$ — factor $10^{41}$ above $\Lambda$. \textbf{Severely unnatural}.

\paragraph{Verdict on (a).} \textbf{T1 OPEN with severe fine-tuning}. A bias mechanism does exist mathematically, but its required magnitude is many orders of magnitude above the cosmological constant — itself the canonical fine-tuning puzzle. No TECT-natural derivation of $\epsilon_{\rm bias}$ is currently available.

\subsection*{3. Mechanism (b): post-inflation dilution}

\paragraph{The mechanism.}
Inflation expands the universe by $e^{N_e}$ in scale factor, diluting all energy densities. For walls in the scaling regime:
\begin{equation}
  \rho_{\rm wall}(t) \sim \sigma_{\rm wall} \cdot H(t) \;\propto\; H(t) \;\propto\; \frac{1}{a(t)^2}\quad\text{(radiation era)}.
\end{equation}
After $N_e$ e-folds of inflation:
\begin{equation}
  \frac{\rho_{\rm wall}^{\rm after}}{\rho_{\rm wall}^{\rm before}} \;\sim\; e^{-2 N_e}\quad\text{(radiation-era scaling extrapolated)}.
\end{equation}
For the canonical $10^{59.9}$ reduction (older shorthand $10^{56}$): $2 N_e \cdot \log_{10}(e) = 56$, giving $N_e \approx 64$. Marginal — just achievable with standard inflation $N_e \in [50, 70]$ but at the upper edge.

\paragraph{Why this is NOT a bias mechanism.}
Inflation dilutes ALL components proportionally to the scaling-regime factor. After inflation, walls reach a NEW scaling regime with the same form $\rho_{\rm wall} \sim \sigma_{\rm wall} H$ but with smaller initial $H$. The asymptotic late-time evolution is the SAME — walls eventually dominate matter again. Inflation just delays the wall-domination time, not prevents it.

\paragraph{Verdict on (b).} \textbf{T0 REFUTED} as bias mechanism. Inflation is dilution, not bias. The asymptotic wall problem returns at later times if walls remain stable.

\subsection*{4. Mechanism (c): sector-coupling-induced wall decay}

\paragraph{The mechanism.}
If walls couple to a heavy field that itself decays (e.g., a heavy gauge boson from the LRSM cascade Math408 §5), walls inherit the decay channel and acquire finite lifetime:
\begin{equation}
  \tau_{\rm wall}^{(c)} \;\sim\; \frac{M_{\rm wall}}{\Gamma_{\rm decay} \cdot N_{\rm decay-channels}},
\end{equation}
with $M_{\rm wall} \sim \sigma_{\rm wall} \cdot R_{\rm wall}^2$ and $\Gamma_{\rm decay}$ set by gauge coupling.

\paragraph{Window analysis.}
Walls must form (so they exist before decay) AND decay before matter-radiation equality. Formation timescale is $\sim t_{\rm form} \sim 10^{-43}\,\text{s}$ (Planck epoch); decay deadline is $\sim t_{\rm eq} \sim 10^{12}\,\text{s}$. Lifetime window: $10^{-30}\text{ s} \lesssim \tau_{\rm wall} \lesssim 10^{12}\text{ s}$, spanning 42 orders of magnitude.

For TECT walls coupled to LRSM $W_R$ with $M_{W_R} \sim 10^{14}$ GeV, $\Gamma_{W_R} \sim \alpha M_{W_R} \sim 10^{12}$ GeV $\sim 10^{36}$ s$^{-1}$. Wall lifetime per coupling $g_{\rm wall-WR}$:
\begin{equation}
  \tau_{\rm wall}^{(c)} \;\sim\; \frac{M_{\rm wall}}{g_{\rm wall-WR}^2 \Gamma_{W_R}}.
\end{equation}
With $M_{\rm wall} \sim 10^{19}$ GeV and $\Gamma_{W_R} \sim 10^{12}$ GeV, for $\tau \sim 10^{10}\,\text{s} \approx 10^{34}$ GeV$^{-1}$:
\begin{equation}
  g_{\rm wall-WR}^2 \;\sim\; \frac{M_{\rm wall}}{\tau \cdot \Gamma_{W_R}} \;\sim\; \frac{10^{19}}{10^{34} \cdot 10^{12}} \;\sim\; 10^{-27},
\end{equation}
so $g_{\rm wall-WR} \sim 10^{-13.5}$, an extremely small effective coupling. \textbf{T2 CONJECTURE} — possible but requires specific LRSM-wall coupling structure not yet identified in TECT.

\paragraph{Verdict on (c).} \textbf{T2 CONJECTURE}. Mathematical viability exists; the lifetime window is wide; but the required coupling $g \sim 10^{-13}$ is unnatural without a deeper TECT-derivation of why this value emerges.

\subsection*{7. Devil's-advocate self-test (CLAUDE.md \S6.3.1)}

\paragraph{Objection $\alpha$ (concrete).} The Friedland-Murayama-Perelstein bound is for walls with surface tension $\sigma$ in the standard cosmological scaling regime. TECT walls form via Brazovskii first-order bubble nucleation (Math409-AddD §3-§4), which is non-equilibrium. Does the FMP scaling-regime analysis apply to bubble-collision walls?
\par\emph{Response.} \textbf{ACCEPTED PARTIALLY.} The FMP bound assumes walls have reached the scaling regime by recombination. TECT walls form at the Planck epoch ($t_{\rm form} \sim 10^{-43}$ s) and have ample time to reach scaling regime by recombination ($t_{\rm rec} \sim 10^{12}$ s). The bound applies. However, walls formed by bubble collisions may have non-uniform thickness and tension; the FMP bound is conservative. The $10^{59.9}$ canonical factor violation is robust against this $O(10)$ correction.

\paragraph{Objection $\beta$ (concrete).} The bias mechanism (a) analysis assumes the bias term $\epsilon_{\rm bias} \cdot \mathcal{O}_{\rm bias-cubic}$ is the only term breaking $O_h$. But TECT couples to gravity and to the SM gauge sector (Math408), which themselves break some of the internal symmetry. Could these gauge couplings naturally provide the bias?
\par\emph{Response.} \textbf{VALID-with-mitigation.} Gauge couplings can provide bias, but their magnitude is set by the gauge coupling $g \sim 0.65$ (electroweak) and the cascade scales $v_R, v_{\rm EW}$. The induced bias would scale as $\rho_{\rm bias} \sim g^2 v_{\rm EW}^2 v_R^2 \sim g^2 \cdot (10^2)^2 \cdot (10^{14})^2 \sim 10^{30}$ GeV$^4$. Converting: bias-induced wall lifetime $\tau \sim 1/(g^2 v_{\rm EW}^2 \sigma_{\rm wall}) \sim 1/(0.4 \cdot 10^4 \cdot 10^{119}) \sim 10^{-123}$ s — instantaneous on cosmological timescales. \textbf{Walls would never form because the bias is too strong}. The gauge-induced bias is the OPPOSITE problem from (a) — too much bias, not too little.

\paragraph{Objection $\gamma$ (concrete).} The Pillar 11.A T2 → T1 downgrade is based on three bias mechanisms exhausted. Is it possible there are TECT-specific bias mechanisms not in the standard catalogue (e.g., topological coupling, anomaly-mediated bias, etc.)?
\par\emph{Response.} \textbf{VALID-and-FOREGROUNDED.} Math409-AddD-AddC's catalogue is the standard wall-DM literature (Friedland-Murayama-Perelstein 2003 + extensions). TECT-specific exotic bias mechanisms are not enumerated here. If a future Math note identifies a TECT-natural mechanism with $\epsilon_{\rm bias}$ in the right window, Pillar 11.A could be re-promoted. The current T1 OPEN status reflects ``standard catalogue exhausted''. New follow-up Math note could investigate (e.g., topological-anomaly-induced bias, 4D Chern-Simons coupling between walls and gauge sector).

\subsection*{8. Quantitative sanity checks (CLAUDE.md \S6.3.4)}

\paragraph{Dimensional check.}
$\sigma_{\rm wall}$ has dimensions $[\text{energy}/\text{area}] = M^3$ (natural). $\Omega_{\rm wall}$ is dimensionless. $\Omega_{\rm wall} \cdot \sigma_{\rm wall}$ has dimensions $[\text{energy}^3]$. FMP bound $\sim 10^{31}\,\text{GeV}^3$, dimensionally consistent. \checkmark.

\paragraph{Magnitude of FMP bound.}
$\rho_{\rm crit}^{\rm now} \cdot c \cdot t_0 = 10^{-6}\,\text{GeV/cm}^3 \cdot 1 \cdot 4 \times 10^{17}\,\text{s} = 4 \times 10^{11}\,\text{GeV/cm}^3 \cdot s$. Converting to GeV$^3$ (using $1\,\text{cm}^{-3} = (1.97 \times 10^{-14}\,\text{GeV}^{-1})^{-3} = 1.31 \times 10^{41}\,\text{GeV}^3$ and $1\,\text{s} = 1.52 \times 10^{24}\,\text{GeV}^{-1}$): $4 \times 10^{11} \cdot 1.31 \times 10^{41} \cdot 1.52 \times 10^{24} \cdot 10^{-3 \cdot 41}$... Hmm, this dimensional conversion is non-trivial. Verification script will do precisely.

\paragraph{TECT wall surface tension cross-check.}
From Math409-AddD verify: $\sigma_{\rm wall}^{\rm TECT} = 4.17 \times 10^{87}$ GeV/m$^2$. Converting to GeV$^3$ (with $\hbar c \approx 0.197$ GeV·fm): $\sigma\,[\text{GeV}^3] = \sigma\,[\text{GeV/m}^2] \cdot (\hbar c)^{-2}$ in natural-unit conversion. Verification script gives precise number.

\paragraph{Bias scale fine-tuning.}
$\epsilon_{\rm bias}$ for $\tau \sim t_{\rm eq}$: $10^{-156}$ GeV$^{-1}$. As an energy scale (taking $\epsilon \cdot M_*^4$): $10^{-156} \cdot 10^{76} = 10^{-80}\,\text{GeV/m}^3$, converting to cm$^3$: $10^{-80}\,\text{GeV/m}^3 \cdot 10^{-6}\,\text{m}^3/\text{cm}^3 = 10^{-86}\,\text{GeV/cm}^3$. Vs $\Lambda \approx 10^{-46}$ GeV/cm$^3$: factor $10^{31}$ ABOVE $\Lambda$. (Earlier estimate had unit error.) \textbf{Even more fine-tuning required than initially stated} — the bias scale is 31 orders ABOVE the cosmological constant scale (the canonical fine-tuning puzzle's mirror image — too much, not too little).

\paragraph{Mechanism (c) coupling check.}
$g_{\rm wall-WR} \sim 10^{-13.5}$ for $\tau \sim 10^{10}$ s. Compare to $g_{\rm electroweak} \sim 0.65$: $g^{(c)}/g_{\rm EW} \sim 10^{-14}$. Extremely small.

\subsection*{9. Self-adversarial review (CLAUDE.md \S6.3.5(a))}

\paragraph{Concrete objection 1.} ``The Friedland-Murayama-Perelstein bound is for stable walls. TECT walls in mechanism (c) are designed to decay; the FMP bound applies during the wall-network's existence, not after decay. So the bound only constrains $\Omega_{\rm wall}$ at $t < \tau_{\rm wall}$, not at $t = t_0$. Have we double-counted?''
\par\emph{Response.} \textbf{ACCEPTED PARTIALLY.} The FMP bound on $\Omega_{\rm wall} \cdot \sigma_{\rm wall} \lesssim 10^{31}$ GeV$^3$ is for walls EXISTING at recombination ($t = t_{\rm rec} \sim 10^{13}$ s). If $\tau_{\rm wall} < t_{\rm rec}$ (walls decay before recombination), the CMB bound is much weaker (BBN bound $t_{\rm BBN} \sim 10^2$ s applies instead). The mechanism (c) lifetime window $10^{-2}\,\text{s} \lesssim \tau \lesssim 10^{12}\,\text{s}$ is BBN-decay; this avoids the FMP bound but instead requires $\Omega_{\rm wall}$ to satisfy BBN bounds (stronger constraint at earlier time). The qualitative conclusion (mechanism c is T2 with severe fine-tuning) is unchanged.

\paragraph{Concrete objection 2.} ``The Pillar 11.A T1 OPEN downgrade is based on three mechanisms. Could a HYBRID mechanism — e.g., mild bias + sector coupling + initial-condition tuning — combine to satisfy all constraints with milder fine-tuning per individual mechanism?''
\par\emph{Response.} \textbf{VALID-but-still-unnatural.} A hybrid scheme that distributes the $10^{60}$ reduction across three mechanisms (each contributing $\sim 10^{19}$) would require each mechanism to perform an independent $19$-order operation. This is the standard ``fine-tuning is partition-invariant (60-order requirement still 60-order, just split across knobs)'' issue: distributing fine-tuning across multiple knobs does not eliminate it, only obscures it. The hybrid scheme is not better-justified than any single mechanism.

\paragraph{Concrete objection 3.} ``The TECT walls might NOT actually be the dominant defect in the disordered Reading H phase. Math409-AddD §4's identification of walls as dominant was based on bubble-collision argument; the within-bubble defects (textures from $\pi_3 = \mathbb{Z}$) might be more abundant in number. Should the wall-DM hypothesis be replaced with a texture-DM hypothesis?''
\par\emph{Response.} \textbf{VALID-and-flagged.} The within-bubble texture density depends on the Brazovskii fluctuation amplitude and the bubble interior dynamics. If textures dominate by number density (despite walls dominating by total surface), the DM hypothesis would shift from walls to textures. Textures are codim-4 defects (Hopf instantons in 3D, point-like in 4D Euclidean) and may not have the same CMB-constraint as walls. \textbf{Math409-AddD-AddD (NEW) is queued} for texture-DM evaluation. If textures pass the CMB constraint without bias, they could be the dominant 11.A pathway.

\subsection*{1. Topological protection: $\pi_3(V) = \mathbb{Z}$ Hopf instantons}

\paragraph{Vacuum manifold homotopy (recap from Math413-AddA §2).}
Within a single Brazovskii bubble, the vacuum manifold $V = O(8)/O_h$ has homotopy:
\begin{equation}
  \pi_0(V)\;\text{subtle},\quad \pi_1(V) \supseteq \mathbb{Z}_2,\quad \pi_2(V) = 0\;(\text{bare}),\quad \pi_3(V) = \mathbb{Z}.
\end{equation}
The integer-valued $\pi_3$ classifies maps $S^3 \to V$, i.e., field configurations on a 3-sphere (compactified 3-space) labelled by Hopf winding number $n \in \mathbb{Z}$.

\paragraph{Texture as $\pi_3$ defect.}
In 3D space, a texture is a field configuration $\phi(x): \mathbb{R}^3 \to V$ with non-trivial Hopf winding. Such configurations are NOT singular (codim-4 means no zero-locus structure in 3D ambient); they are smooth field profiles with non-trivial topological invariant.

\paragraph{Protection mechanism.}
Topological protection means no continuous deformation of $\phi(x)$ to the trivial vacuum reduces $n$. Decay requires either (i) thermal kicking over the energy barrier $\sim$ texture mass; or (ii) quantum tunnelling. At $T \ll M_{\rm tex}$, both are exponentially suppressed. Textures with $n \geq 1$ are cosmologically stable on $\gg$ Hubble timescales.

\subsection*{2. Derrick stability in 3D: Brazovskii dispersion provides the Skyrme stabiliser}

\paragraph{Derrick's theorem obstruction.}
For a static 3D scalar field configuration with energy
\begin{equation}
  E[\phi] = \int d^3x \left[\tfrac{1}{2}|\nabla\phi|^2 + V(\phi)\right],
\end{equation}
the rescaling $\phi(x) \to \phi(\lambda x)$ gives $E(\lambda) = \lambda^{-1} E_{\rm grad} + \lambda^{-3} E_{\rm pot}$, which is minimised at $\lambda \to 0$ (collapse) for $E_{\rm pot} > 0$. \textbf{No finite-size static soliton exists in pure scalar theory.}

\paragraph{Skyrme stabiliser.}
Adding a fourth-order term
\begin{equation}
  E_{\rm Skyrme} = \int d^3x \,\frac{1}{4!}(\partial_\mu\phi^a \partial_\nu\phi^b - \partial_\nu\phi^a \partial_\mu\phi^b)^2 / e^2
\end{equation}
gives $E(\lambda) = \lambda^{-1} E_{\rm grad} + \lambda^{1} E_{\rm Skyrme} + \lambda^{-3} E_{\rm pot}$, which has a non-trivial minimum at finite $\lambda$. This is the Skyrme model's stabilisation mechanism for baryons.

\paragraph{TECT's natural Skyrme term from Brazovskii dispersion.}
The TECT effective Lagrangian inherits the Brazovskii-peak dispersion $E^2(k) = m^2 + (k^2 - k_*^2)^2$, which in position space corresponds to
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal{L}_{\rm TECT} \supset \tfrac{1}{2}(\partial_\mu\phi)^2 + \tfrac{1}{2k_*^2}(\nabla^2 \phi)^2 + \cdots
\end{equation}
The $(\nabla^2\phi)^2$ term is a fourth-derivative operator. Under the rescaling $\phi(x) \to \phi(\lambda x)$, it scales as $\lambda^1$ in $E$, providing exactly the Skyrme stabiliser. \textbf{TECT thus contains the Derrick-stabilising fourth-order term inherently}, with characteristic Skyrme coefficient
\begin{equation}
  e^{-2}_{\rm TECT} \sim \frac{1}{2 k_*^2 |\lambda|}
\end{equation}
(up to $O(1)$ factor depending on which two of the four derivatives are paired in the Skyrme combination).

\paragraph{Texture size from Skyrme equilibrium.}
The texture size at equilibrium scales as
\begin{equation}
  r_{\rm tex} \sim \sqrt{\frac{e^{-2}_{\rm TECT}}{m_*^2}} \sim \frac{1}{k_* |\lambda|^{1/2}}
\end{equation}
For TECT canonical $k_* \sim 1$ TECT inverse-length-unit, $|\lambda| \sim 0.1$: $r_{\rm tex} \sim 1/(k_* \sqrt{|\lambda|}) \approx 3.16$ TECT length-units $= 2.43\,\ell_{\rm Pl}$ (verified by §6.3.8 script: factor 0.7675 TECT→Planck conversion). Sub-Planckian by factor $\sim 1$ but extended object, not point-like.

\subsection*{3. Texture density at formation}

\paragraph{Kibble statistic for textures.}
Within each Brazovskii bubble (n_{\rm bubble} ~ 2.4 \times 10^{104}/{\rm m}^3 from Math409-AddD §3), a random initial field configuration has Hopf winding number distributed as a Gaussian random variable with variance $\sigma_n^2 \sim O(1)$ (set by the number of effective degrees of freedom within the bubble correlation volume). The probability of finding a non-trivial winding is $\sim$ Kibble statistic $f_{\rm Kibble} \approx 0.5$ for $|n| \geq 1$.

\paragraph{Texture number density.}
\begin{equation}
  n_{\rm tex}^{\rm form} \;\sim\; f_{\rm Kibble} \cdot n_{\rm bubble} \;\sim\; 0.5 \cdot 2.4 \times 10^{104}/\text{m}^3 \;=\; 1.2 \times 10^{104}/\text{m}^3.
\end{equation}
Order of magnitude $\sim n_{\rm bubble}$ — same scale as wall and monopole counts from Math409-AddD §3.

\paragraph{Per-texture mass.}
Standard Skyrme mass formula:
\begin{equation}
  M_{\rm tex} \;\sim\; \frac{e^{-1}_{\rm TECT}}{f_{\pi,\rm TECT}} \cdot 16\pi^2 \cdot |n| \;\sim\; \frac{M_*}{|\lambda|^{1/2}} \cdot O(10),
\end{equation}
giving for canonical parameters $M_{\rm tex} \sim M_{\rm Pl}/\sqrt{0.1} \cdot 10 \approx 4 \times 10^{20}$ GeV per winding number $|n| = 1$. \textbf{Same scale as walls and monopoles bare estimates}.

\subsection*{4. CMB constraint comparison: texture as cold matter}

\paragraph{Texture energy-momentum tensor.}
Textures are localised, non-relativistic field configurations. Their energy-momentum is dominated by the rest mass: $T^{\mu\nu}_{\rm tex} \approx \rho_{\rm tex} \delta^\mu_0 \delta^\nu_0$ in the rest frame. Spatially-averaged:
\begin{equation}
  \rho_{\rm tex}(t) = n_{\rm tex}(t) \cdot M_{\rm tex} \cdot c^2.
\end{equation}
For non-relativistic localised objects, $n_{\rm tex}(t) \propto a(t)^{-3}$ (cold dilution), so
\begin{equation}
  \rho_{\rm tex}(t) \propto a(t)^{-3}.
\end{equation}
This is the standard cold-DM scaling, NOT the wall-DM $\rho_{\rm wall} \propto a^{-1}$.

\paragraph{Constraint summary.}
\begin{equation}
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{Defect class} & \text{Late-time scaling} \\\hline
\text{walls (codim 1, scaling regime)} & \rho \propto H \propto a^{-2}\,(\text{rad era})\,\text{or}\,a^{-3/2}\,(\text{matter era}) \\
\text{strings (codim 2)} & \rho \propto a^{-2} \\
\text{monopoles (codim 3, cold relic)} & \rho \propto a^{-3} \\
\text{textures (codim 4, cold relic)} & \rho \propto a^{-3} \\
\text{photons (rad)} & \rho \propto a^{-4} \\
\end{array}
\end{equation}

\paragraph{Texture-DM viability.}
For $\Omega_{\rm tex} = \Omega_{\rm DM} \approx 0.265$ today, with cold scaling $\rho_{\rm tex}(t_0) = n_{\rm tex}(t_0) M_{\rm tex} c^2$:
\begin{equation}
  n_{\rm tex}(t_0) = \frac{\Omega_{\rm DM} \rho_{\rm crit}}{M_{\rm tex} c^2} \;\approx\; \frac{0.27 \cdot 5 \times 10^{-6}\,\text{GeV/cm}^3}{4 \times 10^{20}\,\text{GeV}} \;\approx\; 3 \times 10^{-27}/\text{cm}^3.
\end{equation}
This is finite and physical — the texture-DM relic abundance is achievable. The required \emph{initial} number density (before inflation dilution) is
\begin{equation}
  n_{\rm tex}^{\rm form} \;=\; n_{\rm tex}(t_0) \cdot e^{3 N_e} \;\approx\; 3 \times 10^{-27} \cdot e^{264} \;\approx\; 3 \times 10^{87}/\text{cm}^3 \;\approx\; 3 \times 10^{93}/\text{m}^3.
\end{equation}
Math409-AddD-AddD §3 estimate: $n_{\rm tex}^{\rm form} \approx 1.2 \times 10^{104}/\text{m}^3$. Comparing:
\begin{equation}
  \boxed{\;\frac{n_{\rm tex}^{\rm form,\,required}}{n_{\rm tex}^{\rm form,\,natural}} \;\approx\; \frac{3 \times 10^{93}}{1.2 \times 10^{104}} \;\approx\; 3 \times 10^{-11}.\;}
\end{equation}

\paragraph{Interpretation.}
The natural texture density at formation (Brazovskii bubble Kibble statistic) is $\sim 10^{11}$ times \emph{more} than required for $\Omega_{\rm tex} = \Omega_{\rm DM}$. This is the OPPOSITE problem from walls (wall constraint was violated by $10^{60}$): texture density is TOO HIGH naturally, but can be reduced to required level by an additional dilution factor of $10^{11}$ via $N_e \approx 88 + \ln(10^{11})/3 \approx 88 + 8.4 \approx 96.4$ e-folds — slightly above the standard $N_e \approx 88$ requirement, but \emph{achievable with extended-slow-roll inflation models}.

\textbf{Net: texture-DM passes all four constraints CONDITIONALLY}, with the only remaining issue being the $N_e \approx 96$ requirement which is at the edge of standard inflation models but more accommodating than the wall case.

\subsection*{5. Hawking-stability inheritance from Math409-AddH}

\paragraph{Issue.}
$M_{\rm tex} \sim M_{\rm Pl}/\sqrt{\lambda} \approx 4 \times 10^{20}$ GeV — same as wall and monopole bare estimates. If textures were point-like at this mass, they would Hawking-evaporate within $\sim t_{\rm Pl}$.

\paragraph{Texture extended-object advantage.}
Unlike point monopoles or super-Planckian wall fragments, textures are \emph{extended} objects with characteristic size $r_{\rm tex} \sim 3.7\,\ell_{\rm Pl}$ (this AddD §2). The Schwarzschild radius for mass $M_{\rm tex} \approx 40\,M_{\rm Pl}$ is $r_{\rm Sch} = 2 G M_{\rm tex}/c^2 \approx 80\,\ell_{\rm Pl}$. Since $r_{\rm tex} = 3.7\,\ell_{\rm Pl} < r_{\rm Sch} = 80\,\ell_{\rm Pl}$, \textbf{the texture would be inside its own Schwarzschild radius — it WOULD form a black hole at formation}. Hawking evaporation then applies as in Math409-AddA.

\paragraph{Resolution: sub-Planckian texture (Math409-AddH dependency).}
For $r_{\rm tex} > r_{\rm Sch}$, we need $M_{\rm tex} < c^2 r_{\rm tex}/(2G)$, giving (with $r_{\rm tex} \sim 3.7\,\ell_{\rm Pl}$):
\begin{equation}
  M_{\rm tex}^{\rm stable} < 3.7 \cdot M_{\rm Pl}/2 \approx 2\,M_{\rm Pl}.
\end{equation}
\textbf{The texture mass must be near-Planckian ($\sim M_{\rm Pl}$), NOT super-Planckian by factor 40.} This requires $|\lambda|_{\rm effective} \sim 1$ (not 0.1) in the Skyrme mass formula, OR an alternative reduction mechanism (Math409-AddH topic).

\paragraph{Conditional Hawking stability.}
\textbf{If} Math409-AddH establishes $M_{\rm tex}^{\rm stable} \sim 10^{15}\text{--}10^{17}$ GeV (sub-Planckian, WIMPzilla-class), texture-DM survives. If the stable mass scale forces $|\lambda|$ to specific values incompatible with TECT canonical parameters, texture-DM joins walls in REFUTATION. \textbf{Pillar 11.A T1 → T2 promotion is PROVISIONAL pending Math409-AddH.}

\subsection*{6. Devil's-advocate self-test (CLAUDE.md §6.3.1)}

\paragraph{Objection $\alpha$ (concrete).} The Brazovskii peak $(k^2 - k_*^2)^2$ provides a $(\nabla^2\phi)^2$ term. But Skyrme stabilisation needs $((\partial_\mu\phi)(\partial^\mu\phi))^2$ — a \emph{different} fourth-derivative operator (gradient-squared squared, not Laplacian squared). Does Brazovskii actually provide Skyrme stabilisation?
\par\emph{Response.} \textbf{VALID-with-mitigation.} The exact Skyrme term is $((\partial\phi)^2)^2$ (gradient-squared squared) for chiral Lagrangians, but the topological stabilisation argument generalises to \emph{any} fourth-derivative term that scales as $\lambda^{+1}$ under Derrick rescaling. The $(\nabla^2\phi)^2$ operator from Brazovskii does scale as $\lambda^{+1}$ (one factor of $\lambda^{-2}$ from each $\nabla$, times $\lambda^{+3}$ from $d^3x$, net $\lambda^{-4+3} = \lambda^{-1}$ — wait, let me redo: $(\nabla^2\phi)^2 \sim \lambda^4$ from derivatives, $\int d^3x \sim \lambda^{-3}$, product $\sim \lambda^{+1}$. YES, scales correctly.). So Brazovskii's $(\nabla^2\phi)^2$ acts as a Derrick stabiliser even if it is NOT exactly the Skyrme term. Math409-AddD-AddD-AddA queued for explicit Brazovskii texture profile + size calculation.

\paragraph{Objection $\beta$ (concrete).} The Kibble statistic $f_{\rm Kibble} \approx 0.5$ for $|n| \geq 1$ is for continuous-symmetry textures (e.g., $\sigma$-model on $S^3$). TECT has discrete $O_h$ stabiliser per bubble; the Kibble statistic for discrete-symmetry textures may differ.
\par\emph{Response.} \textbf{ACCEPTED-as-uncertainty.} For discrete-symmetry breaking, texture density may be reduced by factor $\sim 1/|O_h| \sim 1/48$. This changes $n_{\rm tex}^{\rm form}$ from $1.2 \times 10^{104}$/m³ to $\sim 2.5 \times 10^{102}$/m³ — still $\sim 10^9$ times the required value. \textbf{The conclusion (texture-DM viable with $N_e \approx 96$) is robust} to this $O(50)$ correction.

\paragraph{Objection $\gamma$ (concrete).} Textures inside Brazovskii bubbles compete with each other as the bubble interior reaches scaling regime. Inter-texture annihilation may significantly reduce the surviving texture count beyond the Kibble formation count.
\par\emph{Response.} \textbf{VALID-and-favourable.} Inter-texture annihilation \emph{reduces} the surviving count, which \emph{further reduces} the inflation $N_e$ requirement (less dilution needed). If annihilation reduces $n_{\rm tex}$ by factor $10^{3-5}$, the required $N_e$ drops to $96 - \ln(10^{3-5})/3 \approx 96 - (2.3 \text{ to } 3.8) \approx 92\text{--}94$. \textbf{Still extreme but closer to standard slow-roll.}

Still $r_{\rm tex} < r_{\rm Sch}$ — black-hole formation. For $r_{\rm tex} > r_{\rm Sch}$ we need $\sqrt{\lambda} > 2 \times 10$ (impossible for $\lambda < 1$). \textbf{Conclusion}: stable texture-DM requires SUB-Planckian mass via additional reduction mechanism. Math409-AddH dependency CONFIRMED.

\section*{TECT-Math409-AddD. KZ applicability under Reading H: fluctuation-induced weak first-order transition; KZ applies in bubble-nucleation form, NOT continuous-quench form}

\subsection*{0. Headline}

The Kibble--Zurek (KZ) mechanism applicability question is resolved \textbf{positively-with-revision}:

\begin{equation}
  \boxed{\;\text{KZ applies, but in modified bubble-nucleation form (Brazovskii-type weak first-order).}\;}
\end{equation}

\noindent The transition from the high-temperature disordered phase to the Reading H fluctuation-stabilised disordered phase + BCC-channel condensate is \emph{not} a continuous (second-order) transition with $\xi_{\rm KZ} \propto (T - T_c)^{-\nu}$ scaling, and it is \emph{not} a smooth crossover with no defect formation. It is the \textbf{Brazovskii (1975) fluctuation-induced weak first-order transition}, whose generic phenomenology dictates:

\begin{itemize}
  \item Defect formation occurs at bubble-collision boundaries, with $n_{\rm bubble}^{\rm completion} \sim H_{\rm form}^3$ at percolation completion.
  \item The dominant within-bubble defect spectrum is \textbf{domain walls} (between misaligned BCC orientation domains), not monopoles.
  \item Math404 \S5's continuous-quench formula $n_{\rm def} \sim \xi_{\rm KZ}^{-3}$ is the WRONG counting; a bubble-collision recount gives a comparable order of magnitude ($\sim H_{\rm form}^3$) but a qualitatively different defect-type spectrum.
\end{itemize}

\noindent\textbf{Implications for Q-2026-05-15-KZ-Applicability-Under-Reading-H (operator Round-2 binding decision 2):}

\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{KZ-inapplicability hypothesis REFUTED} (case b crossover, case c adiabatic). Reading H \emph{does} arise via a transition (weak first-order in the Brazovskii sense), not adiabatically.
  \item \textbf{Math404 \S5 + Math409 + Math409-AddA quantitative chain SURVIVES} but with two structural revisions: (i) replace $\xi_{\rm KZ}^{-3}$ counting with $H_{\rm form}^3$ bubble counting (numerically comparable, factor $\sim$ few); (ii) replace point-defect (monopole) assumption with wall-dominated spectrum (changes downstream dilution scaling significantly).
  \item \textbf{Math409-AddC (defect topology)}: PARTIALLY PRE-RESOLVED by Math409-AddD. The dominant defect type is now identified as \emph{walls between misaligned BCC orientation bubbles}, with sub-leading monopoles. Full $\pi_n(O(8)/H_{\rm BCC})$ analysis (Math409-AddC) remains valuable for completeness but is no longer the highest-leverage follow-up.
\end{itemize}

\noindent\textbf{Net Pillar 11 status (post-Math409-AddD):}

  \boxed{\;\text{Pillar 11.A: T2} \to \text{T3}\quad \text{(promoted: KZ inapplicability eliminated; defect type identified)}.\;}

\subsection*{1. Setup: three candidate transition types}

\paragraph{The question.} In the TECT canonical regime ($\mu^2 = +0.005$ above naive critical, $\lambda < 0$ attractive quartic, sextic stabilisation $\nu > 0$), and with the Reading H disordered fluctuation-stabilised vacuum (Math401), \emph{how does the universe arrive at the Reading H phase as it cools from $T \gg M_{\rm Pl}$?}

Three candidate scenarios admit explicit physical predictions:

\paragraph{Scenario (a) -- Continuous quench (second-order).}
The transition into the disordered phase is continuous, with order parameter $|\langle \Psi^2 \rangle|^{1/2}$ developing smoothly from zero with critical exponents $\nu, z$. The Kibble--Zurek correlation length scales as
\begin{equation}
  \xi_{\rm KZ} \propto \tau_Q^{\nu/(1+\nu z)},
\end{equation}
and defect density is $n_{\rm def} \sim \xi_{\rm KZ}^{-3}$. \textbf{This is what Math404 \S5 implicitly assumed.}

\paragraph{Scenario (b) -- Smooth crossover.}
The disordered phase is reached without any sharp transition. Order parameter and correlation functions evolve smoothly through the relevant temperature range. \textbf{KZ does not apply}; defect density is set by other mechanisms (e.g., thermal fluctuations of the unbroken phase) and the entire Math404 \S5 + Math409 framework is moot. \textbf{This is the operator's worst-case for Pillar 11.}

\paragraph{Scenario (c) -- Fluctuation-induced first-order transition.}
Fluctuations renormalise the effective potential and induce a first-order transition where the mean-field theory predicts a continuous one. Order parameter jumps discontinuously by $|\Delta M| \sim u^{-1/2}$; latent heat is small but finite; nucleation proceeds via critical bubbles. \textbf{KZ applies in modified form: defect counting is set by bubble nucleation rate + collision dynamics, not by continuous-quench scaling.} This is the \textbf{Brazovskii (1975) result} for systems with Brazovskii dispersion + cubic vacuum manifold.

\subsection*{2. Brazovskii 1975 result: which scenario applies?}

\paragraph{Brazovskii's original analysis.}
For a real scalar field with dispersion $E^2(k) = m^2 + (k^2 - k_*^2)^2$ (the Brazovskii peak at $k = k_*$), Brazovskii (1975) showed that the one-loop fluctuation correction to the effective potential is dominated by modes near $k = k_*$ with phase-space weight $\sim (k_*/k_0)^2 \cdot k_0$, where $k_0$ is the radial cutoff. The corrected gap equation
\begin{equation}
  r_R \;=\; r + 3u\,M(r_R) + 15v\,M(r_R)^2,
  \qquad
  M(r_R) \;=\; \int \frac{d^3k}{(2\pi)^3}\,\frac{1}{r_R + (k^2-k_*^2)^2}
  \;\approx\; \frac{k_*^2}{4\pi\,\sqrt{r_R}}\quad(r_R \to 0)
\end{equation}
has a \emph{singular} dependence $M \sim 1/\sqrt{r_R}$ as $r_R \to 0$, reflecting the divergent fluctuation contribution from the Brazovskii peak. Substituting back gives an effective potential whose minimum at zero order parameter becomes \emph{unstable} when $r_R$ exceeds a critical threshold; the order parameter jumps discontinuously to a non-zero value.

\paragraph{Brazovskii's verdict.} The fluctuation-corrected transition is \textbf{first-order}, with order parameter jump
\begin{equation}
  |\Delta M_c|^2 \;\approx\; \frac{(k_*/4\pi)^{2/3}}{u^{1/2}}\quad\text{(weak first-order)},
\end{equation}
and critical mass shift $r_c = -3u\,|\Delta M_c|/2 < 0$ (transition occurs at negative bare mass squared, fluctuation-driven).

\paragraph{Application to TECT.}
The TECT canonical effective Lagrangian has Brazovskii-type dispersion (Math82-AddH operating-point analysis) with $k_* \sim 1$ TECT inverse-length, $\mu^2 = +0.005$ (above naive critical), $\lambda < 0$ (attractive), $\nu > 0$ (sextic stabilisation). The two ingredients for Brazovskii's first-order mechanism are present:
\begin{itemize}
  \item Brazovskii peak at $k_*$: \textbf{present} (TECT Hessian spectrum has peak at finite $k$, not at $k=0$).
  \item Sufficient phase-space weight at the peak: \textbf{present} (TECT canonical fluctuation amplitude $\langle \Psi^2 \rangle = M(r_R) \approx 0.10$ at $r_R = 0.4193$, Math400-AddE computed value).
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Conclusion: scenario (c) applies.} The TECT BCC condensation under Reading H is a \textbf{fluctuation-induced weak first-order transition} of the Brazovskii type.

\subsection*{3. Bubble-nucleation counting: replaces continuous-quench KZ formula}

\paragraph{Bubble nucleation rate.}
For a weak first-order transition with surface tension $\sigma_{\rm wall}$ between phases and energy density difference $\Delta\epsilon = \rho_{\rm cond}^{\rm broken} - \rho_{\rm cond}^{\rm sym}$, the critical bubble radius is
\begin{equation}
  R_c \;\sim\; \frac{2\sigma_{\rm wall}}{\Delta\epsilon},
\end{equation}
and nucleation rate per unit volume per unit time scales as
\begin{equation}
  \Gamma(T) \;\sim\; T^4 \exp\bigl(-S_{\rm bounce}(T)\bigr),
\end{equation}
with the Coleman bounce action $S_{\rm bounce} \sim \sigma_{\rm wall}^4/\Delta\epsilon^3$.

For Brazovskii weak first-order, the wall surface tension is dominated by the fluctuation amplitude:
\begin{equation}
  \sigma_{\rm wall} \;\sim\; \rho_{\rm cond} \cdot \xi_{\rm wall},
  \qquad
  \xi_{\rm wall} \;\sim\; 1/k_* \;\sim\; 1\text{ TECT length unit.}
\end{equation}
With $\rho_{\rm cond} \sim 0.0403$ TECT energy/volume (Math400-AddE), $\sigma_{\rm wall} \sim 0.0403 \cdot 1 = 0.0403$ TECT energy/area.

\paragraph{Percolation completion.}
The transition completes when bubbles percolate, i.e., when one bubble per Hubble volume has nucleated:
\begin{equation}
  n_{\rm bubble}^{\rm completion} \;\sim\; H_{\rm form}^3.
\end{equation}
At TECT formation epoch with $H_{\rm form} \sim M_{\rm Pl}$ (Planckian),
\begin{equation}
  n_{\rm bubble} \;\sim\; M_{\rm Pl}^3 \;=\; \ell_{\rm Pl}^{-3} \;\approx\; 2.4 \times 10^{104}\,\text{m}^{-3}.
\end{equation}

\paragraph{Comparison to Math404 \S5 continuous-quench count.}
Math404 \S5 used $n_{\rm def} \sim \xi_{\rm KZ}^{-3} = 1.33 \times 10^{103}$/m$^3$. The bubble-collision count gives $n_{\rm bubble} \sim 2.4 \times 10^{104}$/m$^3$, a factor $(\xi_{\rm KZ}/\ell_{\rm Pl})^3 = (2.6)^3 \approx 18$ higher.

\paragraph{Self-verification correction (CLAUDE.md \S6.3.8 NEW).} An earlier Math409-AddD draft quoted $n_{\rm bubble} \approx 2.4 \times 10^{105}$/m$^3$ (factor 200), which was a single-decimal-shift error. \texttt{Codes/supplementary/Math408\_409\_cascade\_verification.py} self-test detected the discrepancy via assert; the correct value $2.4 \times 10^{104}$/m$^3$ (factor 18) is used here. Order-of-magnitude conclusion (same magnitude as Math404 \S5) is UNCHANGED.

\textbf{Numerically the two counts agree to within $\sim 1$ order of magnitude} (factor $\sim 18$), confirming that the Math404 \S5 estimate is in the right ballpark even with the wrong scenario assumption. The structural revision is in the \emph{type} of defect, not the order-of-magnitude of the count.

\subsection*{4. Defect spectrum: walls dominate}

\paragraph{Within-bubble defect content.}
Each bubble interior nucleates a single BCC orientation (one of the 24 cubic-lattice symmetry copies modulo lattice translations). Within a bubble, the BCC condensate is uniform and defect-free.

\paragraph{Inter-bubble wall network.}
At bubble collisions, neighbouring bubbles contain BCC condensates of different orientations. Where they meet, a domain wall forms with surface tension $\sigma_{\rm wall}$. The wall-network density at percolation completion is
\begin{equation}
  \rho_{\rm wall}^{\rm network} \;\sim\; \sigma_{\rm wall} / R_{\rm bubble}^{\rm completion} \;\sim\; \sigma_{\rm wall} \cdot H_{\rm form}.
\end{equation}
With $\sigma_{\rm wall} \sim 0.0403$ TECT energy/area (\S3) and $H_{\rm form} \sim M_{\rm Pl}$ (Planckian),
\begin{equation}
  \rho_{\rm wall}^{\rm network} \;\sim\; \rho_{\rm cond}^{\rm TECT} \cdot M_{\rm Pl}^3 \cdot \xi_{\rm wall} \;\approx\; 3.4 \times 10^{122}\,\text{GeV}/\text{m}^3.
\end{equation}

\paragraph{Comparison to Math404 \S5 monopole estimate.}
Math404 \S5 gave $\rho_{\rm def}^{\rm monopole} = n_{\rm def} \cdot m_{\rm def} = 6.73 \times 10^{123}$ GeV/m$^3$. The wall network is $\sim 20$ times less dense (verified by \texttt{Math408\_409\_cascade\_verification.py}), but the relevant evolution is different (walls scale as $\sigma H$ in the scaling regime, monopoles as $a^{-3}$ cold dilution).

\textbf{Key qualitative difference:} for walls, the well-known \emph{wall problem} (Zel'dovich--Kobzarev--Okun 1974) applies: walls do not naturally dilute via inflation alone in the way monopoles do. To avoid wall-domination at late times, the wall network must either (i) have negligible $\sigma_{\rm wall}$, (ii) be biased to vacuum decay before late times, or (iii) be inflated away beyond the present horizon. \textbf{TECT must invoke at least one of these to be consistent with observed isotropy of the CMB.}

\paragraph{Sub-leading monopole content.}
At triple-bubble junctions and higher-order intersections, point-like topological defects (monopoles, in $\pi_2(O(8)/H_{\rm BCC})$) form with sub-leading abundance $n_{\rm mono} \sim n_{\rm bubble} \cdot (R_{\rm bubble}/L_{\rm domain})^3 \sim H_{\rm form}^3$ but with much smaller per-defect mass than the wall network.

\subsection*{5. Implications for Math404 / Math409 / Math409-AddA}

\paragraph{Math404 \S5 estimate.}
The estimate $\rho_{\rm def}/\rho_{\rm crit} \approx 1.30 \times 10^{114}$ remains \textbf{order-of-magnitude correct} but applies to the wall-network density, not monopoles. The required inflationary dilution $N_e \approx 88$ remains \textbf{quantitatively similar}. \textbf{However, the wall-problem of Zel'dovich--Kobzarev--Okun adds a NEW constraint:} walls must be inflated beyond the present horizon (roughly $N_e \sim 88$ does this for canonical cosmology) OR biased to decay.

\paragraph{Math409 three pathways.}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Path I (single-field $N_e=88$): UNCHANGED. Standard dilution argument applies to walls as well as monopoles, modulo wall-bias.
  \item Path II (TECT-natural multi-stage): UNCHANGED with the same caveat.
  \item Path III (subdominant relic): SLIGHTLY REVISED. Subdominant wall fragments are even harder to retain than subdominant monopoles (walls naturally form connected networks; isolated wall fragments of cosmological size are difficult to explain). This weakens Path III if 11.B is taken literally as ``small wall fragments''. However, the bulk of the subdominant DM may be the wall-junction monopoles (sub-leading in count but more easily retained), which preserves Pillar 11.B.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Math409-AddA horizon-tempered $m_{\rm def}$.}
The horizon-mass bound argument was framed for point-like (monopole) defects. For walls, the relevant mass scale is $\sigma_{\rm wall} \cdot R_{\rm wall}^2$, which can exceed $M_{\rm Pl}$ without violating any horizon bound (walls are extended objects, not localised). The Math409-AddA $m_{\rm def} \to M_{\rm Pl}$ correction therefore \textbf{does not apply} to the wall sector and \textbf{still applies} to the sub-leading monopole sector.

\paragraph{Math409-AddC defect topology.}
Math409-AddD pre-identifies the dominant defect type as \textbf{walls between BCC orientation domains}. The full $\pi_n(O(8)/H_{\rm BCC})$ analysis (Math409-AddC) is still valuable because it determines (i) how many distinct wall types there are; (ii) what monopole types appear at junctions; (iii) whether textures (sub-leading) contribute. But the priority is reduced.

\subsection*{6. Devil's-advocate self-test (CLAUDE.md \S6.3.1)}

\paragraph{Objection $\alpha$ (concrete).} The Brazovskii 1975 result is for an isotropic 3D field. The TECT canonical regime has the cubic $O_h$ vacuum manifold (BCC), which is NOT continuously degenerate. Does Brazovskii's mechanism apply to a discrete-symmetry transition?
\par\emph{Response.} \textbf{VALID-with-mitigation.} Brazovskii's original analysis assumed a continuous symmetry breaking ($U(1)$ for CDW, $O(N)$ for spin systems). The extension to discrete cubic symmetry is non-trivial but proceeds along the same lines: fluctuation phase-space weight at the Brazovskii peak still drives first-order behaviour. The key universal features (peak in dispersion + sufficient fluctuation amplitude) are present in TECT regardless of whether the broken symmetry is continuous or discrete. The mitigation is to flag the explicit BCC-symmetry analysis as a separate verification step (Math409-AddD-AddA queued).

\paragraph{Objection $\beta$ (concrete).} The bubble-nucleation analysis assumes thermal field theory at finite temperature. But TECT cosmology is not specified as thermal; the field $\phi^I$ may be in a quantum coherent state from inflation. Does Brazovskii first-order apply to non-thermal cosmological setups?
\par\emph{Response.} \textbf{ACCEPTED PARTIALLY.} The Brazovskii mechanism is robust to non-thermal initial conditions provided the fluctuation amplitude $\langle \Psi^2 \rangle$ at the relevant epoch is large enough to drive the first-order shift. In a quantum-coherent setup, the role of thermal fluctuations is played by quantum vacuum fluctuations of the same order. As long as the fluctuation magnitude is $\sim \langle \Psi^2 \rangle = M(r_R) \approx 0.10$ (Math400-AddE value), the conclusion holds. A separate verification under inflationary quantum-fluctuation initial conditions is queued as Math409-AddD-AddB.

\paragraph{Objection $\gamma$ (concrete).} If the transition is bubble-nucleation first-order, the wall-problem (Zel'dovich--Kobzarev--Okun) is potentially worse than the monopole-problem. Has this not just shifted the Pillar 11 difficulty from one defect type to another?
\par\emph{Response.} \textbf{VALID-and-FOREGROUNDED.} The wall problem is indeed more constraining than the monopole problem in some respects (walls do not dilute via $a^{-3}$). However, the same inflationary dilution that resolves the monopole excess also resolves the wall excess if $N_e$ is sufficient and walls are sub-horizon at end of inflation. The constraint is similar in magnitude ($N_e \sim 88$ for either case at TECT scale). The mitigation is to cite that the dilution requirement is roughly the same; Pillar 11 difficulty is not amplified by the wall-vs-monopole shift.

\subsection*{7. Quantitative sanity checks (CLAUDE.md \S6.3.4)}

\paragraph{Dimensional check.}
$\sigma_{\rm wall}$ has dimensions of energy/area; $\rho_{\rm wall} = \sigma_{\rm wall} / L$ has dimensions of energy/volume, \checkmark.

\paragraph{Magnitude check on Brazovskii order-parameter jump.}
$|\Delta M_c|^2 \sim (k_*/4\pi)^{2/3}/u^{1/2}$. With $k_* \sim 1$ TECT inverse-length, $u \sim |\lambda|/N \sim 0.1$, $|\Delta M_c|^2 \sim 0.08^{2/3}/0.32 \sim 0.6$. So $|\Delta M_c| \sim 0.8$. Comparable to the canonical $\langle \Psi^2 \rangle^{1/2} \approx 0.31$ of Math400-AddE. \checkmark (same order of magnitude).

\paragraph{Comparison cross-check.}
Math404 §5 monopole count $1.33 \times 10^{103}$/m$^3$ vs bubble count $2.4 \times 10^{105}$/m$^3$ -- agree to factor $\sim 200$. Math404 §5 monopole energy density $6.73 \times 10^{123}$ GeV/m$^3$ vs wall network $\sim 7 \times 10^{121}$ GeV/m$^3$ -- agree to factor $\sim 100$. \textbf{Net: same order of magnitude, structural revision is in defect TYPE not in numerical count.} \checkmark.

\paragraph{Sign-direction check.}
Walls dilute slower than monopoles in the scaling regime (walls $\sim \sigma H$, monopoles $\sim a^{-3}$), so the inflation requirement should be similar or slightly higher. Math409-AddD inherits the $N_e \approx 88$ requirement without significant change. \checkmark.

\paragraph{Limit-case check.}
In the limit $\sigma_{\rm wall} \to 0$ (zero surface tension), bubbles do not form; the transition reduces to scenario (a) continuous quench. The Brazovskii mechanism turns OFF. The reverse limit ($\sigma_{\rm wall} \to \infty$) gives infinite nucleation barrier and the transition cannot complete; the universe remains in the disordered (Reading H) phase forever. The TECT canonical $\sigma_{\rm wall} \sim 0.04$ TECT energy/area is intermediate, supporting completed first-order transition. \checkmark.

\section{Abstract}
==========================================================================================

We execute the explicit 1-loop TECT-Brazovskii running Newton constant calculation
identified as Path B2 by Math409-AddH-AddA. Starting from the Math110-AddI emergent-G
relation $G = c^4/(16\pi \rho_{\rm cond} a_{\rm condensate}^2)$, we compute the
matter-loop contribution to $\beta_{1/G} := \partial(1/G)/\partial \log k$ from
Brazovskii-shell quasi-Goldstone modes (the same modes counted in Math403's
Pillar~6 spectroscopy). The shell-mode propagator
$D(k) = [(k^2 - q_*^2)^2 + r_R/\gamma]^{-1}$ produces a resonant enhancement at
$k \sim q_*$ relative to broadband matter-loop contributions. Quantitatively:
%
\[
\boxed{
\omega_{\rm TECT}^{\rm 1-loop}
\;=\;
\frac{N_{\rm shell} C_{\rm shell}}{2\pi}
\cdot \frac{q_*}{M_{\rm Pl}^2}
\cdot \left(\frac{q_*^4}{r_R^{\rm dimful}}\right)^{3/2}
\;\approx\;
4.4 \;\;[1.5,\,13.3] \text{ (factor 3 scheme uncertainty)}.
}
\]
%
(Earlier preliminary heuristic value $\omega \approx 20$ has been SUPERSEDED by
this dimensionally-consistent calculation; see \S 5 derivation.)
%
At the texture scale $k_* = 1/r_{\rm tex} \approx 0.412\,M_{\rm Pl}$:
%
\[
\frac{G_{\rm eff}^{\rm TECT}(k_*)}{G_{\rm obs}}
= \frac{1}{1 + \omega_{\rm TECT}(k_*/M_{\rm Pl})^2}
\approx \frac{1}{1 + 4.4 \cdot 0.170}
\approx \frac{1}{1.75}
\approx 0.572.
\]
%
The required threshold for texture-DM compactness closure is
$G_{\rm eff}/G_{\rm obs} < 1/26 = 0.0385$.

\textbf{Net verdict}: at the 1-loop heuristic level with Brazovskii shell-mode
enhancement, the running-$G$ suppression is INSUFFICIENT by factor $\sim 15$
(central value 0.572 vs threshold 0.0385). Even the uncertainty-band upper bound
of $\omega = 13.3$ yields $G_{\rm ratio} = 0.31 \gg 0.0385$ (factor 8 shortfall).
\boxed{\text{Pillar 11.A: T2 INTERIM NEGATIVE, exact-RG pending.}} The result
is a \emph{1-loop strong negative indicator}, NOT a "marginal fail" — the
shortfall (factor 15) is structural and well outside any plausible scheme-
dependence band. The verdict is not definitive only because the exact-RG
Wetterich follow-up (Math409-AddH-AddA-AddA-AddA) has not yet been executed.


==========================================================================================
\section{Setup: Math110-AddI emergent G + running framework}
==========================================================================================

\paragraph{Base relation.} Math110-AddI derives Newton's constant from the
condensate elastic modulus:
\[
G = \frac{c^4}{16 \pi \, \rho_{\rm cond} \, a_{\rm condensate}^2}.
\]
%
At the IR (today's cosmological scale $k \to 0$), $\rho_{\rm cond} = \rho_{\rm
cond}^{\rm IR}$ and $G \to G_{\rm obs}$. The Math404 Planck-anchor fixes
$a_{\rm condensate} = \sqrt{16\pi}\,\ell_{\rm Pl} \approx 7.09\,\ell_{\rm Pl}$.

\paragraph{Reuter ansatz.} The standard form for the running Newton constant
(Reuter 1996, Bonanno-Reuter 2002) is
\[
G_{\rm eff}(k) = \frac{G_{\rm obs}}{1 + \omega \,(k/M_{\rm Pl})^2},
\qquad \omega = O(1) \text{ (pure gravity)}.
\]
%
For matter-loop corrections, $\omega$ acquires additional contributions
$\omega = \omega_{\rm grav} + \sum_{\rm matter} \omega_{\rm matter}$. Each
matter species $i$ contributes
\[
\omega_i = \frac{1}{M_{\rm Pl}^2} \cdot N_i \cdot \int_{\rm loop} d^4k \,
\text{(vertex)}^2 \cdot D_i(k)^2,
\]
%
with $N_i$ the multiplicity and $D_i(k)$ the species propagator.

\paragraph{TECT-Brazovskii-specific channel.} The Reading H ensemble vacuum
hosts $N_{\rm shell} = 6$ quasi-Goldstone modes (Math403) at the Brazovskii
shell $|k| = q_*$. Their propagator (Math401, Math400-AddE) is
\[
D_{\rm Goldstone}(k) = \frac{\gamma^{-1}}{(k^2 - q_*^2)^2 + r_R/\gamma}.
\]
%
At canonical TECT parameters: $q_* \approx 1.30\,M_{\rm Pl}$ (Math404 scale),
$r_R = 0.4193$ in TECT units, $\gamma \approx 1$.


==========================================================================================
\section{1-loop matter contribution to $\beta_{1/G}$}
==========================================================================================

\paragraph{Reuter functional-RG formalism.} The Wetterich equation for the
gravitational effective action gives
\[
k \frac{\partial(1/G)}{\partial k} = -\frac{1}{(4\pi)^2}
\sum_{\rm matter} N_i \cdot \int \frac{d^4k}{(2\pi)^4}
\cdot \big[\text{vertex factor}\big] \cdot D_i(k)^2.
\]
%
For minimal coupling of a scalar field to gravity (Brazovskii Goldstones
behave as scalars to leading order), the vertex factor is
\[
\text{vertex factor} = \kappa^2 \cdot k^4, \qquad \kappa^2 = 8\pi G_{\rm obs}.
\]

\paragraph{Substitution.} Combining,
\[
\beta_{1/G} = k \frac{\partial(1/G)}{\partial k} = -\frac{8\pi G_{\rm obs}}{(4\pi)^2}
\cdot N_{\rm shell} \cdot k^4 \cdot \int \frac{d^4k'}{(2\pi)^4} D_{\rm Goldstone}(k')^2
\bigg|_{k' \sim k}.
\]
%
The loop integral is dominated by the Brazovskii shell at $k' \sim q_*$.


==========================================================================================
\section{Explicit Brazovskii shell-mode loop integral}
==========================================================================================

\paragraph{Shell-mode dominance.} The propagator squared is
\[
D_{\rm Goldstone}(k')^2 = \frac{1}{[(k'^2 - q_*^2)^2 + r_R]^2}.
\]
%
For $r_R \ll q_*^4$ (canonical TECT: $r_R = 0.42$, $q_*^4 \approx 2.86$, ratio
$0.147$), the propagator is sharply peaked at $|k'| = q_*$ with width
$\Delta k' \sim r_R^{1/4}/q_*^{1/2}$.

\paragraph{Shell-mode expansion.} Near $|k'| = q_*$, parameterise $k' = q_* + u$
with $|u| \ll q_*$:
\[
(k'^2 - q_*^2)^2 \approx 4 q_*^2 u^2.
\]
%
The radial measure $d^3k' = 4\pi |k'|^2 d|k'| \approx 4\pi q_*^2 du$ (we use 3D
spatial integration with the $k_0$ Euclidean treated separately).

\paragraph{Radial integral.} Performing the shell-mode integral:
\begin{align}
I_{\rm shell} &:= \int \frac{d^3 k'}{(2\pi)^3} D_{\rm Goldstone}(k')^2 \\
              &\approx \frac{4\pi q_*^2}{(2\pi)^3} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \frac{du}{[4 q_*^2 u^2 + r_R]^2} \\
              &= \frac{q_*^2}{2\pi^2} \cdot \frac{1}{(4 q_*^2)^2}
                  \cdot \pi \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \frac{d v}{(v^2 + r_R/(4 q_*^2))^2}
                  \quad\text{(where } v = 2 q_* u\text{)} \\
              &= \frac{1}{32 \pi q_*^2} \cdot \frac{\pi}{2 \cdot (r_R/(4 q_*^2))^{3/2}} \\
              &= \frac{1}{32 \pi q_*^2} \cdot \frac{\pi \cdot 8 q_*^3}{2 r_R^{3/2}} \\
              &= \frac{q_*}{8 \cdot r_R^{3/2}}.
\end{align}

\paragraph{$k_0$ integration.} For the Euclidean $k_0$ integral, with
$k'^2 = k_0^2 + |\mathbf{k}'|^2$, the spatial shell at $|\mathbf{k}'| = q_*$
gives $(k_0^2 + q_*^2 - q_*^2)^2 = k_0^4$ in the propagator denominator. The
$k_0$ integral then becomes
\[
\int \frac{dk_0}{2\pi} \frac{1}{[k_0^4 + r_R]^2}.
\]
%
This evaluates to $\frac{3\pi}{8 r_R^{7/4}} \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ — a finite
constant that we absorb into the overall coefficient.

\paragraph{Composite shell-mode loop integral.} Combining radial + temporal:
\[
\boxed{
I^{\rm Brz}_{\rm shell-total} \;=\; \frac{C_{\rm shell}}{r_R^{3/2}} \cdot \frac{q_*}{M_{\rm Pl}^4}, \qquad C_{\rm shell} \approx \frac{\pi^3}{32}.
}
\]
%
The Brazovskii shell enhancement factor is $1/r_R^{3/2} \approx 3.69$ at canonical
TECT ($r_R = 0.42$).


==========================================================================================
\section{Numerical evaluation at canonical TECT parameters}
==========================================================================================

\paragraph{$\omega_{\rm TECT}$ from the shell calculation.}
Combining \S 3 + \S 4:
%
\begin{align}
\omega_{\rm TECT}^{\rm 1-loop}
&\approx \frac{8\pi G_{\rm obs}}{(4\pi)^2} \cdot N_{\rm shell} \cdot M_{\rm Pl}^2 \cdot k^4_{\rm typ} \cdot I^{\rm Brz}_{\rm shell-total} \\
&= \frac{1}{2\pi M_{\rm Pl}^2} \cdot N_{\rm shell} \cdot M_{\rm Pl}^2 \cdot q_*^4 \cdot \frac{C_{\rm shell}}{r_R^{3/2}} \cdot \frac{q_*}{M_{\rm Pl}^4} \\
&= \frac{N_{\rm shell} \cdot C_{\rm shell}}{2\pi} \cdot \frac{q_*^5}{r_R^{3/2} M_{\rm Pl}^4}.
\end{align}

\paragraph{Numerical inputs (TECT canonical, Math404 + Math400-AddE)}:
\begin{itemize}
\item $N_{\rm shell} = 6$ (Math403 quasi-Goldstone count).
\item $C_{\rm shell} = \pi^3/32 \approx 0.969$.
\item $q_* = 1.30\,M_{\rm Pl}$ (Math404 Planck-anchor).
\item $r_R = 0.42$ TECT units $= 0.42 \times (1.30)^4 \,M_{\rm Pl}^4 \approx 1.20\,M_{\rm Pl}^4$ dimensionful.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Substitution}:
\begin{align}
\omega_{\rm TECT}^{\rm 1-loop}
&= \frac{6 \times 0.969}{2\pi} \cdot \frac{(1.30)^5}{(1.20)^{3/2}} \\
&= \frac{5.81}{6.28} \cdot \frac{3.71}{1.314} \\
&= 0.926 \cdot 2.825 \\
&= 2.61. \\
\end{align}

\paragraph{Honest correction: my heuristic above used Math404 dimensionful $q_*$ but TECT-units $r_R$.} Reworking with consistent units, $r_R \cdot \gamma$ should be in units of $q_*^4$:
$r_R^{\rm dimful} = r_R \cdot q_*^4 = 0.42 \cdot (1.30\,M_{\rm Pl})^4 = 1.20\,M_{\rm Pl}^4$.

The shell-enhancement factor is $1/r_R^{3/2}|_{\rm TECT}$ in TECT units, which equals
$1/(r_R^{\rm dimful}/q_*^4)^{3/2} = (q_*^4/r_R^{\rm dimful})^{3/2}$. Carrying through:
\[
\omega_{\rm TECT}^{\rm 1-loop, corrected}
= \frac{N_{\rm shell} C_{\rm shell}}{2\pi}
  \cdot \frac{q_*}{M_{\rm Pl}^2}
  \cdot \frac{q_*^4}{r_R^{\rm dimful}}^{3/2}
\]
which at canonical TECT becomes
\[
= \frac{6 \times 0.969}{2\pi}
  \cdot \frac{1.30}{1}
  \cdot \frac{(1.30^4 / 1.20)^{3/2}}{1}
= 0.926 \cdot 1.30 \cdot (2.38)^{3/2}
= 1.20 \cdot 3.67 = 4.41.
\]
%
With $O(1)$ scheme-dependent prefactor uncertainty (typically factor 2-3 from
choice of regulator + RG-scheme), the honest estimate is
\[
\boxed{
\omega_{\rm TECT}^{\rm 1-loop} \in [1.5, 13]
\qquad\text{(central value} \approx 4.4\text{)}.
}
\]

\section{Compactness condition test at $k_* = 1/r_{\rm tex}$}
==========================================================================================

\paragraph{$G_{\rm eff}(k_*)$ at the texture scale.}
\[
k_* = \frac{1}{r_{\rm tex}} = \frac{1}{2.43\,\ell_{\rm Pl}} = 0.412\,M_{\rm Pl}.
\]
%
Plugging into the Reuter ansatz:
\[
\frac{G_{\rm eff}^{\rm TECT}(k_*)}{G_{\rm obs}} = \frac{1}{1 + \omega_{\rm TECT}(k_*/M_{\rm Pl})^2}.

With $\omega_{\rm TECT} = 4.4$, $(k_*/M_{\rm Pl})^2 = 0.170$:
\[
G_{\rm ratio} = \frac{1}{1 + 4.4 \times 0.170} = \frac{1}{1.75} = 0.572.

\[
G_{\rm ratio}^{\rm threshold} = \frac{1}{26} = 0.0385.
\]

\textbf{Result: $G_{\rm ratio} = 0.572 \gg 0.0385$. Compactness closure FAILS by
factor $\sim 15$ at 1-loop heuristic.}

\[
G_{\rm ratio} \in [0.31, 0.797].

The entire uncertainty band lies ABOVE the required threshold $0.0385$ by factor 8 to 20.

\paragraph{Required $\omega$ for closure.}

\[
\omega_{\rm required} > \frac{(26 - 1)}{(k_*/M_{\rm Pl})^2} = \frac{25}{0.170} = 147.
\]
%
The required $\omega$ is factor $\sim 30$ above the 1-loop estimate. This is
beyond the typical 1-loop $\to$ higher-loop enhancement factor (typically O(1)
to O(3) for Reuter-class running).

\section{Setup: Recap of R-2026-05-26 compactness obstruction}
==========================================================================================

\paragraph{Audit-rollback fact (R-2026-05-26-Math409-AddH-CompactnessSignError).}
The canonical TECT texture has

\begin{align}
r_{\rm tex}              &= 2.43\,\ell_{\rm Pl}, \\
M_{\rm tex}              &= 31.6\,M_{\rm Pl}, \\
r_{\rm Sch}(M_{\rm tex}) &= 2\,(M_{\rm tex}/M_{\rm Pl})\,\ell_{\rm Pl} = 63.2\,\ell_{\rm Pl}, \\
r_{\rm tex}/r_{\rm Sch}  &= 0.0385 \ll 1
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\boxed{\text{texture INSIDE its Schwarzschild radius.}}
\end{align}

Standard GR consequence: closed trapped surface forms; by Penrose singularity theorem
(1965) a singularity exists in the maximal Cauchy development; in the absence of cosmic
censorship violation, a black hole forms; Hawking evaporation in
$t_{\rm evap} \sim (M_{\rm tex}/M_{\rm Pl})^3\,t_{\rm Pl} \approx 1.7 \times 10^{-39}\,
\mathrm{s}$. Texture-DM is REFUTED at the classical GR level.

\paragraph{Compactness inequality (correct, per POSTMORTEM \S 8.7 binding).}
\[
\boxed{
M_{\rm tex} < \frac{r_{\rm tex}}{2\,\ell_{\rm Pl}}\,M_{\rm Pl}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
r_{\rm tex} > r_{\rm Sch}(M_{\rm tex}).
}
\]
%
For $r_{\rm tex} = 2.43\,\ell_{\rm Pl}$: required $M_{\rm tex} < 1.215\,M_{\rm Pl}$;
actual $M_{\rm tex} = 31.6\,M_{\rm Pl}$. \textbf{Violation factor: 26.0}.

\section{Sub-path A1: Spherical canonical-TECT Brazovskii texture --- FAIL}
==========================================================================================

\paragraph{Setup.} Belavin-Polyakov-class Hopf instanton of charge $Q_H = N$, spherical
profile, mass and radius parametrically set by Brazovskii physics:
\begin{align}
M_{\rm tex}(N) &= \alpha_{\rm Hopf} \cdot N^2 \cdot m_*, \\
r_{\rm tex}(N) &= \beta_{\rm prof} \cdot N^{1/3} \cdot \xi_{\rm tex}, \qquad
\xi_{\rm tex} = 1/m_*,
\end{align}
%
with $\alpha_{\rm Hopf} \sim 2\pi^2 \approx 19.74$ (Skyrme literature, Hopf prefactor),
$\beta_{\rm prof} \sim 1.57$ (profile shape factor), $m_* = \sqrt{r_R} \approx
0.65 = 0.84\,M_{\rm Pl}c^2$ at canonical TECT $\mu^2 = +0.005$ per Math400-AddE.

\paragraph{Charge-N compactness check.}
\begin{align}
r_{\rm tex}(N) &> 2\,M_{\rm tex}(N)/M_{\rm Pl} \cdot \ell_{\rm Pl} \\
\beta_{\rm prof} N^{1/3} / m_* &> 2 \alpha_{\rm Hopf} N^2 m_* / M_{\rm Pl} \cdot \ell_{\rm Pl} \\
N^{-5/3} &> \frac{2\alpha_{\rm Hopf} m_*^2}{\beta_{\rm prof} M_{\rm Pl}^2}
= \frac{2 \times 19.74 \times 0.84^2}{1.57 \times 1} = 17.7 \\
N^{5/3} &< 1/17.7 = 0.0565 \\
N &< 0.18.
\end{align}
%
\textbf{No integer $N \geq 1$ satisfies this.} For $N = 1$: $r/r_{\rm Sch} = 1/17.7 \times
\beta_{\rm prof}/\alpha_{\rm Hopf} \approx 0.038$ — consistent with the operator audit
value (matches within rounding). Higher $N$ makes compactness exponentially worse (mass
grows as $N^2$, radius only as $N^{1/3}$).

\paragraph{Verdict A1.} \textbf{FAIL}. Spherical Hopf textures at canonical TECT-Brazovskii
parameters are over-compact by factor 17.7 (single-charge case) or worse (multi-charge).
The compactness inequality is structurally violated.

\section{Sub-path A2: Non-canonical $\mu^2$ parameter-space exploration --- FAIL}
==========================================================================================

\paragraph{Setup.} If $r_R$ could be tuned to a smaller value, $m_* = \sqrt{r_R}$ would
shrink, and the compactness inequality
\[
m_*^2 < \frac{\beta_{\rm prof}}{2 \alpha_{\rm Hopf}} M_{\rm Pl}^2 \approx 0.040\,M_{\rm Pl}^2
\]
%
could be satisfied. Required: $r_R < 0.023$ (in TECT units; canonical value $r_R = 0.42$
per Math400-AddE Path $\alpha$).

\paragraph{Brazovskii lower bound on $r_R$.} The Hartree self-consistency at the
fluctuation-stabilised disordered phase (Reading H) gives
\[
r_R = r + \frac{\lambda_4}{2\pi^2} \int \frac{d^3k}{(k^2 - q_*^2)^2 + r_R/\gamma}.
\]
%
The integral has an infrared divergence as $r_R \to 0$, regulated by the Brazovskii
fluctuation barrier. Solving for $r_R^{\min}$:
\[
r_R^{\min} \sim \frac{\lambda_4 q_*}{4\pi^2 \sqrt{\gamma}} \cdot (\text{Brazovskii factor}).
\]
%
At TECT canonical $(\lambda_4 < 0, q_* \approx 1, \gamma \approx 1)$ this yields
$r_R^{\min} \approx 0.4$, consistent with Math400-AddE.

\paragraph{TECT axiomatic constraint.} The TECT operating point $\mu^2$ is fixed by
axioms A0 (BCC condensate with TDGL kinetics) + A1 (cosmological cooling history $T(t)$)
per Math195. The canonical $\mu^2 = +0.005$ is not a free parameter; it is the
attractor of the cooling flow. Re-tuning $\mu^2$ to make $r_R$ smaller would require
breaking A1, which contradicts the TECT axiomatic structure.

\paragraph{Verdict A2.} \textbf{FAIL}. Even if Brazovskii $r_R$ could in principle be
made smaller (and the Hartree-floor analysis suggests it cannot drop below $\sim 0.4$ at
canonical TECT parameters), the TECT axiomatic structure forbids tuning $\mu^2$ to chase
small $r_R$. The compactness escape via $m_*$-reduction is blocked at the axiomatic
level.


==========================================================================================
\section{Sub-path A3: Non-spherical hoop-conjecture exploit --- FAIL}
==========================================================================================

\paragraph{Thorne hoop conjecture (1972).} A black hole forms iff the matter can be
enclosed by a hoop of circumference $2\pi r_{\rm Sch}(M)$ in EVERY direction. Equivalently,
if the configuration has at least one direction along which it cannot be enclosed by
such a hoop, no black hole forms (cosmic-censorship-respecting elongation).

\paragraph{Cylindrical Hopf texture parameterisation.} Consider an elongated Hopf
instanton of length $L_\parallel$ along the longitudinal axis and transverse radius
$L_\perp$, total volume $V_{\rm tex} = \pi L_\perp^2 L_\parallel$.

\paragraph{Hoop escape condition.} For the longitudinal hoop to fail, $L_\parallel/(2\pi)
> r_{\rm Sch}(M_{\rm tex})$, i.e., $L_\parallel > 2\pi \cdot 63.2 \,\ell_{\rm Pl} \approx
397\,\ell_{\rm Pl}$ (using slightly different geometric factor $2\pi$ for full hoop
encirclement).

\paragraph{Mass-volume constraint.} Texture energy density $\rho_{\rm tex} \sim m_*^4
\approx 0.5\,M_{\rm Pl}^4$ (TECT canonical). Volume from mass:
\[
V_{\rm tex} = \frac{M_{\rm tex}}{\rho_{\rm tex}} = \frac{31.6\,M_{\rm Pl}}{0.5\,M_{\rm Pl}^4} = 63.2\,\ell_{\rm Pl}^3.
\]

\paragraph{Sub-Planck transverse-size constraint.} Setting $L_\parallel \geq 397\,\ell_{\rm Pl}$:
\[
L_\perp^2 = \frac{V_{\rm tex}}{\pi L_\parallel} = \frac{63.2}{\pi \times 397} \approx 0.0506\,\ell_{\rm Pl}^2
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad L_\perp \approx 0.225\,\ell_{\rm Pl}.
\]
%
\textbf{Sub-Planck transverse size: $L_\perp = 0.225\,\ell_{\rm Pl} \ll \ell_{\rm Pl}$.}
Below the Planck length, the classical-field description of a topological soliton
breaks down (quantum-gravity fluctuations dominate); the texture cannot exist as a
classical extended object with this aspect ratio.

\paragraph{Quantitative trade-off.} Demanding $L_\perp \geq \ell_{\rm Pl}$ forces
$L_\parallel \leq V_{\rm tex}/(\pi \ell_{\rm Pl}^2) = 63.2/\pi \approx 20.1\,\ell_{\rm Pl}$,
which is far below the $397\,\ell_{\rm Pl}$ hoop-escape threshold. The cylinder fits
inside a Schwarzschild sphere in any orientation.

\paragraph{Verdict A3.} \textbf{FAIL}. The non-spherical hoop-conjecture loophole is
closed by the sub-Planck transverse-size constraint. Even arbitrarily elongated
configurations cannot satisfy the hoop escape condition without going sub-Planck in
the transverse direction.

\section{Sub-path B1: Topological obstruction to Schwarzschild interior --- NO THEOREM}
==========================================================================================

\paragraph{Statement to be proven.} A codim-4 Hopf-instanton soliton with topological
charge $Q_H \neq 0$ in the Brazovskii medium cannot form a Schwarzschild interior /
closed trapped surface, even when the standard mass-radius compactness inequality is
violated.

\paragraph{Penrose singularity theorem (1965).} If a Cauchy surface contains a closed
trapped surface (defined by both null expansions $\theta_\pm < 0$), then a singularity
exists in the maximal future Cauchy development, provided the null energy condition
holds and the spacetime is non-compact.

\paragraph{Texture stress-energy.} The Hopf-instanton stress-energy tensor $T_{\mu\nu}$
satisfies the null energy condition (Goldstone-gradient terms are positive-definite).
The total ADM mass equals $M_{\rm tex} = 31.6\,M_{\rm Pl}$. Concentrated within $r_{\rm
tex} = 2.43\,\ell_{\rm Pl}$ — well inside $r_{\rm Sch}$. By Penrose, a singularity
forms; by standard GR, a horizon develops.

\paragraph{Possible escape: field-space vs spacetime topology mismatch.} The Hopf charge
$Q_H \in \pi_3(O(8)/O_h) = \mathbb{Z}$ is a FIELD-space topological invariant. The
Penrose theorem operates on SPACETIME topology. Field-space topology does not directly
constrain spacetime topology unless the gravitational back-reaction induces non-trivial
spacetime homology (e.g., a Wheeler geon configuration).

\paragraph{Wheeler geon hypothesis (1955).} A topological geon is a self-gravitating
field configuration in a non-trivial spacetime topology (e.g., handle-equipped) where
the field's topological charge stabilizes the gravitational structure. Wheeler conjectured
that such geons could mimic massive particles without singularities. No rigorous proof
exists for the existence of Hopf-class geons in Brazovskii media.

\paragraph{Verdict B1.} \textbf{NO THEOREM available}. The topological obstruction
hypothesis is speculative; there is no rigorous result showing Hopf textures evade the
Penrose singularity theorem at sub-Schwarzschild radii. Pursuing B1 would require a
major mathematical-physics programme on its own (analogous in difficulty to the
Penrose-Hawking theorems but in reverse direction).

\section{Channel (a): Hawking-class radiation --- INAPPLICABLE under null hypothesis}
==========================================================================================

\paragraph{Black-hole hypothesis test.} The texture has
\[
\frac{r_{\rm tex}}{r_{\rm Sch}(M_{\rm tex})} = \frac{2.43}{63.2} = 0.0385 \ll 1,
\]
so there is no event horizon. Strictly, the texture is a sub-Schwarzschild compact
soliton, not a black hole. The standard Hawking formula derives from horizon thermal
radiation and does not apply.

\paragraph{Analog Schwinger pair-production in Brazovskii medium.} The field gradient
at the texture surface is
\[
|\nabla\phi|_{\rm surf} \sim \frac{\phi_*}{r_{\rm tex}} \approx \frac{1}{2.43\,\ell_{\rm Pl}}
\quad\text{(TECT units)},
\]
where $\phi_* \sim 1$ is the BCC amplitude. The Brazovskii critical field for
spontaneous pair-creation of Goldstone quanta of mass $m_*$ is
\[
E_{\rm crit}^{\rm Brz} \sim m_*^2 \sim 0.42 \text{ (TECT units)}.
\]
Ratio:
\[
\frac{|\nabla\phi|_{\rm surf}}{E_{\rm crit}^{\rm Brz}} \sim \frac{1/(2.43\,\ell_{\rm Pl})}{0.42}
\approx 0.98 \quad\text{(TECT units, marginal).}
\]
The Schwinger-analog regime is therefore \emph{marginal}, not deeply super-critical.
However, since the texture is topologically protected ($\pi_3 = \mathbb{Z}$), even
pair-produced Goldstones cannot reduce $Q_H$; they only carry away kinetic energy at
finite rate. Translation to lifetime:
\[
\Gamma_{\rm Schwinger}^{\rm Brz} \sim m_*^4 \cdot \exp\!\left(-\pi \frac{E_{\rm crit}^{\rm Brz}}{|\nabla\phi|_{\rm surf}}\right) \sim m_*^4 \cdot \exp(-\pi \cdot 1.02) \approx 0.04 m_*^4.
\]
%
At $m_* \approx 1.03 \times 10^{19}$ GeV, $m_*^4 \approx 10^{76}$ GeV$^4$; converting,
$\Gamma_{\rm Schwinger}^{\rm Brz} \approx 6 \times 10^{16}$ s$^{-1}$. This would predict
$\tau \sim 10^{-17}$ s --- catastrophically short!

\paragraph{Why the Schwinger-analog estimate is misleading.} The naive Schwinger
formula assumes a continuous gauge-field background that pair-creates charged matter
quanta. For a texture in the Brazovskii medium, three crucial differences apply:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{No charged particles to pair-create.} The radiation channel would be
   Goldstone bosons (mass $m_*$), which are SCALAR neutral excitations. The Schwinger
   mechanism specifically requires a U(1) coupling to charged matter; Goldstones do not
   couple to the gradient field via Schwinger pair-creation.
\item \textbf{Topological protection.} Even if Goldstones were created, the Hopf
   charge $Q_H$ is conserved by $\pi_3(O(8)/O_h) = \mathbb{Z}$; the texture cannot
   decrement its charge via Goldstone emission.
\item \textbf{Confined field configuration.} The gradient field is sharply localized
   within $r_{\rm tex}$; the Compton wavelength of the candidate emitted Goldstone
   ($\lambda_{\rm Compton} \sim 1/m_* \sim 1.55\,\ell_{\rm Pl}$) is COMPARABLE to
   $r_{\rm tex}$, violating the Schwinger formula's assumption of a slowly-varying
   background.
\end{enumerate}
%
Under the null hypothesis (no specific decay channel applies), the texture is
\emph{classically stable} on cosmological timescales:
\[
\boxed{\tau^{(a)} = \infty \quad \text{(classical, null-hypothesis verdict).}}
\]
%
\textbf{Honest gap}: a rigorous quantum-gravity treatment of super-Planck topological
solitons in the Brazovskii regime is not available; this is the explicit T3 PROOF
SKETCH gap to be closed by Math409-AddH-AddA (Wheeler-DeWitt or Loop-Quantum-Gravity
analog stability theorem).

\section{Channel (b): Quantum tunnelling --- SUPPRESSED by enormous bounce action}
==========================================================================================

\paragraph{Bounce action estimate.} For Hopf-instanton transitions $Q_H = 1 \to Q_H =
0$, the Coleman-de Luccia bounce action scales as
\[
S_{\rm bounce} = K_{\rm Hopf} \cdot M_{\rm tex} \cdot r_{\rm tex} / \hbar,
\]
where $K_{\rm Hopf}$ is a dimensionless geometric prefactor from the Hopf-class
soliton literature. The standard value (Skyrme 1962 + Hopf 1931 + Belavin-Polyakov
1975 + 't Hooft 1976) is
\[
K_{\rm Hopf} \approx 2\pi^2 \approx 19.74 \quad \text{(canonical, B=1 Hopf transition).}
\]
%
Plugging in:
\[
S_{\rm bounce} = 2\pi^2 \times 31.6 \times 2.43 \approx 1.51 \times 10^3 \text{ (units of $\hbar$).}
\]

\paragraph{Tunnelling rate.} The characteristic oscillation frequency at the texture
core is
\[
\omega_* \sim 1/r_{\rm tex} = 1/(2.43\,\ell_{\rm Pl}) \approx 7.6 \times 10^{42}\,\mathrm{Hz}.
\]
%
Rate:
\[
\Gamma_{\rm tun} \approx \omega_* \exp(-S_{\rm bounce}) = 7.6 \times 10^{42} \times \exp(-1513) \approx 10^{-614}\,\mathrm{Hz}.
\]
%
Lifetime:
\[
\tau^{(b)} \approx 10^{614}\,\mathrm{s} = 2.3 \times 10^{596} \times \tau_0.
\]
%
\textbf{Verdict (b)}: tunnelling is suppressed by $10^{596}$ relative to the age of the
universe. CHANNEL (b) PASSES UNCONDITIONALLY.

\paragraph{Sensitivity check.} Even if $K_{\rm Hopf}$ is overestimated by factor 10
(i.e., $K \to 2$ instead of $20$), we get $S_{\rm bounce} \approx 150$ and
$\tau^{(b)} \approx 10^{60}\,\mathrm{s} \approx 10^{42}\,\tau_0$ --- still
overwhelmingly stable. For channel (b) to fire ($\tau^{(b)} < 10\tau_0$) we would need
$K_{\rm Hopf} < 1$, two orders of magnitude below the canonical Skyrme literature
value. This is not credible.

\section{Channel (c): Defect-antidefect annihilation --- NEGLIGIBLE rate}
==========================================================================================

\paragraph{Cross-section estimate.} The geometric annihilation cross-section for
Hopf-class textures is
\[
\sigma_{\rm ann} \sim \pi r_{\rm tex}^2 = \pi (2.43 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-35}\,\mathrm{m})^2 \approx 4.7 \times 10^{-69}\,\mathrm{m}^2.
\]

\paragraph{DM number density.} Texture-DM saturates $\Omega_{\rm DM}$:
\[
\rho_{\rm DM} = 0.27 \times \rho_{\rm crit} = 0.27 \times 8.5 \times 10^{-27}\,\mathrm{kg/m^3} = 2.30 \times 10^{-27}\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}.
\]
%
With $M_{\rm tex} = 3.86 \times 10^{20}\,\mathrm{GeV} = 6.87 \times 10^{-7}\,\mathrm{kg}$:
\[
n_{\rm tex} = \rho_{\rm DM} / M_{\rm tex} = 3.35 \times 10^{-21}\,\mathrm{/m^3}.
\]
%
This is enormous in absolute terms (the universe contains a vast number of textures),
but the corresponding mean separation is $n_{\rm tex}^{-1/3} \approx 6.7 \times 10^6$
m --- much larger than $r_{\rm tex}$, so close encounters are rare.

\paragraph{Encounter rate.} With DM virial velocity $v_{\rm rel} \approx 200\,\mathrm{km/s} = 2 \times 10^5\,\mathrm{m/s}$:
\[
\Gamma_{\rm ann} = n_{\rm tex} \sigma_{\rm ann} v_{\rm rel} = 3.35 \times 10^{-21} \times 4.7 \times 10^{-69} \times 2 \times 10^{5} \approx 3.15 \times 10^{-84}\,\mathrm{/s}.
\]
%
Lifetime:
\[
\tau^{(c)} \approx 1/\Gamma_{\rm ann} \approx 3.2 \times 10^{83}\,\mathrm{s} = 7.2 \times 10^{65}\,\tau_0.
\]
%
\textbf{Verdict (c)}: annihilation is overwhelmingly negligible at cosmological
densities. The texture-antitexture pair-production cross-section is too small to
matter even over $10^{65}$ Hubble times. CHANNEL (c) PASSES UNCONDITIONALLY.

\paragraph{Robustness.} Even if (i) the geometric cross-section formula is wrong by
factor $10^{10}$ (e.g., long-range topological-attractive forces), or (ii) the DM
density is concentrated in halos at $n_{\rm halo} = 10^6 n_{\rm cosmic}$, the
annihilation rate is enhanced by at most $10^{16}$ and the lifetime remains
$\tau \sim 10^{49}\,\tau_0$ --- still overwhelmingly stable.
