\paragraph{Objection $\beta$ (Math82-AddF $m^{*2}$ measurement might have been performed in pre-Math401 framework, hence invalid under Reading H)}.

\textsc{Response: DISMISSED at the operational-channel level}. The Math82-AddF Newton-Krylov continuation computes the Hessian eigenvalue at the converged field configuration. The pre/post-Math401 distinction is in the INTERPRETATION of what the configuration represents (``BCC ground state'' vs ``BCC channel within Reading H disordered vacuum''); the channel-curvature OBSERVABLE is operationally invariant under the channel-identification prescription, while the full Hessian spectrum need not be identical. \paragraph{Objection $\gamma$ (Spectral gap calculation may have shell-coupling artefacts not captured in pre-Math401 framing)}.

As $r_R \to \infty$ (deep Brazovskii regime), $\lambda_{\min} \to \infty$, recovering massive-mode limit. PASS limit-case.

\paragraph{Check 4 (sign-direction)}. Reading H requires $r_R > 0$ for vacuum stability (Math400-AddE Path $\alpha$). Pillar 2 derivation requires $\lambda_{\min} > 0$ for channel stability. Both signs are consistent with same physical regime ($r_R$ and $\lambda_{\min}$ both positive in Reading H regime). PASS sign-direction.

\section{Abstract}
==========================================================================================

Pillar 3 in the canonical 11-pillar scoreboard (Math411-AddB §10 C1/C2/C3 reclassification) is labeled \textbf{T5 CLOSED@1-loop}. The T5 status is the strongest CLOSED-at-perturbative-order tier; it is honest, but it explicitly records that the closure is at first perturbative order only and that higher-loop or non-perturbative completion is open. This note audits two questions:

\begin{enumerate}
\item Does the T5@1-loop label survive the 2026-05-11 Reading H reformulation? (Answer: \textbf{YES} — Reading H operates at the vacuum/condensate level; Pillar 3's spin-2 emergent-graviton sector is built on the TT-projected fluctuation Hessian which is unaffected by the vacuum reinterpretation.)
\item What technical work would promote Pillar 3 from T5 → T6 (CLOSED@2-loop conditional) or T5 → T7 (unconditional)? (Answer: T5 → T6 via 2-loop extension of either Math200-AddC §2 ℏ_TECT matching (path A) or Math41 emergent-graviton sector (path B); T5 → T7 via Wetterich exact-RG asymptotic-safety analysis (long-tail axiom extension).)
\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{Key audit findings}.

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{T5@1-loop label is currently the correct honest tier.} Pillar 3's core results — Math41 (κ_G² = Y q_0², TT-purity), Math110-AddH (c_T = c identification), Math200-AddC §2 (ℏ_TECT matching scale-coherence at $M_Z$) — are all 1-loop results. No 2-loop work has been performed.

\item \textbf{Reading H reformulation does NOT touch Pillar 3.} The emergent-graviton sector is the TT (transverse-traceless) part of the fluctuation Hessian around the condensate. Reading H reframes ``the condensate'' (BCC ground state $\to$ BCC channel within Brazovskii disordered vacuum) but does NOT modify the TT-projected sub-Hessian. \paragraph{Audit verdict (operator-binding revision 2026-05-27)}. The previous T7-retained interpretation is superseded. Pillar 9 is classified as a \textbf{T6/T7-SPLIT}: the functional relation $\hbar = c^3 a_{\rm BCC}^2/(16\pi G)$ is retained as a high-tier theorem, the Math404 scale identification is non-circular, and the \emph{independent} numerical prediction of $G$ remains OPEN. The Math404 dependence is a \emph{scale identification}, not a circular derivation. Specifically:

\begin{enumerate}
\item Pillar 9 derives the FUNCTIONAL FORM $\hbar = c^3 a_{\rm BCC}^2 / (16\pi G)$ from TECT-internal physics (Math110-AddI master relation; Math41 emergent-graviton sector; Math110-AddH $c_T = c$ identification). This derivation does NOT use any external numerical input for $G$, $\hbar$, or $c$ — it produces a relation between TECT-internal $a_{\rm BCC}$ and the three physical constants.

\item Math404 INVERTS this relation: given observed CODATA $(\hbar, c, G)$, solve for $a_{\rm BCC}$. The result is $a_{\rm BCC} = \sqrt{16\pi G \hbar / c^3} = \sqrt{16\pi}\,\ell_{\rm Pl} = 7.09\,\ell_{\rm Pl}$. The combinatorial factor $\sqrt{16\pi}$ is independently derived from Math110-AddG elastic-modulus calculation (NOT fitted).

\item The dependence structure is therefore: \emph{TECT internal physics $\to$ functional form (Pillar 9 PROVED) $\to$ numerical scale via CODATA invert (Math404 IDENTIFICATION, single combinatorial factor verified).}

\item This is structurally analogous to Einstein's GR: GR's functional form $R_{\mu\nu} - \frac{1}{2}g_{\mu\nu}R = 8\pi G T_{\mu\nu}$ is derived from differential-geometric principles; the value of $G = 6.674 \times 10^{-11}\,\text{m}^3 \text{kg}^{-1} \text{s}^{-2}$ is identified from external measurement. \textbf{However (operator-binding revision 2026-05-27), the previous ``by the same standard, Pillar 9 is T7 PROVED'' inference is withdrawn}: the structural analogy with GR does not by itself substantiate an independent prediction of $G$ from TECT-internal axioms. The Math404 inversion is algebraically consistent with the $\sqrt{16\pi}$ factor, but it is not an independent derivation of $G$ or of $a_{\rm BCC}$.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Logical structure of Pillar 9 derivation chain}
==========================================================================================

\paragraph{Step 1 (Math41): emergent gravitational coupling $\kappa_G^2 = Y q_0^2$}.

The TT-projected fluctuation Hessian around the BCC channel produces a spin-2 graviton propagator with coupling $\kappa_G^2 = Y q_0^2$, where $Y$ is the Brazovskii stiffness and $q_0 = 2\pi / a_{\rm BCC}$ is the spectral-minimum wavenumber. This is internal TECT physics; no external input.

\paragraph{Step 2 (Math110-AddG): elastic-modulus derivation}.

The Brazovskii stiffness $Y$ is computed from the elastic-modulus calculation. The combinatorial factor $\sqrt{16\pi}$ (or $16\pi$ in $Y q_0^2$) arises from the integration over the spherical-shell measure in the elastic-modulus integral. This is internal TECT physics; the factor $16\pi$ is calculated, not fitted.

\paragraph{Step 3 (Math110-AddH): $c_T = c$ identification}.

The TECT transverse-phonon speed $c_T$ is identified with the speed of light $c$ via Pillar 2 (Math97) universality-class membership. This is a relation between two TECT-internal speeds (Brazovskii Goldstone mode speed and the emergent metric speed); structurally enforced, not external input.

\paragraph{Step 4 (Math110-AddI): master relation $\hbar = c^3 a_{\rm BCC}^2 / (16\pi G)$}.

Combining Steps 1-3 with the canonical commutation relation $[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$ derived from the Brazovskii path integral, the master relation emerges. The form is fully TECT-internal; the symbols $\hbar, c, G$ on the right-hand side denote the EXPECTED physical quantities that TECT predicts, not external numerical inputs.

\paragraph{Step 5 (Math404): scale identification via CODATA invert}.

Given observed CODATA $(\hbar, c, G)$, solve Step 4 for $a_{\rm BCC}$:

\[
a_{\rm BCC} = \sqrt{16\pi G \hbar / c^3} = \sqrt{16\pi}\,\ell_{\rm Pl} \approx 7.09\,\ell_{\rm Pl} \approx 1.146 \times 10^{-34}\,\text{m}.
\]

The result $a_{\rm BCC} = \sqrt{16\pi}\,\ell_{\rm Pl}$ matches the Math110-AddG combinatorial-factor prediction \emph{exactly}. The multiplicative factor $\sqrt{16\pi}$ arises both from the elastic-modulus integral (Math110-AddG, TECT-internal) and from the Math404 CODATA invert; the two share the same $16\pi$ algebraic content (Math110-AddG gives the form; Math404 inversion uses the form). Per the operator-binding revision (2026-05-27), this is \emph{algebraic consistency} of the same $16\pi$ factor across two derivations of the same functional form, \textbf{not} two independent numerical determinations of $G$ from disjoint inputs.

\paragraph{What is conditional, what is unconditional}:

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{High-tier theorem (T6, conditional on upstream Math41 / Math110-AddG / Math110-AddH / Math110-AddI hypotheses)}: the FUNCTIONAL FORM $\hbar = c^3 a_{\rm BCC}^2 / (16\pi G)$ (Math110-AddI). The combinatorial factor $16\pi$ is derived from the elastic-modulus integral (Math110-AddG). Per the operator-binding revision (2026-05-27), the previous T7-unconditional labelling of the functional relation is retained \emph{only at the functional-relation level} (sub-claim (i) of the T6/T7-SPLIT); independent prediction of $G$ from TECT-internal axioms (sub-claim (iii)) remains OPEN.

\item \textbf{Conditional (single scale identification, not propagating)}: $a_{\rm BCC} = \sqrt{16\pi}\,\ell_{\rm Pl}$ value (Math404). This is one number, fixed by CODATA $(\hbar, c, G)$ measurement and consistency with Math110-AddG. The conditional aspect is the choice to use CODATA values for scale-fixing rather than (e.g.) other measurement convention.
\end{itemize}

This conditional-vs-unconditional split is consistent with standard physics practice. Quantum field theory has the same structure: functional forms are unconditional (gauge-symmetry-derived); coupling constants are measured (conditional on measurement convention).

\section{Quantitative sanity checks (CLAUDE.md §6.3.4)}

\paragraph{Check 1 (dimensional)}. $\hbar = c^3 a_{\rm BCC}^2 / (16\pi G)$: dim = $[\text{m/s}]^3 \cdot [\text{m}]^2 / [\text{m}^3 \text{kg}^{-1} \text{s}^{-2}] = [\text{m}^3 \text{s}^{-3}] \cdot [\text{m}^2] \cdot [\text{m}^{-3} \text{kg s}^2] = [\text{m}^2 \text{kg s}^{-1}] = [\text{J} \cdot \text{s}]$. PASS dimensional.

\paragraph{Check 2 (magnitude)}. CODATA values: $\hbar = 1.0546 \times 10^{-34}\,\text{J} \cdot \text{s}$, $c = 2.998 \times 10^8\,\text{m/s}$, $G = 6.674 \times 10^{-11}\,\text{m}^3 \text{kg}^{-1} \text{s}^{-2}$. Compute $a_{\rm BCC} = \sqrt{16\pi G \hbar / c^3}$:

\[
a_{\rm BCC} = \sqrt{16\pi \cdot 6.674 \times 10^{-11} \cdot 1.0546 \times 10^{-34} / (2.998 \times 10^8)^3} = \sqrt{16\pi \cdot 2.61 \times 10^{-70}} \approx 1.146 \times 10^{-34}\,\text{m}.
\]

Comparison with $\sqrt{16\pi} \ell_{\rm Pl} = \sqrt{16\pi} \cdot 1.616 \times 10^{-35} = 7.09 \cdot 1.616 \times 10^{-35} = 1.146 \times 10^{-34}\,\text{m}$. PASS magnitude.

\paragraph{Check 3 (limit case)}. As $a_{\rm BCC} \to \ell_{\rm Pl}$, $\hbar \to c^3 \ell_{\rm Pl}^2 / (16\pi G) = (\hbar G/c^3) \cdot c^3 / (16\pi G) = \hbar / (16\pi)$, which is dimensionally consistent but off by $16\pi$ factor — confirming $a_{\rm BCC} = \sqrt{16\pi}\,\ell_{\rm Pl}$ is the unique value satisfying $\hbar$ self-consistency. PASS limit-case.

\paragraph{Check 4 (sign-direction)}. $a_{\rm BCC} > 0$ required (physical length); $\hbar, c, G > 0$ (physical constants). PASS sign-direction.

\paragraph{Check 5 (POSTMORTEM §8.7 Schwarzschild compactness)}. N/A.

\paragraph{Check 6 (POSTMORTEM §8.8 same-session cross-audit)}. Math417 inherits Math41 + Math110-AddG + Math110-AddH + Math110-AddI + Math404 + Math415 + Math416 anchors. Cross-audit verified.

\paragraph{Check 7 (numerical reproducibility)}. Verification script \texttt{Codes/supplementary/Math417\_pillar9\_audit.py} with 6 self-test asserts.

\paragraph{Objection $\alpha$ (CONCRETE: the 4-sector cancellation might be a coincidence, not a structural theorem)}.

\textsc{Response: VALID-with-mitigation}. Each sector cancellation has a different mathematical mechanism: monopole/vortex via CP-pairing of Yang-Mills vacuum-energy functional; BCC via Casimir-type vanishing on periodic box; Dirac via PV-regularised zero-point absorption. The four mechanisms are NOT unified at a single recursive root. The cancellation is \emph{additive over the 4 sectors} with each sector arguing for its own vanishing by its own argument. This is more fragile than a single symmetry-driven cancellation; it is also more typical of real physical $\Lambda$-cancellation programmes (cf.\ SUSY cancellation distributes across boson/fermion separately). The T6 PROVED CONDITIONAL label honestly captures the conditional nature.

\paragraph{Objection $\beta$ (CONCRETE: Math58 cascade predates Reading H; reframing the BCC condensate as a fluctuation channel may invalidate the BCC-sector Casimir argument)}.

\textsc{Response: UPHELD --- explicit OPEN gate}. The BCC-sector closure (v5) argues that the BCC condensate vacuum energy renormalises to zero by Casimir vanishing on the periodic box. Under Reading H, the ``BCC vacuum'' is no longer a condensate but a fluctuation channel within Brazovskii-stabilised disordered vacuum. The Casimir argument may or may not survive this reframing; pre-Reading-H proof methodology assumed condensate vacuum periodicity. \textbf{Math420-AddB is queued} to verify Reading H compatibility of the v5 BCC Casimir argument before promotion can be substantiated.

\paragraph{Objection $\gamma$ (CONCRETE: Math58-v7-AddC's title says ``unified closure'' and the file is labelled ``PROVED CONDITIONAL'' --- shouldn't this be the Pillar 8 anchor?)}.

\textsc{Response: DISMISSED --- close-read confirms different content}. Math58-v7-AddC's full title is ``Canonical commutation relations: unified closure via Dirac sector + CP measure + algebraic monopole cancellation''. The ``unified closure'' refers to the closure of CANONICAL COMMUTATION RELATIONS using the $\Lambda$-cascade machinery as INPUT, NOT the closure of the $\Lambda$-cancellation itself. Reading the file body confirms: H1, H2, H3 are quantum-structure hypotheses (canonical commutation relations $[h(x), \pi(y)] = i\hbar \delta(x-y)$ closure), not $\Lambda$-cancellation hypotheses. Math58-v7-AddC belongs to sub-chain (d) (quantum-structure) per Math420 §6 Step 1 classification, NOT to sub-chain (a) (Λ-suppression).

\section{Abstract}
==========================================================================================

This addendum executes the critical OPEN gate from Math420-AddA: verification that the 4-sector $\Lambda$-suppression cascade located in Math58 (v3 monopole + v4-sublemma vortex + v5 BCC + v7-Dirac-tightening) survives the Reading H reframing established by Math401 and Math400-AddE. The 4 sector arguments are analysed individually for their dependence on the pre-Reading-H assumption ``$\Psi_0$ = BCC condensate vacuum'' versus the post-Reading-H assumption ``$\Psi_0$ = disordered (uniform-zero) classical configuration; BCC structure as fluctuation channel at $|q| = q_*$ with Brazovskii fluctuation-induced effective mass $r_R = +0.4193$''.

\paragraph{Per-sector verdicts}.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Sector 1 (Monopole, Math58-v3 CP-measure)}: \textbf{PASS}. The argument operates at the level of Yang-Mills action CP-invariance, path-integral measure CP-invariance, topological-charge-density CP-oddness, and a functional-integral change-of-variables identity. \item \textbf{Sector 2 (Vortex, Math58-v4-sublemma Chern-Simons CP)}: \textbf{PASS}. All steps are at the topological / operator-algebra level on the gauge sector and are independent of the scalar vacuum. Reading H reframing does not affect any step. Status: same as Sector 1.

\item \textbf{Sector 3 (BCC, Math58-v5 Casimir vanishing)}: \textbf{PASS-CONDITIONAL on Math420-AddC reformulation}. \section{Reading H reframing — formal summary (Math401 + Math400-AddE Path $\alpha$)}
==========================================================================================

\paragraph{Pre-Reading-H (Reading F)}: The TECT vacuum is the BCC condensate, a classical minimum $\Psi_0^{\rm BCC}$ of the Brazovskii functional at $\mu^2 = +5 \times 10^{-3}$. Fluctuations $\delta\Psi$ are quantised around $\Psi_0^{\rm BCC}$; defect sectors (monopoles, vortices, Dirac zero modes) live on the BCC condensate background.

\paragraph{Post-Reading-H (Math401 binding 2026-05-12)}: The TECT vacuum is the \emph{Brazovskii fluctuation-stabilised disordered phase} (Math400-AddE Path $\alpha$ confirmed at 16/16 sweep points). The classical configuration is $\Psi_0 = 0$ (uniform zero); fluctuations $\delta\Psi$ self-consistently generate an effective mass $r_R = +0.4193 > 0$ through the one-loop self-consistency equation
\[
r_R = r_{\rm bare} + \tfrac{1}{2} u \int \frac{d^3 q}{(2\pi)^3} \frac{1}{r_R + \kappa(q^2 - q_*^2)^2 + \dots}\,.
\]
The BCC ``structure'' exists only at the \emph{channel level}: the momentum-space content $|q| = q_*$ is preferentially populated by fluctuations (peak of the Brazovskii spectral shell), but no symmetry-breaking condensate exists at classical level. Math400-AddF further verified that at canonical $\mu^2 = +5 \times 10^{-3}$, the BCC configuration is a TRUE LOCAL MINIMUM (not global), with FCC revealing SADDLE-6 structure and HEX a local minimum.

\paragraph{Key kinematic substitution under Reading H}: Wherever a Math58 cascade argument invokes ``$\Psi_0 = \Psi^{\rm BCC}$, fluctuations $\delta\Psi$ around it'' and computes physical observables (e.g., 1-loop Hessian, defect spectrum, vacuum energy), the Reading H prescription is:

\begin{enumerate}
\item Replace $\Psi_0^{\rm BCC} \to \Psi_0 = 0$ at the classical level.
\item Replace the bare mass $r \to r_R = +0.4193$ (Brazovskii-induced effective mass) wherever it appears in the IR / mass-shell sector of the 1-loop integrand.
\item Replace the BCC-channel-population claim ``classical condensate at $|q| = q_*$ with amplitude $A_0$'' by ``fluctuation amplitude $\langle |\delta\Psi(q_*)|^2 \rangle$ generated dynamically by Brazovskii self-consistency''.
\item Defect sectors (monopoles, vortices, Dirac zero modes) are reinterpreted as topological defects of the FLUCTUATION FIELD on the disordered vacuum, not as defects of the CLASSICAL CONDENSATE.
\end{enumerate}

The Reading H invariance test for each sector cancellation argument reduces to: \emph{does the argument's load-bearing step survive substitution (1)--(4)?}

\section{Sector 1 (Monopole) Reading H compatibility analysis}
==========================================================================================

\paragraph{Math58-v3 cancellation argument structure (recap)}.

The Math58-v3 argument proves the CP-odd transformation of the vacuum-energy functional on the monopole sector of Yang-Mills theory. The four load-bearing steps are:

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{CP-invariance of the Yang-Mills action} (v3 Lemma, line 273): $S_{\rm YM}[A_\mu] = S_{\rm YM}[(CP \cdot A)_\mu]$ where $(CP \cdot A)_\mu$ is the CP-transformed gauge potential. Proof: the Yang-Mills action depends only on the field strength $F_{\mu\nu}$ via $\mathrm{tr}(F_{\mu\nu} F^{\mu\nu})$, which is invariant under CP.

\item \textbf{CP-invariance of the path-integral measure} (v3 Lemma, line 321): $\mathcal{D}[A] = \mathcal{D}[CP \cdot A]$. Proof: the gauge-field measure is a translation-invariant measure on the gauge configuration space; CP induces a bijective measure-preserving map.

\item \textbf{CP-odd transformation of the topological charge density} (v3 Lemma, line 357): $Q_{\rm top}[CP \cdot A] = - Q_{\rm top}[A]$ where $Q_{\rm top} = \tfrac{1}{32\pi^2} \int d^4x\,\epsilon^{\mu\nu\rho\sigma} \mathrm{tr}(F_{\mu\nu} F_{\rho\sigma})$. Proof: $\epsilon$ tensor and $F \wedge F$ pseudoscalar property under parity.

\item \textbf{Vacuum-energy sign-flip} (v3 Theorem, line 558): combining the three lemmas yields $V_{\rm vac}^{\rm monopole}(\theta) = -V_{\rm vac}^{\rm monopole}(-\theta)$, hence $V_{\rm vac}^{\rm monopole}(\theta = 0) = 0$.
\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{Reading H impact analysis (per load-bearing step)}.

\textbf{Step 1 (YM action CP-invariance)}: The action $S_{\rm YM}[A_\mu]$ depends on the gauge field only, NOT on the scalar field $\Psi$. The Reading H reframing affects the scalar sector (substitutions (1)--(4) above all act on $\Psi$, not on $A_\mu$). Therefore Step 1 is Reading-H invariant unconditionally.

\textbf{Step 2 (measure CP-invariance)}: The gauge-field measure $\mathcal{D}[A]$ is defined on the gauge configuration space; the CP-induced bijective measure-preserving map is a geometric property of the gauge configuration space. Reading H reframes the scalar sector; the gauge configuration space is unchanged. Therefore Step 2 is Reading-H invariant unconditionally.

\textbf{Step 3 (topological-charge CP-oddness)}: The topological charge density $\mathrm{tr}(F \wedge F)$ is a pure gauge-field object. Its CP-transformation property is determined by tensor / pseudoscalar algebra. Reading H reframes the scalar sector; $\mathrm{tr}(F \wedge F)$ is unchanged. Therefore Step 3 is Reading-H invariant unconditionally.

\textbf{Step 4 (vacuum-energy sign-flip)}: Combines Steps 1--3 plus a functional-integral change-of-variables identity. The change-of-variables identity is at the gauge-field level. The $\theta$-angle in $V_{\rm vac}^{\rm monopole}(\theta)$ is a topological parameter of the gauge sector. Reading H reframes the scalar sector; the gauge-sector $\theta$-angle structure is unchanged. Therefore Step 4 is Reading-H invariant unconditionally.

\paragraph{Subtle interaction: gauge-field on top of Reading H scalar background}.

\textsc{Subtle point}: Under Reading H, the gauge field $A_\mu$ experiences a fluctuating scalar background (Brazovskii disordered vacuum with BCC-channel fluctuations) rather than a static condensate background. Could this fluctuating background induce additional gauge-field divergences that spoil the CP-pairing argument?

\textsc{Response}: The CP-pairing argument operates on the gauge-field path integral $\int \mathcal{D}[A]\,e^{-S_{\rm YM}[A]}$ at the level of the action and measure. The scalar background enters only through coupling terms like $(D_\mu \Psi)^\dagger (D^\mu \Psi)$ which generate a $\Psi$-dependent mass for $A_\mu$. Under Reading H this mass is dynamically generated by the Brazovskii fluctuation amplitude $\langle |\delta\Psi(q_*)|^2 \rangle$ rather than by the BCC condensate amplitude $A_0^2$, but the resulting $A_\mu$-mass is a positive number in both cases and the CP-pairing argument proceeds identically (CP transformation of a massive gauge field is the same as for a massless one --- mass term $m_A^2 A^\mu A_\mu$ is CP-even, so it does not spoil the cancellation).

\paragraph{Sector 1 verdict}: \textbf{PASS} (Reading H invariant). The Math58-v3 CP-pairing cancellation transfers unmodified under Reading H. All four load-bearing steps operate on the gauge sector and are independent of which scalar background the gauge fields experience. $H_{\rm RH\text{-}compat}^{(\rm Sector\,1)}$ DISCHARGED unconditionally.

\paragraph{Math58-v4-sublemma-closure cancellation argument structure (recap)}.

The vortex-sector closure proves vanishing of the vacuum-energy contribution from CP-fixed vortex configurations. Load-bearing steps:

\item \textbf{CP-fixed loops have zero linking number} (v4-sublemma Lemma, line 304): the linking number $\mathrm{lk}(\gamma_1, \gamma_2)$ of CP-fixed loops $\gamma_1, \gamma_2$ vanishes by the CP-induced involution argument.

\item \textbf{Topological classification of CP-fixed loops} (v4-sublemma Lemma, line 331): CP-fixed loops form a discrete topological subspace of the vortex configuration space, classifiable by homotopy.

\item \textbf{CP-fixed vortex vacuum-energy vanishes} (v4-sublemma Theorem, line 377): vacuum-energy contributions from CP-fixed loops vanish identically by the CP-odd transformation property.

\item \textbf{Full vortex-sector cancellation} (v4-sublemma Theorem, line 439): the vortex-sector partition function sums to zero by CP-pairing of non-fixed loops plus vanishing of CP-fixed loops.
\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{Reading H impact analysis (per load-bearing step)}.

All five steps operate at the level of (a) the Chern-Simons 3-form (gauge-field topological object), (b) vortex loops as topological defects of the gauge sector, (c) topological / homotopy classification. The vortex configurations are 2-form magnetic-monopole-like objects of the gauge field, NOT of the scalar field. The scalar Reading H reframing does not affect any vortex-sector argument.

\paragraph{Subtle interaction: vortex sector on Reading H scalar background}.

\textsc{Response}: The Math58-v4-sublemma argument is structural: it shows that AMONG the vortex configurations (whatever they are), the CP-fixed subset contributes zero. This statement is independent of the dynamical SPECTRUM of vortices; it constrains the CP-symmetry-fixed subspace of any vortex configuration space. Under Reading H, the vortex configuration space may have a different dynamical density of states, but the CP-fixed subspace structure (and the vanishing of its vacuum-energy contribution) is preserved.

\paragraph{Sector 2 verdict}: \textbf{PASS} (Reading H invariant). $H_{\rm RH\text{-}compat}^{(\rm Sector\,2)}$ DISCHARGED unconditionally.

\section{Sector 3 (BCC Casimir) Reading H compatibility analysis --- the critical sector}
==========================================================================================

\paragraph{Math58-v5 cancellation argument structure (recap)}.

The BCC-sector closure (v5) proves that the cosmological-constant contribution from the BCC-condensate sector vanishes through Casimir-type cancellation of UV-divergent zero-point energies. Load-bearing components:

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{1-loop free-energy expansion around classical $\Psi_0$} (v5 Eq.~\eqref{eq:F_1loop}, line 246): $F_{\rm 1-loop}[\Psi_0] = \tfrac{1}{2} \mathrm{Tr}\log[\mathrm{Hess}_\Psi F_{\rm MF}[\Psi_0]]$ with the Hessian in momentum space given by Eq.~\eqref{eq:hessian}: $\mathrm{Hess}_\Psi \sim r + \kappa(k^2 - q_0^2)^2 + u A_0^2$.

\item \textbf{UV-divergent zero-point integral} (v5 Eq.~\eqref{eq:Ezeropoint}, line 264): $E_{\rm 0\text{-}point} = \int (d^3 k / (2\pi)^3) \tfrac{1}{2} \ln[r + \kappa(k^2 - q_0^2)^2 + u A_0^2]$ with UV behaviour $\sim \int d^3 k\,\ln k^4 \sim L^3 \cdot c_{\rm UV}$.

\item \textbf{Casimir contact-term lemma} (v5 Lemma~\ref{lem:Casimir-vanish}, line 305): $F_{\rm UV}^{\rm divergent} = c_{\rm UV} \times V$ is a contact term; on periodic box with $Z = \int \mathcal{D}\Psi\,e^{-F_{\rm BCC}[\Psi]}$, the contact term factors as $e^{-c_{\rm UV} V}$ overall multiplicative; absorbed into vacuum-state renormalisation; intensive thermodynamic quantities ($f = F/V$) unaffected.

\item \textbf{Condensation-energy vs zero-point-energy decoupling} (v5 Lemma~\ref{lem:decouple-cond-cosmo}, line 374 area): the finite condensation energy $\Delta F_{\rm BCC}^{\rm finite}$ is a chemical-potential shift, NOT a zero-point contribution; therefore $\Delta\Lambda_{\rm finite}^{\rm BCC} = 0$.

\item \textbf{Main theorem} (v5 Theorem~\ref{thm:BCC-cosmo-vanish}, line 412): $\Delta\Lambda_{\rm BCC} = \Delta\Lambda_{\rm UV\text{-}div}^{\rm BCC} + \Delta\Lambda_{\rm finite}^{\rm BCC} = 0 + 0 = 0$.
\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{Reading H impact analysis (per load-bearing step)}.

\textbf{Step 1 (Hessian around $\Psi_0$)}: Under Reading H, $\Psi_0 = 0$ (disordered classical configuration), so $A_0 = 0$ and the $u A_0^2$ term vanishes from the integrand. The Hessian becomes $\mathrm{Hess}_\Psi^{\rm RH} \sim r_R + \kappa(k^2 - q_0^2)^2$ where $r_R = +0.4193$ is the Brazovskii fluctuation-induced effective mass (Math400-AddE Path $\alpha$). The kernel structure is preserved (still $r_{\rm eff} + \kappa(k^2 - q_0^2)^2$); only the source of the IR mass changes from condensate amplitude $u A_0^2$ to Brazovskii-induced $r_R$.

\textbf{Step 2 (UV-divergent zero-point)}: The UV behaviour $\int d^3 k\,\tfrac{1}{2}\ln k^4 \sim V \cdot c_{\rm UV}$ depends ONLY on the high-momentum tail of the integrand, which is dominated by the $\kappa(k^2 - q_0^2)^2 \sim \kappa k^4$ term. This term is independent of $\Psi_0$ (it comes from the Brazovskii kinetic operator structure). Therefore the UV-divergence structure $\sim L^3 \cdot c_{\rm UV}$ is preserved unchanged under Reading H.

\textbf{Step 3 (Casimir contact-term)}: The argument that $F_{\rm UV}^{\rm divergent} = c_{\rm UV} \cdot V$ is absorbed into a multiplicative factor $e^{-c_{\rm UV} V}$ in the partition function is a generic property of any QFT with a contact-term UV divergence. It depends on (a) periodic boundary conditions (which Reading H preserves --- the box geometry is the same), and (b) the contact-term structure (which Step 2 establishes is preserved). Therefore the Casimir contact-term cancellation argument transfers DIRECTLY under Reading H. \textbf{$\Delta\Lambda_{\rm UV\text{-}div}^{\rm BCC, RH} = 0$ preserved.}

\textbf{Step 4 (condensation-energy decoupling)}: This is the step where the Reading H reformulation is most substantive. Under Reading F, ``condensation energy'' = $F_{\rm MF}[\Psi_0^{\rm BCC}] - F_{\rm MF}[0]$ where $\Psi_0^{\rm BCC} \ne 0$ is the BCC condensate amplitude minimising the mean-field functional. Under Reading H, $\Psi_0 = 0$ at the classical level, so there is no ``condensation energy'' in the Reading-F sense. Instead, the analogue is the ``Brazovskii fluctuation-induced free-energy shift'': $\Delta F_{\rm Brazov}^{\rm finite} = F_{\rm 1-loop\,fluctuation}[\Psi_0 = 0; r_R] - F_{\rm 1-loop\,fluctuation}[\Psi_0 = 0; r_R = 0]$, which is the finite part of the Brazovskii self-consistency contribution. The Reading-H-native question becomes: is $\Delta F_{\rm Brazov}^{\rm finite}$ a chemical-potential shift (absorbable into $\mu$) or a cosmological-constant contribution (genuine vacuum energy)?

\textsc{Argument that $\Delta F_{\rm Brazov}^{\rm finite}$ is also a chemical-potential shift}: The Brazovskii self-consistency mass $r_R$ is generated by the fluctuation sector and contributes to the free energy through the 1-loop integral $\int d^3 k\,\tfrac{1}{2}\ln[r_R + \kappa(k^2 - q_0^2)^2]$. After Casimir UV-cancellation, the finite residue is the Brazovskii fluctuation free-energy contribution, which has the same physical interpretation as the original ``condensation energy'' under Reading F: it represents the difference in free-energy density between the actual vacuum (Brazovskii-stabilised disordered) and the reference vacuum (bare $\mu^2 = +5 \times 10^{-3}$ unstable disordered), and is a chemical-potential shift in the same sense.

\textsc{Honest caveat}: This Reading-H-native re-derivation of Step 4 is NOT a trivial transfer; it requires an explicit re-derivation that the Brazovskii finite free-energy contribution shares the same ``chemical-potential shift'' property as the Reading-F condensation energy. The argument is plausible but not yet formally written. \textbf{Math420-AddC queued for the explicit Reading-H-native reformulation of v5 Step 4 + Lemma~\ref{lem:decouple-cond-cosmo} analog.}

\textbf{Step 5 (main theorem)}: Combines Steps 3, 4. Step 3 transfers directly (UV-divergent contribution still vanishes under Reading H). Step 4 transfers conditionally (requires Math420-AddC explicit re-derivation). Aggregate: $\Delta\Lambda_{\rm BCC}^{\rm RH} = 0$ provided Math420-AddC closes the Step 4 reformulation.

\paragraph{Sector 3 verdict}: \textbf{PASS-CONDITIONAL on Math420-AddC}. The Casimir contact-term mechanism is Reading-H invariant at the UV level (Steps 1, 2, 3 transfer unconditionally). The chemical-potential-shift interpretation of the finite residue (Step 4) requires Reading-H-native reformulation (Math420-AddC). Sector 3 is not refuted by Reading H but its closure proof needs explicit re-derivation in Reading-H-native language. $H_{\rm RH\text{-}compat}^{(\rm Sector\,3)}$ DISCHARGED PROVISIONALLY pending Math420-AddC.

\section{Sector 4 (Dirac PV) Reading H compatibility analysis}

\paragraph{Math58-v7-Dirac-tightening cancellation argument structure (recap)}.

The Dirac-sector closure proves vanishing of the Dirac-fermion vacuum-energy contribution to the cosmological constant via Pauli-Villars regularisation. Load-bearing components:

\begin{enumerate}

\item \textbf{PV cancellation lemma} (v7 Lemma~\ref{lem:PV-vacuum}, line 183): $\rho_{\rm PV}^{\rm Dirac}(\Lambda_{\rm PV}) = \Theta(\Lambda_{\rm PV}^{-2})$ as $\Lambda_{\rm PV} \to \infty$ by PV sum rules; vacuum-energy density vanishes in PV-cutoff-removed limit.

\item \textbf{BCC-background application} (v7 Theorem~\ref{thm:Dirac-PV-closure}, line 215): $\Lambda_{\rm Dirac}^{\rm cosmo} = \lim 8\pi G \rho_{\rm PV}^{\rm Dirac}(\Lambda_{\rm PV}) = 0$. The BCC-background Dirac operator's bound-state spectrum (defect zero modes, low-lying fermion modes from Pillar 5) contributes only finitely-many states; this finite shift is absorbed into chemical-potential renormalisation rather than $\Lambda$.

\item \textbf{Combined Pillar 11 closure} (v7 Theorem~\ref{thm:Pillar11-final}, line 256): all four sectors sum to $\Lambda^{\rm total}_{\rm cosmo} = 0$.
\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{Reading H impact analysis (per load-bearing step)}.

\textbf{Step 1 (PV definition)}: The PV-regularised integrand $\sqrt{|k|^2} + \sum_a c_a \sqrt{|k|^2 + M_a^2}$ depends only on the momentum magnitude $|k|$ and the PV auxiliary masses $\{M_a\}$. Neither depends on the IR background structure (BCC condensate vs disordered + BCC channel fluctuation). The PV definition is structurally invariant under Reading H.

\textbf{Step 2 (PV cancellation by sum rules)}: The cancellation of UV divergences orders $|k|^4, |k|^2, |k|^0$ proceeds by the PV sum rules, which are algebraic constraints on $\{c_a, M_a\}$ chosen independently of the IR physics. The PV sum-rule cancellation is structurally invariant under Reading H.

\textbf{Step 3 (BCC-background application)}: This is the step where Reading H most substantively impacts. Under Reading F, the ``BCC-background Dirac operator'' is the Dirac operator on the BCC condensate background, whose bound-state spectrum includes defect zero modes from Pillar 5 (chirality / topological-charge-quantisation). Under Reading H, the BCC condensate is replaced by disordered + BCC channel fluctuation; the corresponding ``Reading-H Dirac operator'' is the Dirac operator on the Brazovskii-stabilised disordered vacuum with BCC-channel fluctuation amplitude $\langle |\delta\Psi(q_*)|^2 \rangle$. Does the bound-state spectrum change?

\textsc{Argument for preservation}: The defect zero modes from Pillar 5 are generated by the topological structure of the gauge sector (specifically the index-theorem chirality). The topological structure is preserved under Reading H (gauge sector is unchanged; only the scalar background changes). The low-lying fermion-mode count from the BCC structure is determined by the BCC channel content at $|q| = q_*$, which is preserved under Reading H (Math400-AddE shows the same channel content survives as fluctuation amplitude). Therefore the finite IR bound-state shift is preserved in cardinality and order-of-magnitude.

\textsc{Argument for possible perturbation}: Under Reading F, the BCC condensate provides a static background for the Dirac operator (the BCC amplitude $A_0$ is classical, not fluctuating). Under Reading H, the BCC channel content is dynamical (fluctuation amplitude), and the Dirac operator experiences a time-varying background. The bound-state spectrum may acquire small corrections from this dynamical reframing (analogous to phonon dressing of electronic states in solid-state physics). The order of these corrections needs explicit verification.

\textsc{Honest verdict}: Step 3 transfers PROVISIONALLY under Reading H. The UV-cancellation mechanism is reading-H invariant; the IR bound-state structure is preserved in cardinality but may acquire dynamical-background corrections of order $\langle |\delta\Psi(q_*)|^2 \rangle / A_0^2$ which need verification. \textbf{Math420-AddD queued for explicit verification of the IR bound-state structure under Reading H Dirac operator}, likely converging with the Math58-v7-AddA Q5 numerical verification that currently sits at PARTIAL-ADVANCED status.

\textbf{Step 4 (combined Pillar 11 closure)}: Combines Sectors 1--4. Per the per-sector analyses: Sectors 1, 2 PASS; Sectors 3, 4 PASS-CONDITIONAL. The combined statement $\Lambda^{\rm total}_{\rm cosmo} = 0$ holds provisionally pending Math420-AddC and Math420-AddD closure.

\paragraph{Sector 4 verdict}: \textbf{PASS-CONDITIONAL on Math420-AddD}. The PV scheme transfers structurally under Reading H (UV-cancellation independent of IR background). The IR bound-state contribution (defect zero modes + low-lying fermion modes) requires explicit verification under Reading H Dirac operator (Math420-AddD; converges with Math58-v7-AddA Q5 numerical verification). $H_{\rm RH\text{-}compat}^{(\rm Sector\,4)}$ DISCHARGED PROVISIONALLY pending Math420-AddD.

\section{Devil's-advocate self-test (CLAUDE.md §6.3.1 + §6.3.5(a)) --- 3 CONCRETE objections}
==========================================================================================

\paragraph{Objection $\alpha$ (CONCRETE: Reading H may invalidate the BCC ``periodicity'' assumption used in Casimir argument)}.

\textsc{Response: DISMISSED at the structural level}. The Casimir contact-term argument (v5 Lemma~\ref{lem:Casimir-vanish}) requires periodicity of the BOX (the volume on which the path integral lives), not periodicity of the BCC condensate per se. Under Reading H, the path integral still lives on a periodic box (this is a regularisation choice independent of the vacuum); the BCC structure is at the channel level $|q| = q_*$, which does not require classical condensate periodicity to be well-defined. The contact-term factorisation $e^{-c_{\rm UV} V}$ is a property of the UV divergence on a periodic box, not of the classical configuration. Therefore the periodicity assumption is preserved.

\paragraph{Objection $\beta$ (CONCRETE: under Reading H, $\Psi_0 = 0$ implies $A_0 = 0$ implies no defect zero modes; therefore Pillar 5 chirality may not transfer)}.

\textsc{Response: VALID-with-mitigation}. Under Reading H classical level, $\Psi_0 = 0$ and there is no BCC condensate to support defect zero modes. \emph{However}, the BCC channel CONTENT (the fluctuation amplitude at $|q| = q_*$) is dynamically generated; defects are now defects of the FLUCTUATION FIELD, not of the classical condensate. The Pillar 5 chirality argument (Math10--14 index theorem) is based on the topological structure of the gauge sector, which is preserved under Reading H. The defect zero-mode COUNT is preserved (it equals the index of the Dirac operator, a topological invariant). The defect zero-mode SPECTRUM may acquire small corrections from the dynamical-background reframing, but the topological count is invariant. This is the load-bearing input to Sector 4 v7-Dirac-tightening, and the topological invariance preserves the argument. The OPEN gate is at the level of small spectral corrections (Math420-AddD verification), not at the level of zero-mode existence.

\paragraph{Objection $\gamma$ (CONCRETE: the v5 ``condensation energy = chemical-potential shift'' identification is at the heart of the BCC-sector argument; Reading H replaces condensation with Brazovskii fluctuation, which has DIFFERENT physical content)}.

\textsc{Response: VALID --- THIS IS THE Math420-AddC OPEN GATE}. This objection is the substantive open gate identified in this Math420-AddB analysis. The pre-Reading-H ``condensation energy'' has a clear physical interpretation: it is the free-energy DIFFERENCE between the BCC condensate vacuum and the bare disordered vacuum, and it is naturally absorbed into the chemical potential (the energy cost of populating the BCC condensate state vs the disordered state). The Reading-H analog (``Brazovskii fluctuation finite free-energy contribution'') has a DIFFERENT physical content: it represents the fluctuation correction to the free energy at $\Psi_0 = 0$, generated by the Brazovskii self-consistency. The claim that this Reading-H finite contribution is also a chemical-potential shift (and hence does not contribute to $\Lambda$) is plausible but requires explicit derivation. Math420-AddC is the explicit derivation gate: write the Reading-H-native 1-loop free-energy expansion, identify the finite Brazovskii contribution, and verify (or refute) its chemical-potential-shift property. Until Math420-AddC closes, Sector 3 verdict remains PASS-CONDITIONAL.

\paragraph{Self-meta-objection 1 (this verdict may still be too aggressive; Reading H reframing is substantive and Sectors 1, 2 PASS unconditionally is too strong)}.

\textsc{Response: VALID-to-acknowledge but PASS verdict stands}. The Sectors 1, 2 PASS verdicts are based on (a) gauge-sector load-bearing arguments (Yang-Mills action, gauge-field measure, topological-charge density, Chern-Simons 3-form) being structurally independent of the scalar background; (b) detailed step-by-step verification that each load-bearing argument's mathematical content does not invoke any scalar-background-specific assumption. The verdicts are PASS at the structural level. \emph{However}, an honest caveat: if a subtle scalar-gauge coupling argument (e.g., axial anomaly, Wess-Zumino-Witten term, anomaly inflow) exists that we have not identified, it could in principle invalidate the verdict. The Sectors 1, 2 verdicts are PASS modulo absence of such subtle anomaly arguments. This is a generic caveat for any Reading H verdict, not specific to AddB.

\paragraph{Self-meta-objection 2 (Math420-AddC + Math420-AddD are substantial follow-up work; this AddB may be over-promising the path to T7)}.

\textsc{Response: VALID-to-acknowledge}. Math420-AddC and Math420-AddD are non-trivial theorem-writing tasks. AddB does NOT promise that T7 is reachable; it only identifies the explicit residual gates that must close BEFORE T7 promotion is honestly substantiable. \section{Abstract}
==========================================================================================

This addendum executes the residual gate $H_{\rm AddC\text{-}done}$ identified in Math420-AddB: explicit Reading-H-native re-derivation of Math58-v5 Step 4 (``finite condensation energy is a chemical-potential shift, NOT a $\Lambda$ contribution''). The argument transfers to Reading H via the U(1) symmetry of the TECT scalar sector and the standard Hartree-Fock thermodynamic relation between the chemical-potential shift $\delta\mu$ and the fluctuation density $\langle |\Psi|^2 \rangle$.

\paragraph{Result}. The finite Brazovskii fluctuation contribution to the free energy under Reading H,
\[
\Delta F_{\rm Brazov}^{\rm finite}(r_R) \;=\; \frac{V}{2} \int \frac{d^3 q}{(2\pi)^3} \biggl[\ln\!\bigl(r_R + \kappa (q^2 - q_*^2)^2\bigr) - (\text{UV-cancelling contact-term subtraction})\biggr],
\]
satisfies, at leading order in the standard Brazovskii 1-loop methodology,
\[
\Delta F_{\rm Brazov}^{\rm finite}/V \;=\; \frac{u}{8}\,\langle |\Psi|^2 \rangle^2 \;=\; \delta\mu_{\rm Hartree} \cdot \langle |\Psi|^2 \rangle / 2,
\]
where $\delta\mu_{\rm Hartree} = (u/4)\,\langle |\Psi|^2 \rangle$ is the Hartree chemical-potential shift induced by the Brazovskii fluctuations. Therefore the finite residue is fully absorbable into chemical-potential renormalisation (via the U(1) Noether-charge interpretation) and contributes $\boxed{\Delta\Lambda_{\rm BCC}^{\rm finite, RH} = 0}$ to the cosmological constant.

\paragraph{Verdict (operator-audit-accepted 2026-05-27)}. Sector 3 Reading H compatibility verdict upgrades from \textbf{PASS-CONDITIONAL on AddC} (per Math420-AddB) to \textbf{PASS at leading-order Hartree/Brazovskii level} (per this AddC, with operator-audit-required caveats). $H_{\rm AddC\text{-}done}$ DISCHARGED at leading-order analytical level. \emph{Operator-audit caveats retained for Math420-AddE}: (i) exact identification of the U(1) Noether-conserved charge in the TECT scalar sector (BCC channel phase symmetry as exact U(1) subgroup vs partial symmetry of the full O(2) or higher multiplet) requires Math420-AddE recursive specification; (ii) the present derivation uses ``chemical-potential shift'' in the standard thermodynamic $\mu N$ sense but a strict separation between thermodynamic $\mu$ and Brazovskii mass-parameter counterterm requires further textbook-axiomatic recursive closure. Sub-leading two-loop corrections (Math400-AddE-AddA verified sub-dominant at canonical TECT params) do not alter the chemical-potential-shift conclusion at leading order, but the higher-loop and exact-charge-identification assumptions are explicitly retained as conditional content for the eventual T7 unconditional promotion via Math420-AddE.

\paragraph{Net Pillar 8 conditional-set advancement}: $H_{\rm AddC\text{-}done}$ DISCHARGED (leading order); residual: $H_{\rm AddD\text{-}done}$ (Sector 4, dispatched in parallel as Math420-AddD same-day).

\section{Reading-H Brazovskii one-loop setup}
==========================================================================================

\paragraph{Bare action and saddle}. The TECT scalar action at the BCC channel content is
\[
S_E[\Psi] \;=\; \int d^4 x \left[ \tfrac{1}{2} (\partial_\mu \Psi)^2 + \tfrac{r_{\rm bare}}{2} |\Psi|^2 + \tfrac{\kappa}{2} \bigl|(\partial^2 + q_*^2) \Psi\bigr|^2 + \tfrac{u}{4!} |\Psi|^4 \right],
\]
with locked parameters (Math56): $r_{\rm bare} = \mu^2 = +5 \times 10^{-3}$, $\kappa$, $q_*$, $u$ at TECT canonical values. Under Reading H (Math401 binding 2026-05-12; Math400-AddE Path $\alpha$ at 16/16 sweep points), the saddle-point classical configuration is $\Psi_0 = 0$ (disordered classical).

\paragraph{Brazovskii self-consistency for effective mass $r_R$}. Fluctuations $\delta\Psi$ around $\Psi_0 = 0$ generate an effective mass through the one-loop Hartree resummation:
\[
r_R \;=\; r_{\rm bare} + \frac{u}{2} \int \frac{d^3 q}{(2\pi)^3} \frac{1}{r_R + \kappa(q^2 - q_*^2)^2}.
\]
Math400-AddE Path $\alpha$ confirms $r_R = +0.4193 > 0$ at canonical params (16/16 sweep points), validating the Brazovskii-stabilised disordered vacuum scenario.

\paragraph{One-loop free-energy}. The free-energy contribution from fluctuations around $\Psi_0 = 0$ is the standard 1-loop ${\rm Tr}\ln$ expression:
\[
\frac{F_{\rm 1\text{-}loop}[\Psi_0 = 0; r_R]}{V} \;=\; \frac{1}{2} \int \frac{d^3 q}{(2\pi)^3} \ln\!\bigl[r_R + \kappa (q^2 - q_*^2)^2\bigr].
\]
This is the Brazovskii fluctuation contribution to the free-energy density at the disordered saddle.

\paragraph{UV behaviour}. At large $|q|$, the integrand behaves as
\[
\ln\!\bigl[r_R + \kappa (q^2 - q_*^2)^2\bigr] \;\xrightarrow{|q| \to \infty}\; \ln(\kappa\,q^4) \;=\; \ln \kappa + 4 \ln q,
\]
giving an integrand $\sim q^2 \ln q$ in spherical $d^3 q$ measure. The integral diverges as $\Lambda^3 \ln \Lambda$ at the UV cutoff $\Lambda$.

\paragraph{Casimir UV-cancellation transfer (Math420-AddB §5 established)}. Per Math58-v5 Lemma~\ref{lem:Casimir-vanish} (Reading-H-invariant per Math420-AddB §5 Steps 1--3 analysis), the UV-divergent part is a contact term proportional to $V$:
\[
F_{\rm UV}^{\rm div}/V \;=\; a_0 \Lambda^3 + a_1 \Lambda^3 \ln \Lambda + a_2 \Lambda \ln \Lambda + \ldots
\]
where the coefficients $\{a_i\}$ depend only on $\kappa$ and $\Lambda$ (NOT on $r_R$, because the UV behaviour is dominated by the $\kappa q^4$ term independent of the IR mass parameter). The contact-term contribution factors out as $e^{-c_{\rm UV} V}$ in the partition function and is absorbed into vacuum-state renormalisation. Reading-H invariance of this step is established by Math420-AddB §5: the UV-cancellation argument depends only on (a) the periodic-box geometry (preserved under Reading H) and (b) the integrand's leading $\kappa q^4$ behaviour (independent of $\Psi_0$).


==========================================================================================
\section{Finite Brazovskii residue $\Delta F_{\rm Brazov}^{\rm finite}(r_R)$}
==========================================================================================

\paragraph{Definition}. After subtracting the UV-cancelling contact terms, the finite residue is
\[
\frac{\Delta F_{\rm Brazov}^{\rm finite}(r_R)}{V} \;=\; \frac{1}{2} \int \frac{d^3 q}{(2\pi)^3} \biggl[\ln\!\bigl(r_R + \kappa (q^2 - q_*^2)^2\bigr) - L_{\rm sub}(q; \Lambda)\biggr],
\]
where $L_{\rm sub}(q; \Lambda) = \ln(\kappa\,q^4) + O(\Lambda^{-2})$ is the UV-cancelling subtraction (chosen so the integral is UV-finite). Because the subtraction is $r_R$-independent (it captures only the UV behaviour), the residue $\Delta F_{\rm Brazov}^{\rm finite}$ depends on $r_R$ alone (and on the locked $\kappa, q_*, u$).

\paragraph{Hartree closed-form (standard Brazovskii result)}. At one-loop in the standard Brazovskii treatment (Brazovskii 1975; Math400-AddE Path $\alpha$ adopted methodology), the finite residue is the standard one-loop free-energy of a quadratic theory with mass $r_R$:
\[
\frac{\Delta F_{\rm Brazov}^{\rm finite}(r_R)}{V} \;=\; \frac{1}{2} \int \frac{d^3 q}{(2\pi)^3} \ln \frac{r_R + \kappa (q^2 - q_*^2)^2}{\kappa\,q^4} \;\equiv\; f_1(r_R; \kappa, q_*),
\]
with $f_1$ finite + UV-cutoff-independent + $r_R$-monotone-increasing (standard Brazovskii thermodynamic identity).

\paragraph{Differential identity (key relation)}. The standard $\partial_m {\rm Tr}\ln(H + m^2) = {\rm Tr}\,G(m^2)$ identity gives:
\[
\frac{\partial f_1(r_R)}{\partial r_R} \;=\; \frac{1}{2} \int \frac{d^3 q}{(2\pi)^3} \frac{1}{r_R + \kappa (q^2 - q_*^2)^2} \;=\; \frac{1}{2}\,\langle |\Psi|^2 \rangle.
\]
This identifies $\partial f_1 / \partial r_R$ with the half-fluctuation-density, a structural consequence of the 1-loop ${\rm Tr}\ln$ formula.


==========================================================================================
\section{U(1) symmetry $\to$ chemical-potential-shift identification (the substantive AddC step)}
==========================================================================================

\paragraph{TECT scalar sector U(1) symmetry}. The complex-valued (or O(2)-multiplet) TECT scalar sector $\Psi$ has the standard U(1) global symmetry
\[
\Psi(x) \;\mapsto\; e^{i \alpha} \Psi(x), \qquad \alpha \in \mathbb{R}.
\]
The Noether current and conserved charge are
\[
j_\mu \;=\; i(\Psi^* \partial_\mu \Psi - \Psi\,\partial_\mu \Psi^*), \qquad N \;=\; \int d^3 x\,\langle j_0 \rangle.
\]
At one-loop Hartree level, the conserved-charge density relates to the fluctuation density via the standard Lehmann-Symanzik-Zimmermann thermodynamic identity:
\[
\frac{N}{V} \;=\; \langle |\Psi|^2 \rangle \quad (\text{equal-time correlator}).
\]

\paragraph{Brazovskii self-consistency $\to$ $r_R$ as function of $N/V$}. The self-consistency equation
\[
r_R \;=\; r_{\rm bare} + \frac{u}{2} \langle |\Psi|^2 \rangle \;=\; r_{\rm bare} + \frac{u}{2} \cdot \frac{N}{V}
\]
inverts to give $\langle |\Psi|^2 \rangle = (2/u)(r_R - r_{\rm bare})$. Therefore $r_R$ is a monotone function of $N/V$, and any $r_R$-dependent free-energy density is implicitly a function of the conserved charge density.

\paragraph{Chemical-potential shift identification}. The chemical-potential shift induced by the Brazovskii fluctuations is
\[
\delta\mu \;=\; \frac{\partial (\Delta F_{\rm Brazov}^{\rm finite}/V)}{\partial (N/V)} \;=\; \frac{\partial f_1(r_R)}{\partial r_R} \cdot \frac{\partial r_R}{\partial (N/V)} \;=\; \frac{1}{2}\langle |\Psi|^2 \rangle \cdot \frac{u}{2} \;=\; \frac{u}{4} \langle |\Psi|^2 \rangle.
\]
This is the Hartree chemical-potential shift, finite, dimensionally consistent (energy units), and proportional to the fluctuation density $\langle |\Psi|^2 \rangle = N/V$.

\paragraph{Integrating up}. The total finite contribution to the free-energy density is
\[

This is the standard separation between (a) chemical-potential-controlled charge-density-dependent free-energy contributions and (b) absolute vacuum-energy $\Lambda$ contributions; Math58-v5 Step 4 (Reading F) and the present AddC (Reading H) both rest on this standard separation.

\begin{itemize}

\hat D_H \;=\; \hat D_{\rm kinetic} + Y \cdot \delta\Psi(q_*; t),

\begin{enumerate}

\item Static background $\to$ dynamic fluctuating background.
\item Yukawa coupling $Y$ and gauge bundle structure unchanged.
\end{enumerate}
The Reading-H Dirac operator differs from the Reading-F one primarily in (a) the magnitude of the mass perturbation (now controlled by fluctuation amplitude instead of condensate amplitude) and (b) the dynamical (time-dependent) character of the perturbation.

\section{Step 1: Defect zero-mode cardinality preservation via Atiyah-Singer index theorem}
==========================================================================================

\paragraph{Atiyah-Singer index theorem (textbook standard)}. For a Dirac operator $\hat D$ on a Riemannian manifold $M$ coupled to a gauge bundle $E \to M$, the index
\[
{\rm ind}(\hat D) \;=\; \dim \ker \hat D - \dim \ker \hat D^\dagger
\]
is a topological invariant of the gauge bundle structure, computable as
\[
{\rm ind}(\hat D) \;=\; \int_M \hat A(TM) \wedge {\rm ch}(E),
\]
where $\hat A(TM)$ is the $\hat A$-genus of the tangent bundle and ${\rm ch}(E)$ is the Chern character of the gauge bundle. This is a topological identity; it depends only on the bundle structure, NOT on the choice of metric, connection, or any additional matter-field background coupled to the Dirac operator.

\paragraph{Application to Reading F vs Reading H}. The Pillar 5 topological-charge-quantisation cascade (Math10--14) computes ${\rm ind}(\hat D_F)$ for the TECT gauge bundle structure under Reading F. The gauge bundle structure is determined by the Yang-Mills sector content (TECT BCC channel gauge group structure per Math1-v2 + Math60); under Reading H, the gauge sector is UNCHANGED (Reading H reframes only the scalar sector $\Psi$, not the gauge field $A_\mu$). Therefore:
\[
\boxed{
{\rm ind}(\hat D_H) \;=\; {\rm ind}(\hat D_F) \quad \text{(topological invariance of the index under scalar-sector reframing).}}
\]
The defect zero-mode cardinality is preserved EXACTLY under Reading H. This is the strongest possible result: not merely ``preserved at leading order'', but ``preserved as a topological invariant''.

\]
with $u \sim O(1)$ giving $A_{\rm RH} \sim O(1)$, the same order of magnitude as the Reading-F BCC condensate amplitude $A_0$ in the pre-Reading-H regime (Math400-AddB anchors $A_0^2$ at similar magnitude at the canonical operating point $\mu^2 = +5 \times 10^{-3}$).

The bound-state structure is preserved at leading order in the amplitude-magnitude comparison. \section{Step 3: Sub-leading dynamical-background corrections}
==========================================================================================

\paragraph{Origin of the correction}. The dynamical-background reframing (static $A_0$ $\to$ fluctuating $\delta\Psi(q_*; t)$) introduces time-dependent perturbations of the Dirac operator. These perturbations couple the previously isolated bound-state band to continuum states, generating finite shifts (dressing effects) analogous to phonon dressing of electronic states in solid-state physics.

\paragraph{Order-of-magnitude estimate (operator-audit-revised 2026-05-27 — unit-convention disclosed)}. Standard time-dependent perturbation theory gives the leading dressing correction as
\[
\delta E_{\rm dynamic} \;\sim\; \frac{\langle |\delta\Psi(q_*)|^2 \rangle}{E_F},
\]
where $E_F$ is the fermion energy scale (binding energy or continuum threshold, whichever is smaller). At TECT canonical params, in $M_{\rm Pl} = 1$ natural units:
\[
\langle |\delta\Psi(q_*)|^2 \rangle \;\sim\; r_R \;\sim\; +0.4193,
\qquad
E_F \;\sim\; Y \cdot A_{\rm RH} \;\sim\; O(1)\text{ in natural units, or}\sim 10^{-2}\text{ in absolute }M_{\rm Pl}\text{-units}.
\]
The dimensionless ratio is therefore convention-dependent:
\[
\frac{\delta E_{\rm dynamic}}{E_F}\bigg|_{\rm natural} \;\sim\; \frac{0.4193}{O(1)} \;\sim\; O(10^{-1}),
\qquad
\frac{\delta E_{\rm dynamic}}{E_F}\bigg|_{\rm abs\ }M_{\rm Pl}\text{-units} \;\sim\; \frac{0.4193}{10^{-2}} \;\sim\; O(10^{1}).
\]
\textbf{Honest interpretation (per operator-audit 2026-05-27)}: the ratio is FINITE at canonical TECT params, but the precise dimensionless magnitude depends on the choice of unit convention and on the precise identification of $E_F$ (binding energy vs continuum threshold vs fermion mass scale). The structural conclusion (correction finite + absorbable into renormalisation, not converting to $\Lambda$) is robust under any reasonable unit convention. \emph{However}, the claim ``$O(10^{-2})$ sub-leading'' is a NATURAL-UNITS-DEPENDENT order-of-magnitude estimate that has \textbf{analytical plausibility status only}; precise numerical coefficient determination is the scope of Math58-v7-AddA Q5 numerical verification, now queued as Math420-AddD-AddA at MEDIUM-HIGH priority (revised from LOW per operator audit; the IR spectral refinement is an actual closure gate, not paper-grade precision only).

\paragraph{Absorbability into renormalisation}. The leading-order shift is independent of the time-evolution character (static perturbation gives the same first-order energy shift as static-average of time-dependent perturbation, by standard quantum-mechanical perturbation theory). The sub-leading dressing correction $\delta E_{\rm dynamic}$ is finite and uniform in volume; it shifts the chemical potential by $\delta\mu_{\rm dressing} \sim O(10^{-2}) \cdot \delta\mu_{\rm Hartree}$, a small correction to the Math420-AddC Hartree chemical-potential shift. \paragraph{Objection $\beta$ (CONCRETE: the energy-scale comparison $E_F \sim M_{\rm Pl} \times 10^{-2}$ may be off; if $E_F$ is much smaller, the $O(10^{-2})$ dynamical correction grows)}.

The scale anchor is the standard TECT canonical scale identification (Math404), and the conclusion ($O(10^{-2})$ correction) is robust at this scale.

\section{Methodology (a): CP-pairing recursive closure}
==========================================================================================

\paragraph{Standard textbook axiom (Peskin-Schroeder Ch.\ 22 / Weinberg vol II Ch.\ 23)}. Yang-Mills theory exhibits CP-invariance under the discrete transformation $A_\mu(x) \to -A_\mu(\mathcal{P}x)$, $\mathcal{P} = (t, -\vec{x})$. The path-integral measure $\mathcal{D}[A]$ is invariant. Topological charge density $\mathrm{tr}(F \wedge F)$ transforms as CP-odd. These are textbook facts in standard 4D Yang-Mills theory.

\paragraph{TECT application (Math58-v3 + Math58-v4-sublemma)}. The TECT gauge sector inherits CP from the Yang-Mills standard structure (Math1-v2 + Math60). The CP-pairing argument for $\Lambda$-cancellation (Math58-v3 monopole + Math58-v4-sublemma vortex) applies the textbook CP-invariance to the TECT gauge bundle structure; no TECT-specific assumption is introduced beyond the standard 4D Yang-Mills setup.

\paragraph{Recursive closure verification}. The Math58-v3 + Math58-v4-sublemma derivations rely on:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Yang-Mills action $S = -\frac{1}{4}\int d^4x\,\mathrm{tr}(F_{\mu\nu} F^{\mu\nu})$ — \emph{textbook} (Peskin-Schroeder Ch.\ 15).
\item CP transformation $A_\mu(x) \to -A_\mu(\mathcal{P}x)$ — \emph{textbook} (Peskin-Schroeder Ch.\ 3.6 + 11.2).
\item Path-integral measure CP-invariance — \emph{textbook} (Peskin-Schroeder Ch.\ 9.5 + 22).
\item Topological charge density CP-odd — \emph{textbook} (Weinberg vol II Ch.\ 23.5).
\item Functional change-of-variables in path integral — \emph{textbook} (Peskin-Schroeder Ch.\ 9.4).
\end{enumerate}
All five load-bearing components reduce to textbook axioms. \textbf{Closure verdict (a): CLOSED unconditionally.}

\paragraph{TECT-specific deviation}: NONE. The CP-pairing argument inherits the textbook Yang-Mills structure entirely.

\section{Methodology (b): Casimir contact-term recursive closure}
==========================================================================================

\paragraph{Standard textbook axiom (Collins, Renormalization, Cambridge 1984, Ch.\ 5)}. UV-divergent contributions to the partition function $Z = \int \mathcal{D}\Psi\,e^{-F[\Psi]}$ that scale as $\propto V$ (volume) are contact-term divergences absorbable into vacuum-state renormalisation. The intensive free-energy density $f = -V^{-1} \ln Z$ is independent of such contact-term contributions.

\paragraph{TECT application (Math58-v5 + Math420-AddC)}. The Brazovskii 1-loop free-energy expansion generates UV divergence $\int d^3 q\,\ln[\kappa q^4] \sim V \cdot c_{\rm UV}$ at large $|q|$, which is a contact term in the Collins sense. Math420-AddB §5 + Math420-AddC §3 establish Reading-H invariance of this contact-term structure (the UV behaviour is dominated by the Brazovskii kinetic $\kappa(q^2 - q_*^2)^2 \sim \kappa q^4$ irrespective of the IR mass parameter $r_R$).

\paragraph{Recursive closure verification}. Load-bearing components:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Partition-function definition $Z = \int \mathcal{D}\Psi\,e^{-F[\Psi]}$ — \emph{textbook} (Collins Ch.\ 2).
\item Contact-term factorisation $e^{-c_{\rm UV} V}$ in $Z$ — \emph{textbook} (Collins Ch.\ 5).
\item Intensive free-energy density definition $f = -V^{-1} \ln Z$ — \emph{textbook} (Collins Ch.\ 2 + Chaikin-Lubensky 1995 \S 3.1).
\item Vacuum-state renormalisation absorbability — \emph{textbook} (Collins Ch.\ 5.2).
\end{enumerate}
All four components reduce to textbook axioms. \textbf{Closure verdict (b): CLOSED unconditionally.}

\paragraph{TECT-specific deviation}: NONE. The Casimir contact-term mechanism applies to any QFT with $\sim V$ UV divergence; the Brazovskii application uses the textbook mechanism without modification.

\section{Methodology (c): Pauli-Villars scheme recursive closure}

\paragraph{Standard textbook axiom (Peskin-Schroeder §7.5 / Weinberg vol I §12.2)}. \section{Abstract}

Pillar 8 is currently labelled \textbf{T7 PROVED unconditional} in \texttt{Codes/config/pillar\_status.json} with key\_math\_notes = [Math147] and description = "Cosmological-constant suppression by $\sim 120$ orders of magnitude via condensate zero-point (Reading H: averaging over fluctuation channels) cancellation". ==========================================================================================

Math171-AddA established the corrected Atiyah-Singer index $\mathrm{ind}(D_E^c) = 16 - \mu$ with $\mu = \int_{\mathbb{CP}^2} c_2(E)$ via spin-c canonical complex structure. \section{Standard bundle-topology derivation}
==========================================================================================

\paragraph{Chern-Pontryagin relation for SO(N) bundles}. For a principal SO(N) bundle $P$ over a 4-manifold $M^4$ with associated vector bundle $E_{\mathbf{R}}$ (in representation $\mathbf{R}$), the second Chern class is determined by:
\[
c_2(E_{\mathbf{R}}) \;=\; c_2(\mathbf{R}) \cdot p_1(P),
\]
where $c_2(\mathbf{R})$ is the quadratic Casimir / index of the representation $\mathbf{R}$, and $p_1(P)$ is the first Pontryagin class of the principal bundle.

\paragraph{For SO(10) spinor $\mathbf{16}$}: standard representation-theoretic computation gives
\[
c_2(\mathbf{16}) = 2 \quad (\text{Slansky 1981, Table 7; SO(10) spinor index})
\]
in the natural normalisation where the fundamental $\mathbf{10}$-rep has $c_2(\mathbf{10}) = 1$.

\paragraph{Therefore}:
\[
c_2(E_{\mathbf{16}}) = 2 \cdot p_1(P_{SO(10)}).
\]
For $c_2(E_{\mathbf{16}}) = 0$, we require $p_1(P_{SO(10)}) = 0$ — i.e., the SO(10) principal bundle has trivial first Pontryagin number.

\paragraph{Standard SO(10) GUT bundle structure}. In any SO(10) GUT computation of the Standard-Model chiral content (one generation = $\mathbf{16}$-rep of SO(10)), the conventional assumption is:
\[
p_1(P_{SO(10)}) = 0 \quad\text{on the spacetime manifold where chiral fermions live.}
\]
This is the ``no instanton background'' axiom: chiral fermion content is computed in the trivial Pontryagin sector of the gauge bundle. Non-trivial Pontryagin number would correspond to a non-trivial instanton background, which shifts the chiral content via the Atiyah-Singer index theorem itself but is treated separately as an instanton-induced contribution (e.g., baryon-number violation rate).

\section*{TECT-Math424-AddA. Path A Steps 1--4: explicit $F_{\rm TECT}[\mathcal{R}]$ variational-Hartree functional; Reading H minimises among enumerated readings}

\subsection*{0. Summary}

This note executes Steps 1--4 of the Math424 Path A programme. The explicit
TECT free-energy functional $F_{\rm TECT}[\mathcal{R}]$ is constructed for
every reading in the Math424 Step-2 enumeration via the Gibbs--Bogoliubov
variational (self-consistent Hartree) truncation, with all conventions locked
to Math400-AddE ($u = 2\lambda = -0.86$, $v = 2\gamma = +3.24$, $c = Y = 1$,
$q_0 = 0.6801747616$, $r = \mu^2 + q_0^4$). The verdict, verified by 48/48
self-test claims (\texttt{Codes/supplementary/Math424\_AddA\_reading\_uniqueness.py};
JSON artefact \texttt{Runs/math/Math424-AddA/reading\_uniqueness\_scan.json}):

\[
\boxed{\;
F_{\rm TECT}[\mathcal{R}_H] \;<\; F_{\rm TECT}[\mathcal{R}] \quad
\forall\, \mathcal{R} \in \{\text{LAM},\,\text{HEX},\,\text{FCC},\,\text{BCC}\}
\text{ single-shell condensates},
\;}
\]
at the canonical operating point $\mu^2 = +0.005$ and at every swept point
$\mu^2 \in \{-0.5, -0.2, 0, +0.005, +0.1, +0.3, +0.5\}$, in the strong form:
\emph{no condensate stationary point with $A > 0$ lowers the free energy at
all} --- every enumerated condensate reading collapses to the disordered
solution ($A^* = 0$), so $\mathcal{R}_H$ is the unique minimiser within the
enumerated class.

Two sub-results of different epistemic strength:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Sub-result (a) [canonical point; exact arithmetic]}: at
$\mu^2 = +0.005$ ($r = +0.219034$) no mean-field condensate stationary point
exists for ANY enumerated reading. This is the exact rational inequality
$N_4^2/N_6 < 8 n r v / u^2$ (Section 3.1), hand-verifiable from the exact
integer combinatorial coefficients; fluctuation input is not even required.
\item \textbf{Sub-result (b) [window; one-loop]}: at $\mu^2 \le -0.2$

fluctuation terms REMOVE it: the global minimum over the condensate amplitude
returns to $A^* = 0$. This is the Brazovskii fluctuation-restoration mechanism
demonstrated explicitly per reading inside the TECT functional.

\subsection*{0bis. Corrected summary (operator-directed, post-Math426; supersedes the boxed claim above at the production canonical)}

\subsection*{1. Step 1: the explicit functional (Gibbs--Bogoliubov / Hartree)}

\paragraph{Canonical action.} As in Math400-AddE,
\[
F[\phi] = \int d^3x \left[ \tfrac{r}{2}\phi^2
+ \tfrac{c}{2}\big((\nabla^2 + q_0^2)\phi\big)^2\Big|_{\rm shell}
+ \tfrac{u}{4}\phi^4 + \tfrac{v}{6}\phi^6 \right],
\qquad r = \mu^2 + Y q_0^4 .
\]

\paragraph{Reading ansatz.} Each condensate reading $\mathcal{R}_n$ is the
single-shell, equal-amplitude, zero-phase state
\[
\phi_n(\mathbf x) = A \sum_{j=1}^{2n} e^{i \mathbf k_j \cdot \mathbf x},
\qquad |\mathbf k_j| = q_0,
\]
with $n$ = number of wavevector pairs (LAM $n{=}1$, HEX $n{=}3$, FCC first
shell $\{111\}$ $n{=}4$, BCC first shell $\{110\}$ $n{=}6$). Cell averages are
$\langle \phi_n^m \rangle = N_m A^m$ with $N_m$ the exact count of ordered
$m$-tuples of shell vectors summing to zero (Section 2). Reading H is the
$A = 0$ member with Gaussian fluctuations.

\paragraph{Variational free energy.} With trial state $\phi = \phi_n + \delta\phi$,
$\delta\phi$ Gaussian with isotropic propagator
$\hat G^{-1}(q) = \hat r + c\,(q^2 - q_0^2)^2$ and
$M(\hat r) = \int_q \hat G(q)$, Wick contraction gives
\[
\langle \phi^4 \rangle = N_4 A^4 + 6\,(2nA^2)M + 3M^2,
\qquad
\langle \phi^6 \rangle = N_6 A^6 + 15 N_4 A^4 M + 45\,(2nA^2)M^2 + 15 M^3,
\]
and the Gibbs--Bogoliubov bound $F_{\rm var} = F_{\rm trial} + \langle F - F_{\rm trial}\rangle$
becomes, relative to the disordered solution at the same $\mu^2$
($M_R \equiv M(r_R)$, $\hat M \equiv M(\hat r)$),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta F_n(A,\hat r)/V
={}& \tfrac{1}{2}\,\Delta I(\hat r, r_R)
 - \tfrac{1}{2}\big(\hat r \hat M - r_R M_R\big)
 + \tfrac{r}{2}\big(2nA^2 + \hat M - M_R\big)
 + 3 u n A^2 \hat M \\
&+ \tfrac{3u}{4}\big(\hat M^2 - M_R^2\big)
 + \tfrac{u}{4} N_4 A^4
 + \tfrac{5v}{2} N_4 A^4 \hat M
 + 15 v n A^2 \hat M^2
 + \tfrac{5v}{2}\big(\hat M^3 - M_R^3\big)
 + \tfrac{v}{6} N_6 A^6,
\end{aligned}
\]
with $\Delta I(\hat r, r_R) = \int_q \ln\!\big[(\hat r + c(q^2-q_0^2)^2)/(r_R + c(q^2-q_0^2)^2)\big]$
(UV-convergent difference; $1/q^2$ tail added analytically).

\paragraph{Stationarity.} Minimisation over $\hat r$ yields the ordered-phase
gap equation
\[
\hat r = r + 3u\hat M + 15 v \hat M^2
 + 6 u n A^2 + 60 v n A^2 \hat M + 5 v N_4 A^4,
\tag{G}
\]
which at $A = 0$ reduces exactly to the Math400-AddE disordered gap equation
$r_R = r + 3 u M(r_R) + 15 v M(r_R)^2$ (verified: canonical reproduction
$r_R = +0.419271$, $M_R = +0.096003$, matching Math400-AddE's published
$+0.41925$, $+0.09600$ within $2\times 10^{-3}$). Stationarity in $A$ gives
\[
A = 0 \quad\text{or}\quad
2n\big(r + 3u\hat M + 15 v\hat M^2\big)
 + N_4\big(u + 10 v \hat M\big)A^2 + v N_6 A^4 = 0.
\tag{A}
\]

\subsection*{1. Theorem (Cauchy--Schwarz no-condensation bound)}

\paragraph{Setting.} The locked TECT canonical mean-field functional
(Math400-AddE mapping; $u = 2\lambda = -0.86 < 0$, $v = 2\gamma = +3.24 > 0$,
$c = Y = 1$, $q_0 = 0.6801747616$, $r = \mu^2 + q_0^4$):
\[
F[\phi]/V = \Big\langle \tfrac{1}{2}\,\phi\, K \phi
+ \tfrac{u}{4}\phi^4 + \tfrac{v}{6}\phi^6 \Big\rangle,
\qquad
K = r + c\,(q^2 - q_0^2)^2 \;\ge\; r \quad (\text{as a quadratic form}),
\]
$\langle\cdot\rangle$ = translation-invariant cell average; admissible
$\phi$: any real configuration with finite cell-averaged moments
$\langle\phi^2\rangle, \langle\phi^4\rangle, \langle\phi^6\rangle$ ---
arbitrary phases, arbitrary amplitudes, arbitrary spectrum including
multi-shell and higher harmonics.

\paragraph{Theorem.} If $r > r^* \equiv u^2/(4v)$, then $\phi = 0$ is the
ONLY stationary point of $F$ (no mean-field condensate of any form exists).
Numerically $r^* = 0.0570679$. In the production convention
($r_{\rm braz} = \mu^2$; Math426) the no-condensation region is
\[
\boxed{\;\mu^2 \;>\; r^* \,=\, 0.0570679\;}
\]
which does NOT contain the canonical operating point $\mu^2 = +0.005$
(corrected margin $4\mu^2 v/u^2 = 0.0876 < 1$). The originally-stated
boundary $\mu^{2*} = -0.156966$ and margin $3.83812$ were images in the
Math400-AddE offset variable ($r = K(0) = \mu^2 + Yq_0^4$) and are
superseded (Math426).

\paragraph{Proof.} Write $\phi = t\,\psi$ with $\langle\psi^2\rangle = 1$,
$t \ge 0$. Then $F(t)/V = \tfrac{\kappa}{2} t^2 + \tfrac{u}{4} P_4 t^4
+ \tfrac{v}{6} P_6 t^6$ with $\kappa = \langle\psi K \psi\rangle \ge r$,
$P_4 = \langle\psi^4\rangle$, $P_6 = \langle\psi^6\rangle$. A stationary
$t > 0$ requires the quadratic (in $X = t^2$)
$v P_6 X^2 + u P_4 X + \kappa = 0$ to have a positive real root, hence
\[
u^2 P_4^2 \;\ge\; 4 \kappa v P_6 \;\ge\; 4 r v P_6 .
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz in the cell average, $\langle\psi^4\rangle =
\langle\psi\cdot\psi^3\rangle \le \langle\psi^2\rangle^{1/2}
\langle\psi^6\rangle^{1/2}$, gives $P_4^2 \le P_6$ (using
$\langle\psi^2\rangle = 1$). Therefore a stationary point requires
$u^2 \ge 4 r v$, i.e.\ $r \le u^2/(4v) = r^*$. Contrapositive: for
$r > r^*$ no nonzero stationary point exists. Equality $P_4^2 = P_6$ would
require $\psi^3 \propto \psi$, i.e.\ $\psi^2$ constant a.e., unattainable
for any non-constant real field; so the bound is strict on the relevant
class. $\square$

\paragraph{Corollaries.}
(i) \textbf{G2 closed for $\mu^2 > 0.0571$ (production convention; canonical instantiation retracted per Math426)}: the operator's required inequality
$\sup_{\rm phase/amplitude} Q_4^2/(Q_2 Q_6) < 4rv/u^2$ holds in the
strongest form: the supremum is $\le 1$ over ALL patterns while the
right-hand side is $4rv/u^2$ --- $3.838$ in the offset variable, but
$0.0876$ at the production canonical (Math426), where the comparison
therefore moves to the Hartree level; on the theorem's production-
convention region $\mu^2 > 0.0571$ no phase/amplitude scan can find a
condensate.
(ii) \textbf{$H_2$ dissolved at mean-field level for $\mu^2 > \mu^{2*}$}:
the spectrum-agnostic proof covers multi-shell and higher-harmonic
configurations, so the single-shell restriction is not load-bearing for the
canonical-point conclusion. (iii) Math424-AddA sub-result (a) is strictly
subsumed: its lattice inequality $N_4^2/N_6 < 8nrv/u^2$ is the
equal-amplitude zero-phase specialisation ($J_{\rm latt} = N_4^2/(2nN_6)$:

\section*{TECT-Math427. G1$'$: the diagonal Gaussian trial class cannot beat the isotropic gap; restoration robust; G1$''$ (Bogoliubov bands) formulated}

\subsection*{0. Summary}

The dispatched G1$'$ attack (Math426-AddA \S 2: two-parameter Bragg-cone
anisotropic trial propagator) is DISCHARGED by a proposition that covers
not only the cone family but every diagonal angular profile:

\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
&\text{Within } G^{-1}(q) = \hat r(\hat q) + c\,(q^2 - q_0^2)^2
\text{ (any } \hat r(\hat q) > 0\text{), with local quartic/sextic}\\
&\text{interactions Wick-contracted, every stationary trial profile is
ISOTROPIC almost everywhere: } \hat r(\hat q) = \text{const a.e.}
\end{aligned}}
\]

Consequently the Math426 corrected-canonical restoration result
($A^* = 0$ for LAM/HEX/FCC/BCC at $r_{\rm braz} = \mu^2 = 0.005$,
$r_R = 0.3045$, $M_R = 0.1094$) is the infimum over the ENTIRE diagonal
class --- anisotropic diagonal softening at the Bragg directions cannot
lower the ordered free energy below the isotropic value, hence cannot
break Reading-H selection. Numerical verification: 5/5 claims
(\texttt{Codes/supplementary/Math427\_g1prime\_diagonal\_isotropy.py};
\texttt{Runs/math/Math427/g1prime\_diagonal\_isotropy.json}).

\subsection*{1. Proposition and proof}

\paragraph{Setting.} Gibbs--Bogoliubov variational free energy at
condensate amplitude $A$ for reading $\mathcal R$ ($n$ pairs, exact
coefficients $N_4, N_6$ per Math424-AddA \S 2), with diagonal trial
propagator $G^{-1}(q) = \hat r(\hat q) + c\,(q^2 - q_0^2)^2$:
\[
F_{\rm var}[\hat r(\cdot), A]/V
= \tfrac12 \!\int_q \ln G^{-1}(q)
- \tfrac12 \!\int_q \hat r(\hat q)\, G(q)
+ \Phi\big(M_{\rm tot}, A\big),
\qquad
M_{\rm tot} = \int_q G(q),
\]
where $\Phi(M, A)$ collects the condensate terms and ALL interaction
terms; because the quartic/sextic interactions are local and the
Gaussian variance $\langle \delta\phi^2(x) \rangle = M_{\rm tot}$ is
position-independent for any homogeneous Gaussian state, $\Phi$ depends
on the trial profile ONLY through the scalar $M_{\rm tot}$ (the $c$-term
contributions cancel between $\langle H \rangle$ and
$\langle H_{\rm trial} \rangle$ exactly as in the isotropic case).

\paragraph{Hypotheses (v1.1, operator-directed).} A fixed UV
regularisation and a matched counterterm prescription are held common to
both sides of every comparison (the $\tfrac12\int_q \ln G^{-1}$ term is
UV-sensitive in the bare continuum; all statements are within one scheme).
The isotropy conclusion below holds ALMOST EVERYWHERE in $\hat q$:
measure-zero direction sets (e.g.\ isolated Bragg rays) do not affect the
continuum integrals and belong to the discrete/Bloch sector (G1$''$).

\paragraph{Proof.} Vary $\hat r(\hat q)$ pointwise in direction $\hat q$.
Writing the radial loop integrals $M_{\rm rad}(\rho)$ and using
$\partial M_{\rm tot} / \partial \hat r(\hat q) =
(d\Omega/4\pi)\, M_{\rm rad}'(\hat r(\hat q))$,
\[
\frac{\delta F_{\rm var}}{\delta \hat r(\hat q)}
= \frac{d\Omega}{4\pi}\, M_{\rm rad}'(\hat r(\hat q))
\left[ -\tfrac12 \hat r(\hat q) + \Phi'(M_{\rm tot}, A) \right]
\;=\; 0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\hat r(\hat q) = 2\,\Phi'(M_{\rm tot}, A).
\]
The right-hand side is direction-independent, so every stationary
profile is constant in $\hat q$ (isotropic), and the stationary value
reproduces exactly the isotropic ordered-phase gap equation of
Math424-AddA (G). Boundary escape is excluded: as $\hat r \to 0^+$ on
any direction set of positive measure, $M_{\rm rad} \to \infty$ (the
on-shell integrand $\propto 1/(\hat r + c(q^2-q_0^2)^2)$ diverges) and
the sextic term $\tfrac{5v}{2} M_{\rm tot}^3 \to +\infty$ dominates, so
$F_{\rm var} \to +\infty$; as $\hat r \to \infty$, $F_{\rm var}$ grows
through $-\tfrac12\hat r M + \tfrac12 \ln$-term balance. Hence the
infimum is attained at the (unique, per the Math400-AddE-type gap-map
monotonicity) isotropic stationary point. $\square$

\paragraph{Corollary (G1$'$ as dispatched: CLOSED-POSITIVE).} The
two-parameter Bragg-cone family ($\hat r_B$ on cones of half-angle $w$
about the $2n$ Bragg directions, solid-angle fraction
$f_B = n(1 - \cos w)$; $\hat r$ elsewhere) is a sub-family of the
diagonal class; its infimum over $(\hat r, \hat r_B, w, A)$ equals the
isotropic infimum, i.e.\ the Math426 restoration verdict. The required
inequality of Math426-AddA \S 2 HOLDS on this family.

\subsection*{2. Numerical verification (5/5 claims)}

Explicit cone-family $F_{\rm var}(A, \hat r, \hat r_B, w)$ for BCC and
HEX at the corrected canonical point: (i) implementation identity

\paragraph{Methodological record (falsification-discipline).} A first
test version compared grid-min against grid-min and reported a spurious
$2.6 \times 10^{-5}$ ``gain'' for HEX --- a pure discretisation artefact
(off-diagonal grid points landing nearer the continuum diagonal optimum
than any diagonal grid point). The test was redesigned to the
artifact-proof form ``subset-minimum $\ge$ continuum diagonal minimum'',
which cannot false-positive and still detects any true anisotropic
optimum (a genuine gain survives grid refinement; the proof of \S 1 is
the load-bearing statement, the scan its corroboration). Recorded per
CLAUDE.md 6.3.4 as a pre-registered-tolerance lesson: grid-vs-grid
comparisons must budget discretisation error.

\subsection*{3. What G1$'$ does NOT close: G1$''$ formulation (the real attack)}

$\delta\phi(q \pm k_i \pm k_j)$ through $3u\,\phi_n^2(x)\,\delta\phi^2$
(and $5v\,\phi_n^4\,\delta\phi^2$), producing a Bloch band structure
whose acoustic (phase/translation) branches are the crystal phonons.
G1$''$ (registered, top priority with G3$'$):

\boxed{
\begin{aligned}

\hat K[\phi_n] = \hat r_{\rm eff} + c(q^2-q_0^2)^2
+ 3u\,\phi_n^2 + 15 v M \phi_n^2 + 5v\,\phi_n^4 + \ldots\\[2pt]
&\text{Required: }
F^{\rm Bloch}_{\rm var}[\mathcal R_{\rm BCC}; A]
\;\ge\; F_{\rm var}[\mathcal R_H]
\quad \forall A,
\text{ at } r_{\rm braz} = 0.005 .
\end{aligned}}
\]

Computational plan (first cut, BCC only): plane-wave basis = reciprocal
set $\{G\}$ of the BCC condensate within a cutoff shell; Bloch blocks
