MF-condensate scale, the $26{\times}26$ grid minimum over
$(\hat r, \hat r_B)$ never falls below the CONTINUUM isotropic minimum
(golden-refined) --- maximum ``anisotropic gain'' $\le 10^{-9}$;
(iii) the global minimum over all scans remains $\Delta F = 0$ at
$A = 0$ (restoration unchanged); (iv) $r_R = 0.304526$, $M_R = 0.109414$
reproduce Math426.

\paragraph{Methodological record (falsification-discipline).} A first
test version compared grid-min against grid-min and reported a spurious
$2.6 \times 10^{-5}$ ``gain'' for HEX --- a pure discretisation artefact
(off-diagonal grid points landing nearer the continuum diagonal optimum
than any diagonal grid point). The test was redesigned to the
artifact-proof form ``subset-minimum $\ge$ continuum diagonal minimum'',
which cannot false-positive and still detects any true anisotropic
optimum (a genuine gain survives grid refinement; the proof of \S 1 is
the load-bearing statement, the scan its corroboration). Recorded per
CLAUDE.md 6.3.4 as a pre-registered-tolerance lesson: grid-vs-grid
comparisons must budget discretisation error.

\subsection*{3. What G1$'$ does NOT close: G1$''$ formulation (the real attack)}

The operator's physical concern --- ordered-phase soft modes lowering
$F_{\rm ordered}$ --- lives in the OFF-DIAGONAL sector excluded by the
diagonal class: the condensate couples $\delta\phi(q)$ to
$\delta\phi(q \pm k_i \pm k_j)$ through $3u\,\phi_n^2(x)\,\delta\phi^2$
(and $5v\,\phi_n^4\,\delta\phi^2$), producing a Bloch band structure
whose acoustic (phase/translation) branches are the crystal phonons.
G1$''$ (registered, top priority with G3$'$):

\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
&\text{Trial class: full homogeneous-ensemble Gaussian states with}\\
&\text{covariance } = \text{Wick-dressed Bloch operator }
\hat K[\phi_n] = \hat r_{\rm eff} + c(q^2-q_0^2)^2
+ 3u\,\phi_n^2 + 15 v M \phi_n^2 + 5v\,\phi_n^4 + \ldots\\[2pt]
&\text{Required: }
F^{\rm Bloch}_{\rm var}[\mathcal R_{\rm BCC}; A]
\;\ge\; F_{\rm var}[\mathcal R_H]
\quad \forall A,
\text{ at } r_{\rm braz} = 0.005 .
\end{aligned}}
\]

Computational plan (first cut, BCC only): plane-wave basis = reciprocal
set $\{G\}$ of the BCC condensate within a cutoff shell; Bloch blocks
$K_{G,G'}(k)$ on a sampled reduced BZ; matched-basis regularisation of
$\tfrac12 \mathrm{Tr}\ln K$ against the disordered reference (same
finite basis, isotropic $r_R$); existing infrastructure:
\texttt{Math374\_canonical\_BCC\_hessian.py} (Hessian assembly; Lanczos
$\lambda_{\min}$) extended to log-determinant; Math400-AddF
$n_{\rm neg} = 0$ already certifies spectral NON-NEGATIVITY of the
dressed operator at the channel state (no instability), so G1$''$ is a
free-energy race, not a stability question. Pre-registered outcomes:
PASS $\Rightarrow$ Reading-H selection robust at the full one-loop
Gaussian level (candidate T4 $\to$ T5 promotion of the selection
statement, subject to 15.5 independent audit); FAIL $\Rightarrow$
Math424 Outcome-3 branch.

\subsection*{4. Devil's-advocate self-test (CLAUDE.md 6.3.1 + 6.3.5(a))}

\textbf{Objection $\alpha$ (the class is too weak to address the
physics):} closing the diagonal family does not address crystal phonons.
\emph{UPHELD-as-designed}: this is exactly why G1$''$ is opened with a
concrete plan (\S 3); the note claims ONLY the diagonal-class closure
and does not upgrade the Reading-H selection tier.

\textbf{Objection $\beta$ (numerical-test design):} the initial
grid-vs-grid comparison produced a false positive; could the redesigned
test mask a true gain? \emph{DISMISSED}: subset-min $\ge$ continuum-min
is a one-sided inequality that holds identically when the continuum
optimum is diagonal and FAILS for any true anisotropic optimum once the
grid resolves it; the load-bearing statement is the \S 1 proof, which is
grid-free. The artefact episode is documented in \S 2.

\textbf{Objection $\gamma$ (boundary/soft-cone escape):} could
$\hat r_B \to 0$ (gapless Bragg cones, mimicking Goldstone softening)
lower $F$ outside the stationary analysis? \emph{DISMISSED}: the
on-shell radial integral diverges as $\hat r_B \to 0$ on any positive-
measure cone, and the $\tfrac{5v}{2}M_{\rm tot}^3$ sextic penalty sends
$F_{\rm var} \to +\infty$ (verified by the scan floor at small grid
$\hat r_B$). True gapless phonons require the off-diagonal sector
(G1$''$), where the divergence is cut by the Bogoliubov structure.

still diagonal class). 5/5 scripted claims; JSON artefact. PASS.

\section*{TECT-Math428. G1$''$-0: BCC Bloch log-det race --- finite-basis artefact diagnosed, continuum-anchored verdict PASS}

\subsection*{0. Summary}

The operator-specified Bloch operator
\[
K^{(k)}_{G,G'}(A,M) = \big[m_H^2 + c(|k+G|^2-q_0^2)^2\big]\delta_{GG'}
+ (3u+30vM)A^2\,p_2(G{-}G') + 5vA^4\,p_4(G{-}G'),
\qquad m_H^2 = r_{\rm braz} + 3uM + 15vM^2,
\]
was assembled exactly ($p_2, p_4$ = exact integer convolution counts of the
BCC shell; $p_2(0)=12$, $p_4(0)=540$ asserted) on the $D_3$ reciprocal
basis with matched reference $K_H = r_R + c(q^2-q_0^2)^2$ on the identical
basis/mesh, with the uniform-Wick counterterm
\[
C_{\rm unif}(A,M) = \big[-\tfrac{3u}{4}M^2 - 5vM^3 - 15vnA^2M^2\big]
- \big[-\tfrac{3u}{4}M_R^2 - 5vM_R^3\big]
\]
pinned by the EXACT diagonal-reduction identity: dropping off-diagonals
reproduces the Math424-AddA isotropic $\Delta F$ on the same finite basis
(verified to $10^{-10}$; the algebra is in Section 1). $A{=}0$ identity
$\Delta F = 0$ at $10^{-10}$; spectral positivity throughout
($\lambda_{\min} \approx 0.55$ at the scan minimum --- no soft modes,
consistent with Math400-AddF $n_{\rm neg}=0$).

\textbf{Verdict --- G1$''$-0 PASS UNDER THE CONTINUUM-ANCHORED
SECOND-ORDER/LOG-DET ESTIMATOR, $M = M_R$ FIXED, BCC FIRST-SHELL ONLY
(operator-mandated qualifier, v1.1; this is an estimator PASS, not a
fully-converged matched Bloch log-det theorem, and NOT an unconditional
G1$''$ closure):}
\[
\boxed{\;\Delta F^{\rm Bloch}_{\rm est}(A) > 0 \quad \forall A \in [0.02, 0.14],
\quad \min = +7.3\times 10^{-4}\ (\text{calibrated}),\;
+6.7\times 10^{-4}\ (\text{worst case})\;}
\]
Reading-H selection SURVIVES the off-diagonal Bloch attack at the G1$''$-0
protocol. The off-diagonal softening is real and sizeable (the operator's
physical intuition is confirmed: it contributes $\sim -0.021$ at the
finite-basis minimiser, second-order continuum bubble), but the exactly-
anchored isotropic penalty ($+0.0227$ there) outweighs it at every
amplitude.

\subsection*{1. Counterterm derivation (diagonal-reduction pinning)}

Gibbs--Bogoliubov with trial kernel $\hat K_{\phi,M}$ around
$\phi_A = A\sum_{j=1}^{2n} e^{ik_j x}$ gives
$F_{\rm var} = F_{\rm cl} + \tfrac12\mathrm{Tr}\ln\hat K + \langle H - H_{\rm trial}\rangle$;
in the uniform-variance (Hartree) treatment $\sigma(x) \to M$ the remainder
evaluates to $C_{\rm unif}$ above. Substituting the disordered gap relation
$r_R = r + 3uM_R + 15vM_R^2$ shows term-by-term agreement with the
Math424-AddA $\Delta F$ formula; numerically the identity holds to
$10^{-10}$ on every tested basis. The diagonal of the Bloch matrix is
exactly the isotropic ordered kernel ($p_2(0) = 2n$, $p_4(0) = N_4$), so
the OFF-DIAGONAL share is cleanly isolated as
$\Delta F_{\rm full} - \Delta F_{\rm diag}$.

\subsection*{2. Finite matched-basis race: apparent FAIL and its diagnosis}

Fixed $M = M_R$ scan ($|G_{\rm int}|^2 \le 12$, 87 vectors, $4^3$ shifted
mesh): $\min_A \Delta F = -7.05\times 10^{-3}$ at $A^* = 0.0856$ ---
nominally a FAIL by the pre-registered thresholds. Convergence
decomposition at $(A^*, M_R)$:

\subsection*{3. Continuum-anchored estimator (primary verdict path)}

\[
\Delta F_{\rm est}(A) = \underbrace{\Delta F_{\rm diag}^{\rm continuum}(A)}_{\rm exact\ radial\ integrals}
+ \rho \cdot \underbrace{\Big[-\tfrac14 \sum_{Q\neq 0} W(Q)^2\, B(|Q|)\Big]}_{\rm 2nd\text{-}order\ bubble,\ convergent},
\qquad
B(|Q|) = \int\!\frac{d^3q}{(2\pi)^3}\, G_d(q)\, G_d(q{+}Q),
\]
with $W(Q) = (3u+30vM_R)A^2 p_2(Q) + 5vA^4 p_4(Q)$ and the resummation
ratio $\rho$ calibrated in-basis (exact vs.\ second order on the SAME
basis): $\rho = 0.416$ (cut 16), $0.414$ (cut 20) --- stable to $0.5\%$,
asserted. Worst case $\rho = 1$ (no resummation credit) is also reported.

\subsection*{3bis. Analytic amplitude bounds (v1.1; operator-audit weakness 3)}

\paragraph{Small $A$ (closes $A < 0.02$).} Expanding the anchored
estimator at $A \to 0$: $\hat r(0) = m_H^2(M_R) = r + 3uM_R + 15vM_R^2
= r_R$ and $d\hat r/dA^2|_0 = 2n(3u + 30vM_R)$, so
\[
\Delta F_{\rm est}(A) = c_2 A^2 + O(A^4),\qquad
c_2 = n\big[r + 3uM_R + 30vM_R^2 - 15vM_R^2\big] = n\, r_R
= 6 \times 0.304526 = 1.8272 \;>\; 0 ,
\]
exactly (the off-diagonal share is $O(A^4)$: $W \propto A^2$). Numerical
cross-check: $\Delta F_{\rm est}(0.02)/A^2 = 1.815$ ($0.7\%$ from
$c_2$; scripted claim). The region $A < 0.02$ is therefore closed
analytically with positive margin.

\paragraph{Large $A$ (closes $A > 0.14$).} The classical sextic dominates:
$F_{\rm cl} \sim (v/6) N_6 A^6$ with $C_6 = (v/6)N_6 = 22809.6 > 0$,
while $\tfrac12\Delta I = O(\ln A)$, $C_{\rm unif} = O(A^2)$, and the
second-order off-diagonal share is bounded by
\[
|\Delta F^{(2)}_{\rm offdiag}| \le \tfrac14 \sum_{Q\neq0} W(Q)^2\, B(0),
\qquad B(0) = -M'(\hat r) \sim \tfrac{q_0^2}{8\pi\sqrt{c}}\,\hat r^{-3/2},
\quad \hat r \sim 5vN_4A^4 ,
\]
so $W^2 B \sim A^8 \cdot A^{-6} = O(A^2) \ll A^6$. Scripted spot check:
$\Delta F_{\rm est}(0.30) = +15.9 > \tfrac12 C_6 (0.30)^6$. The scan
window $[0.02, 0.14]$ together with these two bounds covers all $A \ge 0$.

\subsection*{5. Devil's-advocate self-test (CLAUDE.md 6.3.1 + 6.3.5(a))}

\textbf{$\alpha$ (scheme mixing):} anchoring the diagonal on continuum
integrals while computing off-diagonals in basis mixes regularisations.
\emph{DISMISSED}: the diagonal anchor evaluates the SAME functional
exactly (the identity of Section 1 ties the two representations at
$10^{-10}$); the off-diagonal share is the convergent continuum bubble;
only the resummation ratio is taken from basis, and the verdict is
insensitive to it (positive even at $\rho = 1$).

\textbf{$\beta$ (calibration transfer):} the in-basis ratio may not
transfer to the continuum bubble. \emph{VALID-with-band}: this is exactly
why the worst-case $\rho = 1$ band is reported; both bands positive.
A $\rho > 1$ (anti-resummation) would be needed to flip the verdict ---
excluded by the alternating-sign structure of the expansion
($W/\hat r \sim 0.3$ at the minimiser) and by both in-basis measurements.

\textbf{$\gamma$ (the discarded $(A,M)$-scan negative):} ignoring the
$-0.102$ could hide a real instability. \emph{UPHELD-as-gate}: it is NOT
ignored --- it is recorded, diagnosed (boundary minimum under a
counterterm outside its validity window), and assigned to G1$''$-1$'$,
which must close before any tier promotion of the selection statement.

\textbf{$\delta$ (initial FAIL announcement):} the finite-basis FAIL was
provisionally reported in-session before the convergence diagnosis.
\emph{Documented}: this note records the full inversion arc; the lesson
(quadrature-artefact class; anchor the exactly-computable part before
verdicts) is registered in Section 6 for the recurrence ledger.

$\neq$ continuum convergence; when one part of a race is exactly
computable, ANCHOR it before reading off a verdict (candidate addition to
POSTMORTEM_RECURRENCE_POLICY at next policy edit).

C_{\rm unif}(A,M) = \big[-\tfrac{3u}{4}M^2 - 5vM^3 - 15vnA^2M^2\big]
- \big[-\tfrac{3u}{4}M_R^2 - 5vM_R^3\big]
\]
pinned by the EXACT diagonal-reduction identity: dropping off-diagonals
reproduces the Math424-AddA isotropic $\Delta F$ on the same finite basis
(verified to $10^{-10}$; the algebra is in Section 1). $A{=}0$ identity
$\Delta F = 0$ at $10^{-10}$; spectral positivity throughout
($\lambda_{\min} \approx 0.55$ at the scan minimum --- no soft modes,
consistent with Math400-AddF $n_{\rm neg}=0$).

\textbf{Verdict (G1$''$-0, $M = M_R$, BCC):}
\[
\boxed{\;\Delta F^{\rm Bloch}_{\rm est}(A) > 0 \quad \forall A \in [0.02, 0.14],
\quad \min = +7.3\times 10^{-4}\ (\text{calibrated}),\;
+6.7\times 10^{-4}\ (\text{worst case})\;}
\]
Reading-H selection SURVIVES the off-diagonal Bloch attack at the G1$''$-0
protocol. The off-diagonal softening is real and sizeable (the operator's
physical intuition is confirmed: it contributes $\sim -0.021$ at the
finite-basis minimiser, second-order continuum bubble), but the exactly-
anchored isotropic penalty ($+0.0227$ there) outweighs it at every
amplitude.

\subsection*{1. Counterterm derivation (diagonal-reduction pinning)}

Gibbs--Bogoliubov with trial kernel $\hat K_{\phi,M}$ around
$\phi_A = A\sum_{j=1}^{2n} e^{ik_j x}$ gives
$F_{\rm var} = F_{\rm cl} + \tfrac12\mathrm{Tr}\ln\hat K + \langle H - H_{\rm trial}\rangle$;
in the uniform-variance (Hartree) treatment $\sigma(x) \to M$ the remainder
evaluates to $C_{\rm unif}$ above. Substituting the disordered gap relation
$r_R = r + 3uM_R + 15vM_R^2$ shows term-by-term agreement with the
Math424-AddA $\Delta F$ formula; numerically the identity holds to
$10^{-10}$ on every tested basis. The diagonal of the Bloch matrix is
exactly the isotropic ordered kernel ($p_2(0) = 2n$, $p_4(0) = N_4$), so
the OFF-DIAGONAL share is cleanly isolated as
$\Delta F_{\rm full} - \Delta F_{\rm diag}$.

\subsection*{2. Finite matched-basis race: apparent FAIL and its diagnosis}

Fixed $M = M_R$ scan ($|G_{\rm int}|^2 \le 12$, 87 vectors, $4^3$ shifted
mesh): $\min_A \Delta F = -7.05\times 10^{-3}$ at $A^* = 0.0856$ ---
nominally a FAIL by the pre-registered thresholds. Convergence
decomposition at $(A^*, M_R)$:

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{|l|c|c|c|c|}

$\Delta F_{\rm diag}$ drifts $+0.005$/shell toward its EXACT continuum

$|q| \approx q_0$ shell only at lattice points and grossly under-counts
the positive fluctuation penalty. The finite-basis negative is therefore a
QUADRATURE ARTEFACT, not physics --- matched-basis internal consistency
does not imply continuum convergence.

\subsection*{3. Continuum-anchored estimator (primary verdict path)}

\[
\Delta F_{\rm est}(A) = \underbrace{\Delta F_{\rm diag}^{\rm continuum}(A)}_{\rm exact\ radial\ integrals}
+ \rho \cdot \underbrace{\Big[-\tfrac14 \sum_{Q\neq 0} W(Q)^2\, B(|Q|)\Big]}_{\rm 2nd\text{-}order\ bubble,\ convergent},
\qquad
B(|Q|) = \int\!\frac{d^3q}{(2\pi)^3}\, G_d(q)\, G_d(q{+}Q),
\]
with $W(Q) = (3u+30vM_R)A^2 p_2(Q) + 5vA^4 p_4(Q)$ and the resummation
ratio $\rho$ calibrated in-basis (exact vs.\ second order on the SAME
basis): $\rho = 0.416$ (cut 16), $0.414$ (cut 20) --- stable to $0.5\%$,
asserted. Worst case $\rho = 1$ (no resummation credit) is also reported.

\subsection*{5. Devil's-advocate self-test (CLAUDE.md 6.3.1 + 6.3.5(a))}

\textbf{$\alpha$ (scheme mixing):} anchoring the diagonal on continuum
integrals while computing off-diagonals in basis mixes regularisations.
\emph{DISMISSED}: the diagonal anchor evaluates the SAME functional
exactly (the identity of Section 1 ties the two representations at
$10^{-10}$); the off-diagonal share is the convergent continuum bubble;
only the resummation ratio is taken from basis, and the verdict is
insensitive to it (positive even at $\rho = 1$).

\textbf{$\beta$ (calibration transfer):} the in-basis ratio may not
transfer to the continuum bubble. \emph{VALID-with-band}: this is exactly
why the worst-case $\rho = 1$ band is reported; both bands positive.
A $\rho > 1$ (anti-resummation) would be needed to flip the verdict ---
excluded by the alternating-sign structure of the expansion
($W/\hat r \sim 0.3$ at the minimiser) and by both in-basis measurements.

\textbf{$\gamma$ (the discarded $(A,M)$-scan negative):} ignoring the
$-0.102$ could hide a real instability. \emph{UPHELD-as-gate}: it is NOT
ignored --- it is recorded, diagnosed (boundary minimum under a
counterterm outside its validity window), and assigned to G1$''$-1$'$,
which must close before any tier promotion of the selection statement.

\textbf{$\delta$ (initial FAIL announcement):} the finite-basis FAIL was
provisionally reported in-session before the convergence diagnosis.
\emph{Documented}: this note records the full inversion arc; the lesson
(quadrature-artefact class; anchor the exactly-computable part before
verdicts) is registered in Section 6 for the recurrence ledger.

Limit case $A \to 0$: est.\ $\to 0^+$ quadratically (diag $\propto A^2$

$\neq$ continuum convergence; when one part of a race is exactly
computable, ANCHOR it before reading off a verdict (candidate addition to

\section*{TECT-Math429. G1$''$-1$'$: exact inhomogeneous Wick dissolves the $M$-scan negative; PASS}

\subsection*{0. Summary}

Implementing the operator's specification verbatim: the uniform variance
assumption $\sigma(x) \to M$ is replaced by the exact Bloch Green diagonal
\[
\sigma_A(x) = G_{\phi_A}(x,x), \qquad
\hat\sigma(Q) = \frac{1}{v_{\rm cell} N_k}\sum_k \sum_G
\big[K^{(k)}\big]^{-1}_{G,\,G+Q},
\]
and the exact Wick remainder is used in the Gibbs--Bogoliubov functional
\[
F_{\rm var}/V = F_{\rm cl}(A) + \tfrac12\,\overline{\mathrm{Tr}\ln K}
- \tfrac12(3uM{+}15vM^2)\,\bar\sigma - 15vM\,\overline{\phi_A^2\sigma}
+ \tfrac{3u}{4}\,\overline{\sigma^2} + \tfrac{15v}{2}\,\overline{\phi_A^2\sigma^2}
+ \tfrac{5v}{2}\,\overline{\sigma^3},
\]
with all cell averages computed exactly (band-limited $48^3$ grid;
$\hat\sigma(Q)$ from per-$k$ inversion of the full Bloch matrix). With
this remainder $F_{\rm var}(A,M)$ is a TRUE variational upper bound for
every $(A,M)$, and at $A = 0$ its $M$-stationarity reproduces the
disordered gap equation, so the Reading-H reference is the $A{=}0$
optimum of the SAME functional (implementation identity exact $=$
diagonal at $W{=}0$: $10^{-10}$; continuum reference zero and $M$-optimal
at $M_R$: asserted).

\textbf{Verdict (13/13 claims; physics outcome recorded, not asserted):}
\[
\boxed{\;
\Delta F^{\rm inhomWick}(A, M) > 0 \quad \text{at every scanned point},\quad
\min_{\rm in\text{-}basis} = +0.0046,\quad
\min_{\rm anchored} = +0.0077,\;}
\]
over $A \in \{0.06, 0.0856, 0.114\}$ (the dangerous window),
$M \in [0.6, 2.2]\,M_R$ (extended beyond the old boundary). The
$M$-direction minima are INTERIOR ($\approx 0.66$--$0.88\,M_R$), not at
the window edge.

\subsection*{1. Autopsy of the uniform-Wick $-0.102$}

At the old artefact point $(A, M) = (0.114, 1.6\,M_R)$ the exact-Wick
values are $+0.060$ (in-basis) and $+0.092$ (anchored) --- an inversion
of $\sim 0.16$. Mechanism: the exact remainder uses the ACTUAL trial
variance, and $\bar\sigma$ DECREASES monotonically with $M$ (e.g.\ at
$A = 0.06$: $\bar\sigma = 0.042 \to 0.014$ as $M: M_R \to 2.2 M_R$),
because the kernel mass $m_H^2(M) = r + 3uM + 15vM^2$ stiffens. The
uniform-Wick counterterm instead substituted the scan parameter $M$
itself, producing the spurious $-5vM^3 - 15vnA^2M^2$ runaway that
manufactured the boundary negative. G1$''$-1$'$ thereby CONFIRMS the
Math428 classification of $-0.102$ as a counterterm-validity artefact ---
now by direct computation rather than interpretation.

\subsection*{2. Method (anchoring, reference-free bracket)}

$\Delta F_{\rm anchored}(A,M) = \Delta F^{\rm cont}_{\rm diag}(A,M)
+ \big[F^{\rm exact}_{\rm basis}(A,M) - F^{\rm diag}_{\rm basis}(A,M)\big]$:
the continuum diagonal-limit closed form (radial integrals; reference
$(0, M_R)$ built in, $= 0$ there) plus the in-basis off-diagonal $+$
$\sigma$-inhomogeneity bracket, which needs NO reference subtraction
because exact $\equiv$ diagonal at $A = 0$ identically. This extends the
Math428 anchoring protocol to the exact-Wick functional; the basis-trace
quadrature shift (the in-basis $A{=}0$ optimum sits below $M_R$;
recorded) affects only the diagnostic in-basis race, not the anchored
construction.

\subsection*{3. Devil's-advocate self-test (CLAUDE.md 6.3.1 + 6.3.5(a))}

\textbf{$\alpha$ (coarse $A$-grid):} three amplitudes only.
\emph{VALID-with-coverage}: the three points bracket the dangerous region
identified by Math428 (finite-basis minimiser $0.0856$, MF amplitude
$0.057$, old artefact $0.114$); $A < 0.02$ and $A > 0.14$ are closed
analytically at $M = M_R$ by Math428 v1.1 \S 3bis, and the observed
$M$-dependence is monotone-benign (positive everywhere, interior minima);
a denser $(A, M)$ surface belongs to G1$''$-2.
\textbf{$\beta$ (bracket at cut 12 only):} the off-diagonal bracket could
drift with cutoff. \emph{VALID-with-margin}: in Math428 the bracket
magnitude grew only mildly with cutoff ($-0.005 \to -0.007$) while the
anchored minimum here is $+0.0077$ --- an order above that drift scale;
full convergence sweep = G1$''$-2.
\textbf{$\gamma$ (self-consistency vs scan):} the trial family is
parameterised by $(A, M)$ rather than solving $\sigma$-self-consistency.
\emph{DISMISSED-as-stronger}: minimising the true upper bound over the
$(A,M)$ family DOMINATES any self-consistent point of the family; a
self-consistent solution can only sit at or above the scanned minimum,
which is positive.

\section{Math432: G3' two-shell ensemble race --- \{110\}+\{200\} CLOSED-PASS}

\subsection{Dispatch context}

The G1'' programme (Math427--Math431) closed the single-shell enumerated
readings at estimator-to-exact-Wick grade. The operator-registered G3'
question (OPEN-QUESTIONS, 2026-06-04) shifts the attack from single-shell
readings to \emph{multi-shell / higher-harmonic ensembles}: can a condensate
enriched with second-harmonic content beat the disordered Reading-H
reference at the Gaussian variational level? The dispatch spec fixes the
minimal ensemble as the first two BCC shells,
\begin{equation}
\phi_c(\mathbf{x}) \;=\; A_1 \sum_{\mathbf{k} \in \{110\}} e^{i\mathbf{k}\cdot\mathbf{x}}
\;+\; A_2 \sum_{\mathbf{k} \in \{200\}} e^{i\mathbf{k}\cdot\mathbf{x}},
\qquad |\mathbf{k}_{\{110\}}| = q_0,\quad |\mathbf{k}_{\{200\}}| = \sqrt{2}\,q_0,
\end{equation}
with the D3 reciprocal lattice unchanged, per-shell amplitudes $(A_1, A_2)$
scanned together with the variational mass $M$, and the anchored exact-Wick
protocol of Math429/430 applied verbatim. Outcomes were pre-registered
(CLAUDE.md \S 6.3.3): FAIL $\Leftrightarrow$ some scanned $(A_1, A_2, M)$ has
anchored $\Delta F < 0$ confirmed at both cut-12/$48^3$ and cut-20/$64^3$
$\Rightarrow$ Math424 Outcome-3; PASS $\Leftrightarrow$ all points positive
with convergence margins exceeding the last-step drift $\Rightarrow$ T5
candidacy of the Reading-H selection statement proceeds to the \S 15.5
independent audit.

\subsection{Why G3' is structurally dangerous: the SHG resonance}

The two shells are coupled by an exact 4-wave resonance: with
$\mathbf{k}_1 = (1,1,0)$, $\mathbf{k}_2 = (1,0,1)$, $\mathbf{k}_3 = (0,-1,-1)$
(all in the first shell, units $s = q_0/\sqrt{2}$) and
$\mathbf{k}_4 = (2,0,0)$ in the second shell,
$\mathbf{k}_1 + \mathbf{k}_2 + \mathbf{k}_3 - \mathbf{k}_4 = 0$. Consequently
the cross moment
\begin{equation}
m_{31} \;=\; \big\langle \varphi_1^3\,\varphi_2 \big\rangle \;=\; 144
\qquad (\text{exact; } 4 \text{ unordered shell-1 triples} \times 3! \times 6
\text{ shell-2 partners})
\end{equation}
is nonzero, so the free energy contains the second-harmonic-generation (SHG)
tilt $u\,m_{31} A_1^3 A_2$ at classical level: \emph{the single-shell BCC
point is not stationary in the two-shell space}. The optimal $A_2^*$ is
strictly nonzero for every $A_1 > 0$, and the enriched ensemble is
guaranteed to undercut the single-shell BCC channel at equal $A_1$. The G1''
chain never probed this direction; G3' asks whether the enrichment can
reach below the disordered reference itself. The remaining structural
constants are $m_{22} = \langle \varphi_1^2 \varphi_2^2\rangle = 96$,
$\langle \varphi_2^4 \rangle = 90$, and the kernel value on the second
shell,
\begin{equation}
K_2 \;=\; r_{\rm braz} + C\,(2q_0^2 - q_0^2)^2 \;=\; \mu_2 + C\,q_0^4
\;=\; 0.219034,
\end{equation}
numerically identical to $K(0)$ -- the \{200\} shell sits as far off the
$q_0$ sphere (in kernel units) as the homogeneous mode, which is the
Math426 convention cross-check.

\subsection{Protocol}

Identical to Math429/430 with the condensate generalised: Bloch operator on
the exact D3 basis (cut $|G|^2 \le 12$, basis 87; the \{200\} shell is
in-basis, $|G|^2 = 4$),
\begin{equation}
K^{(k)}_{GG'} = \big[m_H^2 + C(|k+G|^2 - q_0^2)^2\big]\delta_{GG'}
+ (3u + 30vM)\,\widehat{\phi_c^2}(G-G') + 5v\,\widehat{\phi_c^4}(G-G'),
\end{equation}
$m_H^2 = r + 3uM + 15vM^2$, with $\widehat{\phi_c^2},\ \widehat{\phi_c^4}$
extracted by forward FFT of the band-limited grid fields (exact by the
Nyquist guard $3 \times 6 = 18 < 24$; verified max imaginary part
$< 10^{-9}$). Exact inhomogeneous Wick remainder with
$\sigma(\mathbf{x})$ the Bloch Green diagonal (FFT-reconstructed), all cell
averages exact on $48^3$. Classical sector
\begin{equation}
F_{\rm cl} = r\,n_1 A_1^2 + K_2\, n_2 A_2^2
+ \tfrac{u}{4}\,\langle\phi_c^4\rangle + \tfrac{v}{6}\,\langle\phi_c^6\rangle,
\qquad n_1 = 6,\ n_2 = 3,
\end{equation}
with all condensate moments exact grid means. Anchored estimator as in
Math430: $\Delta F_{\rm anc} = \Delta F^{\rm cont}_{\rm diag} +
\big(F_{\rm exact} - F^{\rm basis}_{\rm diag}\big)$, reference = disordered
optimum $(A_1 = A_2 = 0,\ M = M_R)$, $r_R = 0.30453$, $M_R = 0.10941$.

\subsection{Results (25/25 scripted claims)}

\textbf{Scan.} $A_1 \in \{0.01, \ldots, 0.14\}$ (8) $\times\ A_2 \in
\{-0.12, \ldots, +0.12\}\setminus\{0\}$ (10, both signs) $\times\ M \in
\{0.7, 1.0, 1.4\} M_R$ (3), plus the pure-\{200\} column ($A_1 = 0$): 244
points, all positive-definite, \textbf{0 negatives}. Minimum
$+5.536 \times 10^{-4}$ at $(A_1, A_2, M) = (0.01, +0.015, M_R)$.

\textbf{Zoom.} Local refinement at the argmin: minimum
$+2.302 \times 10^{-4}$ at $(0.01, +0.005, M_R)$ -- the $A_2 \to 0$,
$A_1 \to 0$ corner, reproducing the two-shell small-amplitude bound (below)
to 3.9\%. The surface rises in every direction away from the disordered
point; there is no two-shell valley.

\textbf{Tilt (non-stationarity) confirmed.} At $(A_1, M) = (0.0856, M_R)$:
$\Delta F_{\rm anc}(A_2 = +0.03) = +0.0395$ vs
$\Delta F_{\rm anc}(A_2 = -0.03) = +0.0225$ -- the SHG tilt is active
($|\Delta| \approx 0.017$, far above numerical noise) and the favorable
branch is $A_2 < 0$ at this point: the classical quartic tilt
$u\,m_{31}A_1^3 A_2$ (favoring $A_2 > 0$ for $u < 0$) is overridden by the
sextic and Wick-dressed cross moments. Both branches remain positive
everywhere scanned.

\textbf{Convergence (cut-12/$48^3$ vs cut-20/$64^3$, basis 87 vs 201).}
Argmin: $+0.000230 \to +0.000230$ (drift $< 10^{-6}$, $\ge 100\times$
margin separation); dangerous mixed points $(0.01, \pm 0.015, M_R)$:
drift $\le 2\times 10^{-6}$ vs margins $+5.5\times 10^{-4}$; legacy
single-shell anchor $(0.0856, 0, 0.7M_R)$: $+0.023450 \to +0.022142$,
identical to the Math430 record. This is the cleanest convergence
separation in the G1''/G3' series because the minimum sits in the
small-amplitude regime where the bracket is nearly converged already.

\subsection{Two-shell small-amplitude bound}

The Math428 v1.1 small-$A$ derivation is shell-additive at quadratic order
(shells are orthogonal; the SHG cross term is cubic in amplitudes):
\begin{equation}
\Delta F_{\rm est} = c_2^{(1)} A_1^2 + c_2^{(2)} A_2^2
+ O(A^3_{\rm mixed}, A^4), \qquad
c_2^{(s)} = n_s\big[r_R + C(k_s^2 - q_0^2)^2\big],
\end{equation}
giving $c_2^{(1)} = 6\,r_R = 1.8272$ (Math428 v1.1, unchanged) and
$c_2^{(2)} = 3\,(r_R + C q_0^4) = 1.5557$, verified numerically to 2.7\% at
$A_2 = 0.01$ (claim \texttt{smallA2\_bound\_10pct}). Every off-sphere shell
$s \ge 2$ carries the strictly positive stiffness excess
$n_s\,C(k_s^2-q_0^2)^2$: at quadratic order \emph{no} harmonic enrichment
direction is soft. The danger is confined to the cubic SHG tilt, which the
scan bounds directly: the induced optimum $A_2^* = O(|u| m_{31} A_1^3 /
2c_2^{(2)}) \lesssim 0.025$ on the scanned $A_1$ range, well inside the
$A_2$ grid, and the free-energy gain it produces never approaches the
disordered baseline.

\subsection{Devil's-advocate self-test (CLAUDE.md \S 6.3, \S 6.3.5(a))}

\textbf{Objection $\alpha$ (ensemble coverage).} Only two shells; shells
$\ge 3$, incommensurate wavevectors, and quasicrystalline ensembles are
unscanned. \emph{VALID with mitigation}: at quadratic order every
off-sphere shell is stiff ($c_2^{(3)} = 12\,[r_R + 4Cq_0^4] = 13.93$ for
\{211\} -- an order of magnitude above $c_2^{(1)}$, with stiffness growing
as $(k_s^2 - q_0^2)^2$); the unique structurally dangerous low-order
channel (the SHG resonance) is probed directly. Residual registered as
G3'-b(i): shells $\ge 3$ at large amplitude (sextic-dominance argument of
Math428 v1.1 \S 3bis extends but has not been re-derived for mixed shells).

\textbf{Objection $\beta$ (phase restriction).} The ansatz is real-even
with a single isotropic $A_2$ across the three \{200\} cosine pairs;
anisotropic per-axis second harmonics (tetragonal SHG) and generic relative
phases are unscanned. \emph{VALID with mitigation}: the physical target
(Math400-AddF N=64 BCC channel) is cubic-symmetric, forcing an isotropic
second harmonic; the sign scan $\pm A_2$ captures both extremes of the
single SHG phase channel. Residual registered as G3'-b(ii).

\textbf{Objection $\gamma$ (estimator grade).} The anchored estimator is
not a fully-converged log-det (recurring Math428--431 objection).
\emph{VALID with qualifier}: the verdict language carries the mandatory
estimator qualifier; mitigation is quantitative -- argmin drift
$< 10^{-6}$ vs margin $2.3\times 10^{-4}$ ($\ge 100\times$), the strongest
separation in the series.

\textbf{Quantitative sanity checks (\S 6.3.4).}
(i) \emph{Magnitude/regression}: $K_2 = 0.219034$ independently reproduces
the Math426 kernel forensics value $K(0) = 0.219$; $\langle\varphi_1^6\rangle
= 42240 = N_6$ and $\langle\varphi_1^4\rangle = 540 = N_4$ reproduce the

(iii) \emph{Small-amplitude consistency}: zoom minimum $+2.302\times10^{-4}$

(3.9\%, consistent with the $O(A^4)$ and tilt corrections); scan minimum

(iv) \emph{Sign-direction physics}: the tilt asymmetry is nonzero (SHG

module, and the primary JSON artefacts, and re-derived the load-bearing
algebra independently before forming any verdict. Every formula quoted
below was re-derived by the auditor, not transcribed.

Constants throughout (chain convention, Math426): $u = -0.86$, $v = 3.24$,
$q_0 = 0.6801747616$, $C = 1$, $r_{\rm braz} = \mu_2 = 0.005$; disordered
reference $r_R = 0.304526$, $M_R = 0.109414$.

\subsection{Task 3 (taken first; it underpins tasks 1--2): exact-Wick
remainder algebra --- DISMISSED (independently confirmed)}

\textbf{Re-derivation.} For $F[\phi] = \frac12\int\phi K_0\phi
+ \frac{u}{4}\int\phi^4 + \frac{v}{6}\int\phi^6$, Gaussian reference with
covariance $G = \hat K^{-1}$, $\sigma(x) = G(x,x)$, condensate $\phi_c$,
the Gibbs--Bogoliubov functional is
$F_{\rm var} = \frac12\,\overline{\operatorname{Tr}\ln \hat K} + F_{\rm cl}[\phi_c]
+ \langle H_{\rm int}\rangle - \frac12\operatorname{Tr}[(\hat K - K_0)\hat K^{-1}]/V$
with trial kernel $\hat K = m_H^2 + C(q^2-q_0^2)^2 + (3u+30vM)\phi_c^2
+ 5v\phi_c^4$, $m_H^2 = r + 3uM + 15vM^2$. Wick moments:
$\langle\phi^4\rangle = \phi_c^4 + 6\phi_c^2\sigma + 3\sigma^2$,
$\langle\phi^6\rangle = \phi_c^6 + 15\phi_c^4\sigma + 45\phi_c^2\sigma^2
+ 15\sigma^3$. Collecting per cell-average:
\begin{align*}
\overline{\phi_c^2\sigma}:&\quad \tfrac{6u}{4} - \tfrac{3u}{2} - 15vM
= -15vM \qquad\checkmark\ (\text{script: } -15vM\,\texttt{p2s})\\
\overline{\sigma^2}:&\quad \tfrac{3u}{4} \qquad\checkmark\\
\overline{\phi_c^4\sigma}:&\quad \tfrac{15v}{6} - \tfrac{5v}{2} = 0
\qquad\checkmark\ (\text{correctly ABSENT from the scripts})\\
\overline{\phi_c^2\sigma^2}:&\quad \tfrac{45v}{6} = \tfrac{15v}{2}
\qquad\checkmark\\
\overline{\sigma^3}:&\quad \tfrac{15v}{6} = \tfrac{5v}{2}\qquad\checkmark\\
\bar\sigma:&\quad -\tfrac12(3uM + 15vM^2)\qquad\checkmark
\end{align*}
All five remainder coefficients of Math429 \S 0 (and the identical blocks
in the Math430/431/432 engines) are confirmed coefficient-by-coefficient;
the exact cancellation of the $\overline{\phi_c^4\sigma}$ term is a
non-trivial cross-check the chain implementation passes. (i) Upper-bound
property: standard Gibbs--Bogoliubov for any positive-definite $\hat K$;
positivity is enforced per-$k$ by the \texttt{slogdet} sign guard in every
engine. \emph{Caveat (recorded, not a defect)}: on a FINITE basis/k-mesh the
inequality holds for the basis-projected theory; transfer to the continuum
is exactly what the anchoring protocol (task 1) addresses. (ii) $A = 0$
identity: with $W = 0$, $\sigma$ uniform, the remainder reduces to
$-\frac12(3uM{+}15vM^2)M_t + \frac{3u}{4}M_t^2 + \frac{5v}{2}M_t^3$ and
$M$-stationarity reproduces the disordered gap equation; the auditor
additionally verified $\partial\,\mathrm{rem}/\partial M_t = 0$ at
$(A{=}0, M{=}M_t{=}M_R)$ exactly (term-pair cancellation), which is the
structural reason the anchored construction is first-order protected
against small $M_t$ errors (used in task 1c below). (iii) The diagonal
closed form's substitutions $\overline{\phi_c^2\sigma}\to 2nA^2M_t$,
$\overline{\phi_c^2\sigma^2}\to 2nA^2M_t^2$ are the correct uniform-$\sigma$
limits. \textbf{Verdict: DISMISSED} --- the remainder algebra is correct.

\subsection{Task 1: anchored-estimator construction at the $10^{-5}$
scale --- DISMISSED, with two VALID-with-mitigation sub-findings}

\textbf{(1a) Decomposition identity and reference consistency.} The
anchored object is
\[
\Delta F_{\rm anc}(A,M) = \big[F^{\rm cont}_{\rm diag}(A,M)
- F^{\rm cont}_{\rm diag}(0,M_R)\big]
+ \big[F^{\rm basis}_{\rm exact}(A,M) - F^{\rm basis}_{\rm diag}(A,M)\big].
\]
Because $F_{\rm exact}\equiv F_{\rm diag}$ at $A=0$ identically (verified at
$10^{-10}$ in every gate), the EXACT identity
$\Delta F_{\rm true} = \Delta F^{\rm cont}_{\rm diag}
+ [F^{\rm cont}_{\rm exact} - F^{\rm cont}_{\rm diag}]$ holds, and the
anchored estimator differs from $\Delta F_{\rm true}$ ONLY by the
continuum-vs-basis error of the BRACKET --- a single, clean substitution.
Both bracket members are evaluated on the same functional, the same
\texttt{den} arrays, the same k-mesh, the same remainder structure; the
continuum anchor (\texttt{F\_diag\_cont\_rel}) is the same functional in the
diagonal limit with the $(0, M_R)$ reference built in
(\texttt{continuum\_ref\_zero} at $10^{-9}$ in all gates). DISMISSED.

\textbf{(1c) Diagonal/off-diagonal boundary: no double-count, no omission.}
Auditor code-level check: the diagonal of the Bloch coupling is
$W_{ii} = \mathrm{cou2}\,p_2(0) + \mathrm{cou4}\,p_4(0)
= \mathrm{cou2}\cdot 2n + \mathrm{cou4}\cdot N_4$, and the diagonal closed
form uses $\hat r = m_H^2 + \mathrm{cou2}\cdot 2n + \mathrm{cou4}\cdot N_4$
--- IDENTICAL. The bracket therefore isolates exactly (off-diagonal
log-det shift) $+$ ($\sigma$-inhomogeneity remainder difference); the
diagonal enters once (continuum) and the basis diagonal is common to both
bracket members. DISMISSED.

\textbf{Residual systematics at the $10^{-5}$ scale (quantified).}
(i) Bracket basis-truncation: covered by the chain's own c12$\to$c20
convergence data ($<10^{-6}$ at the argmins; decelerating drift with
3--10$\times$ margins mid-region). (ii) \texttt{M\_fast} interpolation in
the continuum anchor: 480-point geomspace log-interp; auditor estimate of
the local interpolation error $O(10^{-6})$ in $M_t$, FIRST-ORDER PROTECTED
in $\Delta F$ by the $\partial\,\mathrm{rem}/\partial M_t = 0$ stationarity
at the reference (task 3.ii) and by reference cancellation (same table
feeds $M_R$); net effect estimated $\lesssim 10^{-6}$ ---
\emph{VALID-with-mitigation}: registered as a one-line scripted check
(replace \texttt{M\_fast} by direct quadrature at the LAM argmin and
difference; included in the pending Math434 script). (iii) \texttt{dI}
tail: the analytic $1/q^2$ tail term is included; the next-order residual
is $O(2q_0^2/q_{\max}^2)$ relative $\approx 4\times 10^{-9}$ at the LAM
argmin --- negligible (hand-verified: $(\hat r' - r_R)/(Cq_{\max})/(2\pi^2)
= 1.61\times10^{-3}/27.2/19.74 = 3.0\times10^{-6}$ is the included tail;
its own correction is three decades smaller). DISMISSED.

\textbf{(1b) The resummation-ratio calibration and the $\rho = 1$
``worst case'' label --- VALID-with-mitigation.} Auditor norm analysis
(full derivation in task 2): for off-diagonal $W$ with zero diagonal,
$X = D^{-1/2} W D^{-1/2}$, $\operatorname{Tr} X = 0$, $\|X\| < 1$,
\[
\operatorname{Tr}\ln(I{+}X) \;\ge\; \frac{1}{1-\|X\|}
\Big({-\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}X^2}\Big)
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \rho_{\rm exact} \le \frac{1}{1-\|X\|}.
\]
Hence $\rho = 1$ is a rigorous worst case ONLY where $\|X\| \ll 1$. At the
binding small-$A$ argmins this holds ($\|X\| \approx 3\times10^{-3}$ at the
LAM argmin, see task 2), so the chain's $\rho = 1$ bands ARE conservative
exactly where the minima live. At BCC mid-amplitude ($W/\hat r \sim 0.3$
per Math428), $(1-\|X\|)^{-1}$ can reach $\approx 1.4$, so the ``worst
case'' label there was an overstatement --- \emph{mitigation: the BCC
mid-amplitude region was subsequently computed at TRUE exact-Wick grade
(Math429/430), superseding the $\rho$-band question for BCC entirely; for
LAM/HEX mid-amplitude the label imprecision is absorbed by the G1$''$-3b
residual and by the refinement registered in \S 4 below.} The calibration
measurement itself ($\rho_{16} = 0.416$, $\rho_{20} = 0.414$, stability
asserted) is sound as an in-basis measurement; the chain's own v1.1
language (``estimator PASS, not a theorem'') correctly scopes it.

\subsection{Task 2: LAM weakest link / G1$''$-3b --- VALID-with-mitigation
(route (b) directional bound; argmin certified by hand; per-point
mid-amplitude verification delegated to the written-but-unexecuted script)}

\textbf{Setting.} LAM condensate $\phi_c = 2A\cos(q_0 z)$; 1D reciprocal
lattice $G_m = m q_0\hat z$; shell convolution counts $p_2(0)=2$,
$p_2(\pm2)=1$; $p_4(0)=6=N_4$, $p_4(\pm2)=4$, $p_4(\pm4)=1$ (auditor
re-enumeration). The Bloch matrix at $(k_\perp, k_z)$ is tridiagonal-like
on each parity chain with nearest coupling
$w = \mathrm{cou2}\,p_2(2) + \mathrm{cou4}\,p_4(2)$,
$\mathrm{cou2} = (3u+30vM)A^2$, $\mathrm{cou4} = 5vA^4$. At the Math431
argmin $(A, M) = (0.01, M_R)$:
\[
3u + 30vM_R = -2.58 + 10.635 = 8.055,\quad
w = 8.055\times10^{-4} + 6.5\times10^{-7} = 8.061\times10^{-4},
\]
\[
\hat r' = r_R + 2\,\mathrm{cou2} + 6\,\mathrm{cou4}
= 0.304526 + 0.001611 + 10^{-6} = 0.306138 .
\]

\textbf{Degenerate geometry.} The only doubly-on-shell coupled pair is
$p_z = \pm q_0$ at $k_\perp = 0$ (the Brazovskii shell-doubling resonance
on the odd-$m$ chain, coupled by the $2q_0$ condensate harmonic) ---
auditor derivation: on-shell + on-shell for a $\Delta p_z = 2q_0$ pair
forces the midpoint condition $k_\perp = 0$, $p_z = \mp q_0$.

\textbf{Norm bound (Gershgorin on $X = D^{-1/2}WD^{-1/2}$).} For an
on-shell row, the neighbours sit at $\hat r' + 16Cq_0^2(q_0 \pm p_z)^2$;
the row sum is maximised at the degenerate endpoint:
\[
\|X\| \le \frac{w}{\hat r'} + \frac{w}{\sqrt{\hat r'(\hat r' + 64Cq_0^4)}}
+ O(w_4)
= 2.633\times10^{-3} + 3.893\times10^{-4} + O(10^{-6})
\le 3.1\times10^{-3},
\]
using $64Cq_0^4 = 13.70$, $\sqrt{0.30614\times 14.006} = 2.071$.

\textbf{Log-det excess beyond second order.} With
$\ln(1+x) \ge x - \frac{x^2}{2(1-a)}$ for $|x|\le a<1$ and
$\operatorname{Tr}X = 0$,
\[
\big|\,\text{exact off-diag log-det} - \text{2nd order}\,\big|
\le \frac{\|X\|}{1-\|X\|}\,|\mathrm{off2}| \le 0.0031\,|\mathrm{off2}| .
\]
Bubble bound (Cauchy--Schwarz, exact): $B(Q) \le B(0) = -M'(\hat r')$;
shell-approximation $-M'(\hat r') \approx \frac{q_0}{8\pi\sqrt C}\,
\hat r'^{-3/2} = 0.160$; conservative $B(0) \le 0.2$. Then
\[
|\mathrm{off2}| \le \tfrac14\cdot 2w^2 B(0)
= \tfrac12 (8.061\times10^{-4})^2\times 0.2 = 6.5\times 10^{-8},
\]
so the log-det excess is $\le 2\times10^{-10}$, and even discarding the
estimator's own off2 and re-adding the full exact bracket can shift the
result downward by at most $6.6\times10^{-8}$.

\textbf{$\sigma$-inhomogeneity remainder (the piece the $\rho$-estimator
omits entirely --- the auditor's principal new finding).} The Math431
LAM/HEX estimator contains ONLY the log-det bubble; the exact-Wick bracket
also contains the remainder difference from $\sigma(z) = \bar\sigma
+ \delta\sigma(z)$, $\delta\sigma = 2\hat\sigma_2\cos 2q_0 z + \cdots$,
entering at the SAME order $O(A^4)$ as off2. Auditor bounds at the argmin:
$|\hat\sigma_2| \le w\,B(2q_0)/(1-\|X\|) \le 1.62\times10^{-4}$;
$\overline{\delta\sigma^2} \le 2\hat\sigma_2^2(1+\epsilon)
\le 5.3\times10^{-8}$; the mean-shift channel is FIRST-ORDER PROTECTED by
the task-3 stationarity ($\partial\,\mathrm{rem}/\partial\sigma_{\rm unif}
= 0$ at the reference up to $O(A^2, M_t{-}M_R)$ prefactors), contributing
$\lesssim 10^{-9}$; the $\delta\sigma$-quadratic block
$\big[\tfrac{3u}{4} + \tfrac{15v}{2}\bar\sigma\big]\overline{\delta\sigma^2}
+ \cdots$ has total magnitude $\le 2\times10^{-7}$ (dominant term
$\tfrac{15v}{2}\bar\sigma\,\overline{\delta\sigma^2} \approx 1.4\times
10^{-7}$, and it is POSITIVE; the only negative leading piece is
$\tfrac{3u}{4}\overline{\delta\sigma^2} \approx -3.4\times10^{-8}$);
cubic and $\phi_c^2$-weighted pieces $\le 10^{-9}$.

\textbf{Directional bound at the argmin (hand-verified arithmetic):}
\[
\boxed{\;\big|\Delta F^{\rm exact\,bracket}_{\rm LAM}
- \Delta F^{\rho=1}_{\rm est, LAM}\big|_{(0.01,\,M_R)}
\;\le\; 6.6\times10^{-8} + 2\times10^{-7} \;\lesssim\; 3\times10^{-7}
\;\ll\; 3.17\times10^{-5}. \;}
\]
The LAM chain minimum SURVIVES the exact-Wick treatment at the argmin with
two decades of headroom. Small-$A$ scaling: margin $\approx c_2 A^2$
($c_2 = n\,r_R$, independently re-derived below), corrections
$\le \kappa A^4 + O(A^6)$ with $\kappa \approx 17$ (auditor scaling), so
the headroom ratio is $\approx 56 A^2$: $0.0056$ at $A = 0.01$, still
$< 0.25$ for $A \lesssim 0.066$.

\textbf{What is NOT closed in this turn (honest scope).} For LAM/HEX
mid-amplitude points ($A \gtrsim 0.07$) the correction bound grows to the
same order as the quadratic margin scale, the per-point estimator values
were not persisted in the Math431 JSON (only minima), and the auditor had
no execution capability; the per-point certification
(estimator value $-$ correction bound $> 0$ at every scanned point) is
delegated to the WRITTEN script
\texttt{Codes/supplementary/Math434\_lam\_exact\_wick\_bracket.py}
(self-test asserts + JSON emission per 6.3.8; NOT YET EXECUTED; no
numerical output from it is cited anywhere in this note). \emph{Why this
does not break the candidate statement}: the statement is pinned at
ESTIMATOR grade --- the certified object at LAM/HEX is the $\rho = 1$
estimator, which IS positive at every probed point (Math431, 15/15
scripted) --- and the exact-Wick gap is exactly the pre-registered
G1$''$-3b residual that the statement's grade qualifier concedes. The
auditor's contribution is to CERTIFY exactness-adequacy at the binding
argmin (where the chain's headline minimum lives) and to sharpen
G1$''$-3b into a concrete per-point bound-verification spec.
\textbf{Verdict: VALID-with-mitigation} (mitigation = argmin directional
bound above + grade qualifier + sharpened G1$''$-3b spec + ready-to-run
script).

\textbf{Independent confirmation of the lattice-independent small-$A$
bound} (used as the margin floor): expanding the anchored estimator at
$A \to 0$, $M = M_R$, with $\tfrac12\,dI' = \tfrac12 M_R\,d\hat r$ and the
remainder's $M_t$-stationarity,
\[
c_2 = n\big[r + 3uM_R + 30vM_R^2 - 15vM_R^2\big] = n\,r_R
\qquad (\text{auditor re-derivation; matches Math428 v1.1 \S 3bis}),
\]
and the two-shell version $c_2^{(2)} = n_2[K_2 + 3uM_R + 15vM_R^2]
= n_2(r_R + Cq_0^4) = 1.5557$ (matches Math432).

\subsection{Task 4: SHG tilt bound (Math432 \S 5) ---
VALID-with-mitigation}

\textbf{Finding.} The Math432 estimate $A_2^* = O(|u| m_{31} A_1^3 /
2c_2^{(2)}) \lesssim 0.025$ describes only the CLASSICAL quartic-tilt
response and understates the actual displacement: auditor analysis of the
quartic cross-stiffness $\tfrac{3u}{2} m_{22} A_1^2 = -123.8\,A_1^2$ shows
it EXCEEDS $c_2^{(2)} = 1.5557$ for $A_1 \gtrsim 0.112$, i.e.\ at large
$A_1$ the bare quadratic restoring force in $A_2$ is overwhelmed and the
optimum is set by the sextic cross-moments, not by the quoted formula.
The Math432 JSON data confirm: at $A_1 = 0.14$, $M = M_R$, the scanned
$A_2$-profile is $0.1556\,(-0.12)$, $0.1201\,(-0.08)$, $0.1309\,(-0.05)$,
$0.1552\,(-0.03)$, $0.1831\,(-0.015)$, $0.2682\,(+0.015)$, rising further
for $A_2 > 0$: the per-row optimum sits near $A_2 \approx -0.065 \pm
0.015$, i.e.\ $|A_2^{\rm opt}| \approx 2.6\times$ the quoted $0.025$, on
the NEGATIVE branch (consistent with Math432's own tilt-sign observation
that the sextic/Wick-dressed moments override the classical quartic).
\textbf{However the load-bearing conclusion is unaffected}: at every
scanned $A_1$ row the $|A_2| = 0.12$ boundary values strictly exceed
interior values (auditor-checked at $A_1 = 0.12$ and $0.14$; e.g.\
$A_1{=}0.12$: $0.1066$ at $-0.12$ vs $0.0670$ at $-0.05$), so the scanned
box BRACKETS the per-row optimum --- the optimum does not exit the box
anywhere in the danger window, and all values are positive (0 negatives
in 244 + zoom points; auditor grep of the JSON: zero matches for negative
\texttt{dF\_anchored}). Beyond-box closure ($|A_2| > 0.12$, mixed-shell
sextic dominance) is correctly REGISTERED OPEN as G3$'$-b(i), not claimed.
\emph{Mitigation required}: Math432 \S 5's $A_2^*$ sentence should be
re-worded at its next versioned re-issue (v1.1) to ``the per-row optimum
is bracketed interior to the scanned box (empirically $|A_2^{\rm opt}|
\lesssim 0.08$, sextic-driven, negative branch); the classical-tilt
formula $O(|u|m_{31}A_1^3/2c_2^{(2)})$ applies only at small $A_1$''.
This is a wording defect, not a result defect. \textbf{Verdict:
VALID-with-mitigation.}

\subsection{Devil's-advocate self-test on THIS AUDIT (CLAUDE.md \S 6.3.1
+ 6.3.5(a))}

\textbf{Objection $\alpha$ (the auditor's Gershgorin norm could miss a
non-row-localised soft direction of $X$).} Gershgorin bounds the spectral
radius by the max row sum; for the LAM chain this is tight near the
degenerate $2\times2$ block, but could long-range products of
moderately-sized entries produce $\|X\|$ above the row bound?
\emph{DISMISSED with counter}: for symmetric $X$,
$\|X\| \le \max_m \sum_{m'} |X_{mm'}|$ is unconditional
(Gershgorin/Schur); no structure assumption is used. The bound was
evaluated at the global supremum over $(k_\perp, k_z)$ including the
degenerate point; off-shell rows have strictly smaller sums entrywise.

\textbf{Objection $\beta$ (the $\sigma$-remainder bound used the
first-order $\hat\sigma_2 = w B(2q_0)$ with an $(1-\|X\|)^{-1}$ dressing
--- is the dressing argument airtight?).} \emph{VALID-with-mitigation}:
the dressing factor was applied as a Neumann-series envelope on
$K^{-1} - D^{-1}$; a fully rigorous statement needs the same
$D^{-1/2}\cdot D^{-1/2}$ sandwich applied to the off-diagonal element
integrals, which introduces at worst an additional $O(1)$ geometric
factor on a quantity that is $10^{2}$ below the margin. Mitigation: the
written script computes $\hat\sigma_2$ EXACTLY (matrix inversion per
$(k_\perp, k_z)$), removing the envelope from the final certification;
the hand bound's two-decade headroom absorbs any $O(1)$ slack.

\textbf{Objection $\gamma$ (auditing the estimator at its own argmin is
circular --- the EXACT functional's minimum could sit elsewhere).}
\emph{VALID-with-mitigation}: correct in principle; the auditor's
small-$A$ scaling (headroom ratio $56A^2$) certifies a NEIGHBOURHOOD of
the argmin ($A \lesssim 0.066$ at the $25\%$-headroom level), not a
point; outside it the estimator values rise (they exceed the recorded
minimum by definition) while the correction bound grows as $A^4$ ---
the script's per-point check (estimator $-$ bound $> 0$ everywhere)
is precisely the closure of this objection, and until it runs the gap is
honestly carried inside G1$''$-3b. The candidate statement's estimator
grade is unaffected either way.

\textbf{Objection $\delta$ (no-execution session: every number in this
note is hand arithmetic).} \emph{VALID-with-documentation}: all hand
arithmetic is elementary (products, square roots, one-line integrals with
quoted approximations) and reproduced step-by-step above so any reader
can re-verify in minutes; the 6.3.8 script with asserts covering each
inequality is on disk awaiting execution; NO claim in this note depends
on an unexecuted script's output.

\subsection{Quantitative sanity checks (CLAUDE.md \S 6.3.4)}

(i) \emph{Magnitude/limit-case}: the auditor's independent $c_2 = n\,r_R$
re-derivation gives LAM $c_2 A^2 = 0.304526\times10^{-4}
= 3.045\times10^{-5}$ at $A = 0.01$ vs the Math431 JSON minimum
$3.1696\times10^{-5}$ --- ratio $1.041$, consistent with positive
$O(A^4)$ corrections; an exact match would have been suspicious.
(ii) \emph{Dimensional/convention regression}: $K_2 = \mu_2 + Cq_0^4
= 0.005 + 0.214036 = 0.219036$ from the auditor's own $q_0^4$
($q_0^2 = 0.462638$, $q_0^4 = 0.214034$; rounding-consistent with the
chain's $0.219034$); reproduces Math426 $K(0)$.
(iii) \emph{Sign-direction physics}: the off-diagonal second-order term
is negative-definite ($-\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}X^2$), i.e.\ off-diagonal
coupling HELPS the condensate --- the attack direction is correctly
oriented in the chain scripts and in this audit's bounds.
(iv) \emph{Exponential/series well-definedness}: $\|X\| \le 3.1\times
10^{-3} < 1$ at the argmin, so every Neumann/log series used converges
absolutely; the bound $(1-\|X\|)^{-1} \le 1.0031$ is finite and near 1.
